**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 7, verses 1–2**

[p. 347]

**Surat al-A'raf (The Heights)**

Its purpose is to warn those who turn away from what the Book called for in the preceding surah: monotheism (tawhid), unity in goodness, and fulfilment of what was established as obligatory by the proof in al-An'am. It also warns against the calamities of the two abodes. This is better than what had appeared to me and what I mentioned at ﴿And the weighing on that day is the truth﴾ [al-A'raf: 8]. The clearest indication of this purpose in it is the matter of al-A'raf (the Heights), for belief in it includes overlooking Paradise and Hell, standing on the reality of what is in them, and of what is prepared for their people. It calls to performing every good, avoiding every evil, and taking admonition from everything that softens the heart.

﴿In the name of Allah﴾, the One who is clothed in the garment of pride and the wrapper of greatness and majesty. ﴿The Most Merciful﴾, whose mercy includes His vengeance upon the people of disbelief and error. ﴿The Most Compassionate﴾, who guides the people of chosen status to adhere to the path of fidelity. ﴿Alif. Lam. Mim. Sad.﴾

When He, glorified is He, mentioned at the end of the previous surah that He sent down to them a blessed Book, commanded that it be followed, gave the reason for its sending down, and mentioned what necessarily follows from that, which is indispensable in the method of eloquence and the arena of excellence, it was among its contents that He commanded those addressed by it to turn to Him alone. If He willed, He would guide them, and if He willed, He would lead them astray. He continued with what is indispensable in completing this, until He concluded the surah with what is connected to its opening. Its embrace of that became so firm (p. 348) that the two became like one thing. He began to argue for what He had concluded that surah with, namely the swiftness of punishment and the universality of righteousness and reward, and for what preceded it. So He said, informing about a subject whose predicate is implied: [it is] ﴿a Book﴾, meaning a great one that made the straight path clear, leaving no ambiguity in it, and leaving no good without commanding it, nor any evil without forbidding it. Its sending down is therefore from His great mercy. Then He described it with what confirms what He had indicated of His mercy, by saying: ﴿sent down to you﴾, meaning: and you are the most noble of people in soul, the most expansive of them in breast, the most beautiful of them in heart, the most rooted in lineage, and the most knowing of how to win over the distant and attract the hostile and hateful. This is something He has specifically granted you, and He has raised you above all creation by degrees without number and ranks without limit that could be exhausted.

Since the purpose of the mission was first of all warning, to turn people back from the error they were upon, and since confronting people with warning is very hard on souls, and undertaking it is extremely difficult, He placed before His words, as a consequence of singling you out with this mercy: ﴿So let there not be﴾ [and He expressed the heart by its dwelling, which is wider than it, for emphasis in the matter, and so He said]: ﴿in your breast any constriction﴾, meaning some measure of distress regarding them, or fear, or the like, ﴿concerning it﴾, referring to what is connected to (sent down) in His words: (p. 349) ﴿that you may warn by it﴾, meaning: a warning to everyone it reaches, or to the opponents, of the swiftness of punishment in the manner in which He, glorified is He, afflicted the past generations and earlier nations, as indicated by the end of al-An'am. He will also narrate from their reports in this surah. ﴿And a reminder﴾, meaning a great one, ﴿for the believers﴾, meaning with glad tidings, admonitions, forgiveness, and mercy, as indicated by the close of al-An'am. The omission of the object indicates the universality of the message for everyone among the rational beings whom it is possible to warn and remind. It is also permissible for the lam of (that you may warn) to be connected to the meaning of a prohibition, i.e. remove the constriction for such-and-such, for whoever is of expanded breast proceeds with what he intends, whereas whoever is constricted is hindered. That is, let the constriction not occur on account of your warning by it. The prohibition addressed to the Prophet ﷺ was transferred to the constriction, as emphasis and courtesy. It is also permissible that the estimate be: ﴿that you may warn by it and remind by it﴾, for it is a warning to the disbelievers and a reminder to the believers. The verse, under every reading, belongs to al-ihtibak (the rhetorical device of mutual omission): its mention of (that you may warn) first indicates the omission of (that you may remind) second, and the mention of the believers second indicates the omission of the opponents first. For souls are of two kinds: dull souls, ignorant, far from the world of the unseen, drowned in seeking bodily pleasures and animal appetites, for whom the sending of the messengers is a warning and a frightening. And noble souls, illuminated by divine lights, for whom the sending of the messengers is a reminder. For these souls, by the requirement of their original essences and their created natures, are prepared to be drawn toward the world of holiness, except that sometimes the veils of the world of bodies cover them, and a kind of stupor and heedlessness befalls them. When they hear the call of the prophets and are joined with it, and the lights of the spirits of the messengers of Allah connect to them, they remember their origin and see their source, and they yearn for what is there of rest and fragrance, and they fly toward them with every flight. Thus those lights become pure in them.

Abu Hayyan said: The linkage of this surah with what precedes it is that when He, exalted is He, mentioned His words: ﴿And this is a Book We sent down, blessed, so follow it﴾ [al-An'am: 155], and digressed from it to what follows it, up to His words at the end of the surah: ﴿And He is the One who made you successors upon the earth﴾ [al-An'am: 165], and mentioned their being tested in what He gave them, which can only be through the legal obligations (taklif), He mentioned that by which the obligations are established, which is the divine Book, and mentioned the command to follow it, as He commanded in His words: ﴿And this is a Book We sent down, blessed, so follow it﴾ [al-An'am: 155]. End of quotation.

And his teacher, the Imam Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: When Allah, exalted is He, said, beginning with consideration: ﴿Did they not see how many generations We destroyed before them, whom We had established on the earth in ways We have not established for you, and We sent the sky down upon them in abundant rain, and made the rivers flow beneath them, then We destroyed them for their sins and produced after them another generation﴾ [al-An'am: 6]. Then He said: ﴿And messengers were mocked before you, so what they used to mock befell those who scoffed at them﴾ [al-An'am: 10]. [Then He said]: ﴿Say: Travel through the earth, then see what was the end of the deniers﴾ [al-An'am: 11]. Then He said (p. 351): ﴿And messengers were denied before you, but they were patient over what they were denied﴾ [al-An'am: 34]. And He said: ﴿And We certainly sent to nations before you, then We seized them with misfortune and adversity﴾ [al-An'am: 42]. And He said: ﴿O assembly of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you, relating to you My verses?﴾ [al-An'am: 130]. Thus in these verses there occurred a referral to consideration of the earlier nations and what they did when they denied their prophets, and the destruction of those generations because of their denial and their insolence, and a consolation to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by the course of what befell the messengers before him: ﴿We know that what they say grieves you﴾ [al-An'am: 33]. So the referral and consolation required an unfolding of the reports of the earlier nations and the past generations, and an informing about the patience of the messengers, peace be upon them, and their gentleness in calling their peoples. In the four surahs before al-An'am there does not occur any referral and consolation like this, though it recurs in al-An'am, as became clear after finishing what was intended: the explanation of the path of the God-fearing in taking and in leaving, and the state of those who deviated from their ways, among those who aspired to them or aimed at them, and were not granted success and were not allowed to fulfil their hope, from the two groups: those who rely on transmitted report (al-sam') and those who rely on reasoning (al-nazar). The first deviated through the intrusion of alteration and substitution, and the others swerved through misuse and the weakness of understandings, and through the cause of the deviation of both groups, which is an ancient prior decree. When the matter of these people ended, and the address turned to consoling him, peace be upon him, and strengthening his heart (p. 352) by mentioning the states of the prophets with their peoples and commanding creation to take lessons from the earlier nations, and when this had been introduced to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at the mention of the prophets:

﴿Those are the ones Allah guided, so follow their guidance﴾ [al-An'am: 90], He, exalted is He, unfolded the state of those referred to, and fully narrated much of their stories, through the end of Surat Hud, to His words, glorified is He: ﴿And We relate to you from the reports of the messengers what We strengthen your heart with﴾ [Hud: 120]. So reflect on how the surah whose purpose is the stories of the nations opens, and how it closes, and it will become clear to you what I have pointed to, and Allah knows best His intent. And reflect on the opening of Surat al-A'raf with His words: ﴿Then We will surely relate to them with knowledge, and We were not absent﴾ [al-A'raf: 7], and the conclusion of the stories in it with His words: ﴿So relate the stories, perhaps they will reflect﴾ [al-A'raf: 176], after following the story of the Children of Israel with the story of Balaam: ﴿And recite to them the report of the one to whom We gave Our signs﴾ [al-A'raf: 175]. Then He said: ﴿That is the example of the people who denied Our signs﴾ [al-A'raf: 176]. So reflect on this allusion after the mention of the stories, and how He attached those among the Arabs and others who denied the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to those of the deniers whose mention He recounted. And reflect on how the mention of the wretched opens with the story of Iblis and closes with the story of Balaam, both of whom disbelieved with knowledge, and in that is the greatest admonition. Allah, exalted is He, said after that: ﴿Whomever Allah guides, he is the guided﴾ [al-A'raf: 178]. Thus He began the response to His Prophet ﷺ by mentioning what He bestowed upon him and upon those who responded to him, and so He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Alif. Lam. Mim. Sad.﴾ ﴿A Book sent down to you﴾ (p. 353). He thereby pointed to His favour by sending down the Book which He made a guidance for the God-fearing, and here He points to what it carries of consolation and expansion of breasts through what has passed of wonders and stories, together with its being guidance and light. So He said: ﴿So let there not be in your breast any constriction from it﴾, meaning: it has included, from what We have made you descend upon, what removes constriction and consoles souls, ﴿that you may warn by it, as the messengers before you warned, from whose reports We relate to you﴾, and that you may follow their examples in your warning, your calling, and your patience, and that the believers may be reminded. Then He commanded His servants to follow what He sent down, saying: ﴿Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord﴾ [al-A'raf: 3]. For the destruction of those nations whose reports We relate to you was only because they did not follow, and inclined toward their allies from the devils of jinn and mankind. Then He followed this with the story of Adam, peace be upon him, to make clear to His servants the custom He has followed concerning them regarding the domination and scheming of the devils, and that the devil is an enemy to them: ﴿O children of Adam, do not let Satan tempt you as he removed your parents from Paradise﴾ [al-A'raf: 27]. In the story of Adam here there occurred what did not occur in the story in al-Baqarah, of the expansion of what was summarized there, such as the accursed one's open declaration of envy, his imagining his own superiority by being created from fire, his request for respite, his domination over the offspring of Adam, the permission granted to him for that, his threat and the threat against his followers, then his proceeding to whisper to Adam, peace be upon him, and his oath to him: ﴿And he swore to them both, "Indeed I am to you both among the sincere advisers"﴾ [al-A'raf: 21]. All of this was summarized in Surat al-Baqarah, and no story recurs except that this is its nature, I mean: it yields, however often it recurs, what had not been obtained from it at first. Then the verses extended (p. 354) to the beginning of the story of Noah, peace be upon him, and the stories continued to the stories of the Children of Israel. So here He unfolded from their states and reports something resembling what He unfolded in the story of Adam and what occurred in the trial of Iblis, and here He detailed much and mentioned what was not mentioned in al-Baqarah, so that it does not truly recur, nor is it limited to the stories of a particular group only. Among the marvels of wisdom is that what occurs in the two surahs of both stories is self-sufficient and healing, and when some of that is joined to some of it, its summariness is lifted and its completeness becomes clear. Blessed is He whose speech this is, and who made it a decisive proof and a dazzling sign.

When, exalted is He, following their stories in al-Baqarah, He commanded His Prophet and the believers to pardon and overlook, saying: ﴿So pardon and overlook﴾ [al-Baqarah: 109], He, exalted is He, also followed here by saying to His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: ﴿Take what is easy, enjoin what is good, and turn away from the ignorant﴾ [al-A'raf: 199]. We have strayed from the intended purpose, so let us return to it. End of quotation.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 3:

When He, glory be to Him, had given direction to him (ﷺ) concerning the matter of warning and reminding through the Book, He gave direction to his followers, commanding them to follow it and forbidding them to follow the people of misguidance and the ornate falsehoods that their allies inspire in them. This came after He had informed them that the Book is a reminder, that it is a cause for the elevation of their station and the might of their authority. So He said, turning toward them and addressing them with the majesty of His sublime glory (p-355) ﴿Follow﴾, that is: burden yourselves with a great burden, with earnestness and vigour, in following ﴿what has been sent down to you﴾, that is: you have been singled out with it apart from others, so be grateful for this blessing ﴿from your Lord﴾, that is: the One who has never ceased to be good to you. ﴿And do not follow﴾. Perhaps He expressed it with the reflexive form (ittaba'a) as a hint that what happens short of deliberate effort, but rather as a slip and a kind of heedlessness, falls within the realm of pardon ﴿other than Him﴾, that is: other than your Lord ﴿allies﴾, that is: from those whom We forbade you in al-An'am, and We explained their harm to you, from the devils of mankind and jinn, and their inability to avail you, and that the entire affair belongs to your Lord.

Since they had opposed clear reason and sound nature in following them, while the examples of this were before them had they remembered, He said, alerting them to remember what they know of their own conduct: ﴿little﴾, and He emphasized the paucity with (ma), the negating particle, and with the assimilation of the tā' of the tafa''ul form, saying: ﴿what you remember﴾, that is: you exert yourselves to remember what is fixed in your original nature. For you acknowledge that your Lord is the Lord of everything, so everyone you invoke besides Him is a creature under His lordship. You do not find in your intellects, your natures, or your usages anything that indicates in any way that a creature could be a partner to its Lord.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 4:

Since among the most important things to be reminded of are the blessings that bring joy and the punishments that bring harm, so that one turns toward God, turns away from everything other than Him, and does not become deceived by the means of security and ease, He says: ﴿And how many﴾, meaning: how little you remember and fear Our punishments, while the reality is that ﴿how many a town﴾ (p. 356), however great, ﴿We have destroyed﴾. Since the intended meaning is an emphasis on destruction, He attributed it to the town, while what is meant are its people, and said: ﴿We have destroyed﴾, meaning: by what We possess of greatness, because of its wrongdoing in following others besides God. So do not be deceived by your protectors besides Him, while you know that they did not benefit those of the earlier nations who went astray at the time when We sent Our might upon them, brought Our vengeance down on them, and they were certainly destroyed then. Moreover, they were stronger in force, greater in number, and more firm in their plotting, yet their (the protectors') failure to avail them became clear, so they did not direct their hopes toward them.

Since the meaning is: We intended to destroy it and decreed that, He made the following statement a consequence of it: ﴿so Our might came upon them﴾, meaning: Our punishment, by what We possess of power and greatness. Or the destruction is in its literal sense, and this is a detailing and explanation of it. Since there is no difference in the coming of His punishment, glorified is He, between it occurring by night or by day, and since the most grievous and severe might is that which comes at a time of rest, ease, and heedlessness, He said: ﴿at night﴾, meaning: at the time of being sheltered in houses by night, as He destroyed the people of Lot, peace be upon him, at the time of the pre-dawn.

Since the intended meaning of "town" is its people, He made this explicit with His words [because when the modified noun (muḍāf) is omitted, two considerations are permissible regarding it according to what the meaning allows: that one does not look to it, as in the beginning of the verse, and that one does look to it, as in this last part, to show that the people are the ones directly intended, because this is the place of threat]: ﴿or they were resting at noon﴾, meaning (p. 357): sleeping at the time of midday rest, or resting without sleep, as He destroyed the people of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him. That is to say: they were heedless in each of the two times because they were secure; they did not think that any of their deeds necessitated punishment, nor were they expecting anything of it. So the implied sense is: "at night, while they were in it sleeping," or "at noon, while they were in it resting," that is, sleeping. Thus the verse is an example of *ihtibāk* (a rhetorical device in which one term is mentioned and its counterpart omitted, and vice versa): the mention of "at night" first indicates the omission of "at noon" second, and the mention of "they were resting" second indicates the omission of "they were sleeping" first. What guided us to this good meaning is the placement of "they" without a conjunction "wa," and this is close to His statement, exalted is He, in what follows: ﴿Do the people of the towns feel secure that Our might will not come upon them at night while they are sleeping?﴾ [al-A'raf: 97]. So the more likely reading is that what is omitted first is "sleeping," and second is "by day," so the implied sense is: "at night, in which they are sleeping, or by day, in which they are resting." He made clear the greatness of what came upon them and its terror by stating that at each of the two times none of them had any thought of turning to resist it, which led to His following statement:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 5:

﴿So their plea was not but that they said, when Our punishment came upon them⁠—﴾ that is, their statement which they sought to utter, ﴿when Our might came upon them⁠—﴾ that is, by what We possess of greatness, ﴿except that they said⁠﴾ that is, nothing but their statement, ﴿"Indeed, we were⁠﴾ that is, by what is in our nature, ﴿wrongdoers"﴾ that is, in that we did not follow what was sent down to us from our Lord. So that did not benefit them at all, except for the intensification of regret;

Then, after the matter of the Messenger and the nations mentioned earlier, he (the author) gave as a cause for it His saying, to repel the delusion of one who thinks that the matter ended with what they were punished with in this world: ﴿So We will surely question﴾, that is, by what We possess of greatness, in the manner of reproach and rebuke for the disobedient, and of honouring and exalting for the obedient. He made the place of the pronoun apparent for generality, so He said: ﴿those﴾

Since the blame was for denying the Messenger, not restricted to the condition of his being specific, He used the passive form in His saying: ﴿to whom We sent [messengers]﴾, that is, to them, namely the nations, whether they carried out Our commands and held back at Our prohibitions as the messengers had ordered them or not. ﴿And We will surely question﴾, that is, by Our greatness, ﴿the messengers﴾, that is, whether there was any constriction in their breasts regarding what We had sent them with, and whether they conveyed it or not. ﴿On the Day when you will be witnesses over the people﴾ by what you knew of My testimony in this Qur'an. ﴿And the Messenger will be a witness over you﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 143]. For We will surely have to revive you after death, then question you on a day when hidden things will be made manifest and hearts will be exposed, however deeply their concealment is intense, and We will surely show the deeds and the words, and We will leave out none of the conditions.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 7:

When questioning conveys to the questioner that the one being questioned is concealed from him, He removes this misconception by saying, indicating that He is more knowledgeable than those questioned about what He asks them about: ﴿So We will surely relate to them﴾, that is, by virtue of Our attributes of greatness, which necessarily entail every perfection, ﴿to them﴾, that is, to those questioned from among the messengers and their nations, all their conditions and what they deserve of their recompense ﴿with knowledge﴾, that is, with knowledge that is certain, not conjectural, for We were with them in all their changing circumstances ﴿And We were not﴾, that is, at no time whatsoever, as the requirement of Our greatness demands, ﴿absent﴾, that is, absent in any way, nor from anyone among the creation (p-359), but rather Our knowledge encompasses all universals and particulars, because that is what the requirement of greatness, of Our attributes of perfection, demands. [And whoever does not have comprehensive knowledge, such that he can distinguish the obedient from the disobedient, is not fit to be a god.]

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 8:

When the allusion had already been made by His saying, ﴿And give full measure and weight with justice﴾ (6:152), to the effect that true equality in weighing is beyond human capacity and that it is the furthest of measures from equality, and the text of His saying, ﴿And whoever comes with an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its like﴾ (6:160), points to the power of the All-Powerful to do so, and He concluded the previous verse with the comprehensive knowledge in the most eloquent form, which requires this in the highest manner, He also emphasized the matter and restricted it to His knowledge here, saying: ﴿And the weighing﴾, by a real balance for the records of deeds, or for the deeds themselves after they are given forms corresponding to what they deserve, or otherwise, after God casts knowledge of it into the hearts. Perhaps it is a circumstantial clause (hal) of the "We" of majesty in the verse before it, meaning: We do not suffice with what We relate, but We weigh it, so that it becomes such that it appears to everyone that it is in the utmost degree of equality. Abu Hayyan and Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Nahwi al-Isfahani said in his grammatical analysis (i'rab): al-wazn (الوَزْنُ) is the subject (mubtada'), yawma'idhin (﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾) is an adverbial of time (zarf) in the accusative governed by it, and al-haqq (﴿الحَقُّ﴾) is the predicate (khabar) of the subject. Al-Isfahani added, saying: The governing of the verbal noun (masdar) when it has the definite article (lam al-ta'rif) is considered weak, and we have mentioned that it has come in revelation: ﴿God does not like the public mention of evil speech except by one who has been wronged﴾ (4:148). End of quote. That is, the weighing on that Day is restricted to the truth, corresponding to reality (p-٣٦٠) with a real correspondence in which there is no excess at all, and the weighing on that Day does not exceed the truth into any falsehood by the addition or subtraction of an atom or anything less than that. Thus it becomes clear that the purpose of the surah is to urge following the Book, and this includes urging following the Messenger and indicating the Oneness of God and the power to resurrect, through showing the awesome acts in the beginning of creation and the destruction of earlier peoples, pointing out that whoever does not follow him and does not affirm the Oneness of Him who sent it in this style that cannot be matched, and in this method before which intellects and natures stand helpless, because of the proofs established for His Oneness through the inability of anyone else to produce its like in speech and deeds, is about to be hastened, before the Day of Resurrection, with a punishment like that of the past nations and the bygone generations, in addition to what is stored up for him on that Day of evil return and the manifestation of the effect of wrath.

When He had informed us that the reckoning by the balance is in a manner that shows there is no injustice in it in any way, there followed from it His saying: ﴿Then whoever's scales are heavy﴾, that is, pressed down and sinking, as is customary in this world, ﴿his scales﴾, that is, the things weighed of his deeds, [that is, his deeds] that are weighed. Perhaps He expressed the deeds by it, as an indication that every deed is weighed separately so that one strives to improve it. ﴿Those﴾, that is, the high-minded ones, ﴿they are﴾ [that is, exclusively] ﴿the successful﴾, that is, those who prevail in attaining all their aims.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 9:

﴿And whoever's scales are light﴾, i.e., those who are lightened [in the balance], ﴿meaning the scales in which deeds are weighed, the righteous deeds﴾, ﴿those are the ones who will be removed far away﴾, ﴿who have lost their souls﴾, i.e., which are their capital, so how much more so what is less than it, ﴿for having wronged Our signs﴾, i.e., despite the greatness that they possess, ﴿they used to wrong﴾ (p-361) i.e., by the continuous act of renewing their placing of them (the signs) in other than the place fitting for them, which is the act of one who is in darkness. Al-Hasan said: "It is only right that a scale into which good deeds are placed should become heavy, and it is only right that a scale into which evil deeds are placed should become light."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 10:

When He had commanded creation to follow the messengers and warned them against opposing them, and had emphasized the warning with the punishment of this world and then the punishment of the Hereafter, He turned to reminding them, encouraging them to this by bestowing His blessings and warning them against their removal; for direct address is more effective in restraining the one addressed. So He said, in a position of circumstance (ḥāl) relative to ﴿they have lost their souls﴾ [al-A'raf: 9], ﴿And We have certainly established you﴾, meaning: they lost them while the situation was that We had established you to save them, by creating for you faculties and capacities and by pouring forth blessings, and by making for you a place where establishment occurs, ﴿in the earth﴾, meaning all of it, there is not a patch of it except that it is suitable for your benefit from it, even if only through reflection. ﴿And We have made for you﴾, meaning, by virtue of the greatness that is Ours, ﴿therein means of livelihood (ma'āyish)﴾, meaning: the plural of ma'īsha, which are things by which life (ʿaysh) is obtained, and ʿaysh is the conduct of the days of life in what benefits. The yā' is original (aṣlīyya), therefore it is not hamzated; [and likewise whatever has after the alif of its plural a root weak letter, and before its alif there is no wāw as in awā'il, nor a yā' as in khayā'ir, the plurals of awwal and khayr, for it is not hamzated except irregularly, as in manā'ir and maṣā'ib, the plurals of manāra and muṣība].

Since the sum of what has passed is that He, glory be to Him, brought them into being, strengthened them, and created for them [that which] sustains their strength, so they ate of His provision and worshipped other than Him, He produced His saying, by way of emphasis: ﴿Little is it that you give thanks﴾, meaning: for One who has poured His blessings upon you, outward (ẓāhira) and inward (bāṭina), by which you are saved (tanjūna) with your souls. (p-362) Abū Ḥayyān said: it refers back to those who were addressed with ﴿Follow what has been sent down to you﴾ [al-A'raf: 3], and what lies between them is brought as an occasion for reflection and admonition, by mentioning what their affair came to in this world and what it will come to in the Hereafter. End of quotation.

When He, glory be to Him, had mentioned the empowerment (*al-tamkin*) He had granted them, He reminded them of their state before this capacity, namely non-existence (*al-'adam*), as a reminder of blessings. This was within a context that points to the resurrection (*al-ba'th*), whose establishment He had just completed, and to what He had specially bestowed upon their father Adam (peace be upon him) of empowerment in the Garden: creation, shaping, breathing into him the spirit of life and the spirit of knowledge, commanding the inhabitants of His heavens to prostrate to him, and His anger toward whoever opposed him. He expelled that opponent from the place of His honour and the source of His happiness, and settled Adam in that exalted abode and lofty dwelling, permitted to enjoy everything in it except one tree. When Adam disobeyed the command, He removed him from it and cast him out of it. In this there is a warning to those who have been empowered against losing the favour through the withdrawal of blessings and the descent of punishment. So He said: ﴿And We created you﴾, that is, by what We possess of the attributes of greatness; ﴿then We shaped you﴾, that is, We decreed your creation and then your shaping, by making in you a capacity close to that, by specifying each part of the matter with its determined measure, by kneading the clay of Adam (peace be upon him) into a state that accepts this, just as the earth is prepared by being kneaded through the sending down of rain so that a tree may come from it. That tree may be prepared to receive the form of fruit, or it may not be, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We did certainly create man from an extract of clay﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 12] ﴿Then We placed him as a sperm-drop in a firm lodging﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 13] ﴿Then We made the sperm-drop into a clinging clot, then We made the clot into a lump of flesh, then We made the lump into bones, then We clothed the bones with flesh; then We produced him as another creation﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 14].

The Prophet (ﷺ) said, as in the Sahih (of al-Bukhari), on the authority of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him): "Indeed, one of you is gathered in his mother's belly as a drop for forty days, then he becomes a clot for a similar period, then a lump of flesh for a similar period; then Allah sends an angel who breathes the spirit into him." And also from him (may Allah be pleased with him), in Muslim's collection, he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "When the sperm-drop has passed forty-two nights, Allah sends an angel to it who shapes it and creates its hearing, its sight, its skin, its flesh and its bones. Then he says: 'O Lord! Male or female?' And your Lord decrees what He wills, and the angel writes..." The hadith.

The apparent meaning of this hadith contradicts the wording before it and the verse. Therefore it is interpreted to mean that the meaning of "shaped her" (*sawwarahā*) is: he prepared her during the second forty-day period for receiving the form, with a preparation close to actual making, and he facilitated the first period by kneading in a specific manner, unlike what came before, for she was a sperm-drop and thus far from being able to receive the form. For this reason the scholars differed regarding her sanctity, whether it is permitted to destroy her and to cause her expulsion. The meaning of "created" (*khalaqa*) is "decreed," that is, He made for each of these things a limit it does not exceed, in general terms. The proof that this is a figurative usage (*majaz*) is his doubt about whether she is male or female. Had it been on its literal sense, there would be no doubt about whether she is male or female, since the organs of male and female are part of the form. By this the verse coheres with His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When your Lord said to the angels: Indeed I am creating a human from clay﴾ [Sad: 71] ﴿So when I have proportioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, then fall down to him in prostration﴾ [Sad: 72]. That is actual creation, whereas what is in this surah is the depositing in him of the capacity that brings him close to it. The purpose of the verse is to remind them of blessings, to appeal to them toward harmony, and to depict the state of opposition as monstrous. That is: they have lost themselves, while We had bestowed upon them the blessing of empowerment after We had brought them into being in the form mentioned, after they had been non-existent, and after We had made the angels prostrate to their father and expelled the one who was arrogant toward him with an expulsion unlike any other, and removed him from the place of Our holiness with a distance that admits no nearness. We settled their father in the Garden, the abode of Our mercy and Our nearness. Then He, exalted is He, expressing this, said: ﴿Then We said﴾, that is, by what We possess of exclusive greatness, ﴿to the angels﴾, that is, those present at that time among the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth, all of them, as indicated by the definite article (*al*), whether we say it is for comprehensiveness (*al-istighraq*) or for the genus (*al-jins*): ﴿Prostrate to Adam﴾, that is, after he had become a man, standing upright and complete, possessed of a soul, as is known from the name (given to him). Then He attached to this command the statement: ﴿So they prostrated﴾, that is, all of them, as indicated by the exception in His saying: ﴿except Iblis﴾. Since the meaning of this exception, to exclude him from those who prostrated, is that he did not prostrate, He stated it explicitly, saying: ﴿He was not among those who prostrated﴾, that is, to Adam.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 12:

Since the one who opposed the king was in the place of punishment, the listener yearned to hear his report, so it was answered with His saying: ﴿He said﴾, meaning: to Iblis, in denunciation of him, rebuke to him, and drawing out his disbelief, which he had been concealing, through what he displayed in his answer, so that creation would know the cause of his expulsion: ﴿What prevented you﴾. Since this expression had already made clear his non-prostration, and so that the meaning would not be confused by inserting (lā) in His saying ﴿that you do not prostrate﴾, He brought it to convey emphasis through the indication of blame for refraining from the act and for proceeding to abandon it. It is as if it were said: "What prevented you from prostrating and what moved you to abandon it?" ﴿When﴾, meaning: at the time ﴿I commanded you﴾, meaning: when the time arrived in which the commanded act was to be performed. ﴿He said﴾, meaning: Iblis, attributing to his Lord, glorified is He, injustice or lack of knowledge of the truth: ﴿I am better than him﴾, meaning: it does not befit me to prostrate to one who is beneath me, nor to be commanded to that, because that contradicts wisdom. Then he explained the aspect of superiority that he imagined, through his poor understanding or through what his bad nature led him to, with his saying: ﴿You created me from fire﴾, meaning: for it is the predominant element of my parts, and it is elevated, shining, high, and dominant; ﴿and You created him from clay﴾, meaning: it is the predominant element of his parts, and it is dense, dark, low, and dominated. He erred in a gross error, for bringing into existence is better than annihilation without dispute, and fire is the cause of annihilation and destruction of what it mixes with, while clay is the cause of growth and nurture of what it mixes with. This would hold if the matter of excellence were considered in terms of elements and origins, but it is not so; rather it is considered in terms of ends.

When this matter was clear, and mere arrogance toward Allah is disbelief in any form, He turned away from his reply without the expulsion (*ṭard*), the meaning of which is his descent to a station other than the one he sought to ascend to. He therefore resumed with His saying ﴿He said﴾, making His words ﴿Then go down from it﴾ a consequence of his refusal, and left the abode in which he was implicit, which was (p-٣٦٦) Paradise, for it does not admit a disobedient one. He expressed it with *al-hubūṭ* (descent), which necessarily entails the loss of station, rather than *al-khurūj* (departure), because the purpose of this surah is warning (*al-indhār*), and descent is more indicative of it. And as a consequence of His command to descend, which means alighting, going down, decline, diminution, and falling into some part of it, is His saying ﴿It is not for you to be arrogant therein﴾, meaning: it is not valid or permissible in any respect for you to deliberately assume pride (*al-kibr*), which is elevation in nobility and greatness and tyrannical self-exaltation. There is no restrictive implication in His saying ﴿for you﴾ or His saying ﴿therein﴾, since there are explicit prohibitions of arrogance absolutely: ﴿Indeed, He does not love the arrogant﴾ [al-Naḥl: 23]; ﴿Thus does Allah seal every heart of an arrogant tyrant﴾ [Ghāfir: 35]; ﴿Those who were arrogant said, "Indeed, we are all therein"﴾ [Ghāfir: 48]. It was restricted only to magnify the matter, as if it were said: arrogance is not befitting except to Us. The closer a person comes to the place of holiness (*al-qudus*), which is the abode of the obedient and humble, the more gravely arrogance is forbidden to him. "No one who has in his heart an atom's weight of arrogance will enter Paradise." Related by Muslim and others from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him. And as a consequence of its not admitting arrogance, He said: ﴿So get out﴾, meaning: from Paradise, the abode of good pleasure, [so as to avoid that the descent be from an elevated place in Paradise to a place in it lower than it]. Then He gave the reason for His command to descend and depart with His saying, indicating that everyone who displays arrogance is clothed in humiliation: ﴿Indeed, you are of the debased﴾, meaning: those who deserve expulsion, distance, lowliness, and disgrace.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 14:

(p-367) When he knew that envy had driven him away, had brought him down from the courtyard of contentment and had made him sit down [in disgrace], he persisted in it, and asked for what would bring about the lowering of those who were envied from their high ranks to his lowly rank, and he did not ask, in his wretchedness, for what would raise him from his lowly rank to their high ranks. This was by his saying ﴿He said﴾, i.e., Iblis, and it is a resumption [of speech] [and since the context, especially the judgment of abasement stated without restriction, refuses to make it the cause of his request for respite, he mentioned it with the form of kindness, and said]: ﴿Give me respite﴾, i.e., by granting me delay, that is: make me existent in a state in which I may watch and act over an extended time ﴿until the day they are raised﴾, i.e., from the graves, which is the Day of Resurrection. The accursed one by this sought that he would not die, for that time is not a time for death; it is rather the time of the outpouring of everlasting life, in wretchedness or in happiness.

Therefore He, glory be to Him, knew that He had decreed for him a respite, but not in the way he intended, nor as an answer to his request; rather, this had long been predestined in His eternal decree and His pre-existing knowledge, and the wording points to this when He says: ﴿He said, "Indeed you are of those given respite."﴾ That is, in general terms. He withheld him from being protected against death, as He mentioned in two surahs, al-Hijr and Sad: "until the Day of the Appointed Time," which is the time of the first blast, when the living die and he dies along with them. This clause was omitted in this surah because this surah is for warning, and vagueness of the matter is more intense in that respect. He granted him the respite while He intended by it corruption, for he does not exceed His command in it nor His determination of it. And because He, glory be to Him, cannot be questioned about what He does, and so that His wisdom may be manifest, exalted is He, in reward and punishment.

(p-٣٦٨) Since He had decreed wretchedness for him, He met the blessing of respite and the lengthening of his life with persistence in disbelief, and informed him of this about himself by saying ﴿He said﴾, as a consequence of his bringing them into disobedience through the species of the children of Adam: ﴿Because You have led me astray﴾, i.e., because of Your leading me astray, which is the bringing about of error and the holding of falsehood in my heart on account of them. ﴿I will surely sit in wait for them﴾, i.e., I will act in turning them away from good like one who is firmly established and wholly devoted [the deliberate one who has no occupation other than what he is devoted to] during the period of Your respite to me, by cutting them off from You, by preventing them from doing what You commanded them and driving them to do what You forbade them, just as a highway robber sits in wait for travelers in order to seize them. ﴿Your path﴾, i.e., along all of Your path, as indicated by the omission of the preposition (naz' al-khafid), ﴿the straight﴾, which is Islam in all its branches. Whoever attributes leading astray to other than God, because he believes that this is something God is exalted above, has fallen into an evil worse than what he fled from, namely that he has made two agents in existence whose choice of one opposes the choice of the other.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 17:

Since he has devoted himself to this with utmost diligence, he works upon them through whispering, by himself and by those among the devils of the jinn and mankind who obey him, to an extent that exceeds all bounds and overwhelms the powers. He indicated this with the particle of delay (thumma), and so, emphatically, said: ﴿Then I will surely come to them﴾, meaning, a coming that is inevitable for me, its beginning being ﴿from before them﴾, meaning, openly confronting them, so that I urge them to do what they know to be wrong; "and" [coming] ﴿from behind them﴾, meaning, by catching them unaware, so that they do what is utterly corrupt while having no awareness at all of its corruption when they engage in it, and thus I guide them, by that, to engage in the like of it while they do not perceive. ﴿And from﴾, meaning, going beyond the direction that is ﴿on their right﴾ toward them; ﴿and from﴾, meaning, going beyond what is ﴿on their left﴾, meaning, by deception, so that they do it while it is confused for them. These are the directions from which it is possible to come. Perhaps the purpose of ʿan (from), which conveys the sense of passing beyond, is to connect the directions of front and back so that his coming encompasses the entire surrounding direction. [The four directions indicate his corruption and deception in what they know well, and in what they know nothing of, and in what is confused for them to a slight or great degree. And the one whose mention is left out above is that he has no power to come from above, lest his affair be confused with the angels; this is mentioned in some reports, as it is mentioned in the biography of Waraqa ibn Nawfal, may Allah be pleased with him.]

When the accursed one resolved upon this with a true resolve, and saw its means made easy through being granted respite and the like, he thought that by what he saw of their desires and fortunes he would attain most of his need, and so, by way of coordinating with his determination, he said: "So I will surely mislead them, and they will certainly follow me." ﴿And you will not find most of them﴾, as is the usual habit of most people in wickedness, ﴿grateful﴾. Thus, misery was intended for him, and he immersed himself in envy; had the wretched one been intended for good, he would have substituted envy with emulation, [so he sought] to elevate himself to their high ranks through weeping, regret, enjoining good, forbidding evil, and giving sincere counsel, in submission to the station of Lordship and humility before the greatness of His majesty.

Since it was as though it were said, "What did he say to him?", the answer is: ﴿He said﴾ in reply to what he (Iblis) mentioned of his own strength and power in this context, and what he revealed of arrogance and self-glorification, which indicated that he belongs to the people of lowliness, who can do nothing except by the permission of the Mighty, the Compeller. [Explicitly stating what was intended by the descent, which may have led to coming down from a high place in Paradise to a place lower than it.] ﴿Get out of it﴾, that is, Paradise, ﴿disgraced﴾, that is, despised, humiliated, and shamed for what you do. Al-Qatta‘ said: "dhamtu al-rajul" means "I shamed the man," and Ibn Faris said: "dha'amtuhu" means "I belittled him." ﴿Expelled﴾, that is, removed and driven away from everything I do not desire.

When he (God) knew something of his condition, the soul became eager to know the condition of those who would follow him. So He said, swearing an oath and emphasizing it with what is due to Him of complete power and perfect majesty: ﴿Whoever of them follows you﴾, that is, of the children of Adam. He answered the oath with what made the answer to the conditional unnecessary, saying: ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you﴾, that is, with you, your kind, and them, ﴿all together﴾, that is, not one of you will escape Me. Whoever among you does this continues to harm his own self, and I do not care at all.

Then he (the Qur'an) connected to that the description of the envier's state with those who are envied, regarding what he (Iblis) asked for, the respite, on account of it; and that he (Iblis) fell upon many of his desires and led astray from among them nations who transgressed the limit, and whose number fell short of counting. Then he made clear that he (Iblis) is less than being able to have any effect, and that the whole matter is in the hand of Him, glorified is He, who made him an instrument for His purpose from him and from them, and that whoever Allah guides is the one guided, and whoever He leads astray, those are the losers. So He said: ﴿Then Satan whispered to them both﴾, i.e., he cast into them in secrecy, with embellishment, repetition, and desire; ﴿to them both﴾, i.e., by what Allah empowered him with, that he flows through the human being as the blood flows, and casts into him in secrecy what inclines his heart toward what he wants. Then he made clear the reason for the whispering by his saying: ﴿that He might reveal﴾, i.e., make manifest, ﴿to them both what was concealed﴾, i.e., what was hidden and covered, by being placed as though it were behind them, so that they would not turn their attention to it, ﴿from them both﴾. The passive construction indicates that the concealing is by something that imposes no burden on them in it, as in His saying: ﴿He strips them of their clothing﴾ [al-A'raf: 27], and ﴿of their private parts﴾, i.e., the places whose exposure would distress them. In this is that the exposure of the shameful part necessitates distance from Paradise, and that between the two there is negation of union and complete contrast.

When he had informed of the whispering and folded up its content, making it understood that it is a great matter and a long deception, he joined to it His saying: ﴿And he said﴾, i.e., in his whispering also, that is, he embellished for them what arose on account of it in their thoughts, this saying: ﴿"Your Lord has forbidden you"﴾, and he reminded them with the attribute of kindness, as a reminder of His honoring them, as a means of enticing them toward what he wants from them, so he said: ﴿"your Lord"﴾, i.e., the One who is kind to you by the kinds of His kindness that you know. ﴿"from"﴾, i.e., He did not make the end of your permission regarding Paradise extend beyond ﴿"this tree"﴾; he combined the demonstrative and the noun for added emphasis in specifying it. ﴿"Except that"﴾, i.e., out of aversion to ﴿"you should become angels"﴾, i.e., in lacking desire and in the ability to fly and to take forms and other properties of theirs, ﴿"or you should become of the immortals"﴾, i.e., by what becomes your nature, those who do not die and are not removed from Paradise at all.

When he had conveyed this meaning to them, he informed that he had emphasized it with a great emphasis, as one who swears emphasizes what he swears to. So he said: ﴿And he swore to them both﴾, i.e., he swore to them. However, he used the form of mutual action (al-mufa'alah, "qasamahuma") to indicate that between them there occurred evasions and attempts in which he exerted effort. And he emphasized what he swore to, knowing that they were disposed to aversion from disobedience, with several kinds of emphasis in his saying: ﴿Indeed, I am to you both﴾. The fronting of the prepositional phrase (taqdim al-jar), which conveys exclusivity (al-ikhtisas), indicates that he is saying: "I have singled you both out with all of my counsel," ﴿[and] indeed, I am of the sincere advisers﴾. In this there is a warning to be wary of the one who swears, for the more prevalent case is that every frequent swearer is a liar, since he does not swear except when he thinks that the one he addresses will not believe him, and no one thinks this except one who is habituated to lying.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 22:

(p-374) When he had informed them of part of his whispering to them, he made its consequence their descent, which is a fall from the height of nobility to the depth of harm and excess. So He said: ﴿So he brought them down﴾, that is, He lowered them from what they were in of the loftiness of obedience, [like what He did to himself through disobedience, which made him deserve descent from the abode of honour], ﴿by deception﴾, that is, by trickery and stratagem, until Adam forgot the covenant of his Lord. His saying ﴿So when they tasted﴾ indicates swiftness in the requital through the particle fa' (so), and the tasting, which is the beginning of eating, ﴿of the tree﴾, that is, they found its taste. ﴿There became apparent to them﴾, that is, there appeared to them ﴿their private parts﴾, that is, their nakedness, whose appearing distressed them, and their clothing fell away from them, so each of them saw what had been hidden from him of the other's nakedness, and that was the aim of the envious one. So they were ashamed at that. ﴿And they began﴾, that is, they set about and proceeded ﴿to attach over themselves﴾, that is, to join together by sewing ﴿from the leaves of the Garden﴾, one leaf to another. ﴿And their Lord called to them﴾, that is, the One who is good to them by His commanding and forbidding them, and they did none of that except in His sight. So He said, rebuking them for what they had done and reproaching them: "O My servants, ﴿Did I not forbid you﴾", that is, did I not set for you a limit in what was permitted to you, transgressing ﴿from that tree﴾, that is, the one whose due was distance from it, which caused nearness to this noble place as a kindness to you, ﴿and did I not tell you that Satan﴾, that is, the one who was arrogant about prostrating out of envy of you, O Adam, and jealousy of you, so he was burned (p-375) by My anger, was expelled and was removed from My mercy, ﴿is to you both﴾, that is, to you and your spouse and to everyone who branches from you both and is attributed to you both, ﴿a clear enemy﴾, evident in enmity, who comes to you from every place he can come from, openly, covertly and deceitfully. So he, despite the evident nature of his enmity, is subtle in scheming through what I have empowered him to do by establishing causes. For I gave him strength for the scheming, and I gave you strength for the escape, and I told you: "Contend with him; if you overcome him, you are of My party, and if he overcomes you, you are of his party," along with the enmity he has toward you. Thus the verse alerts that whoever goes astray is only following the greatest of his enemies and abandoning the best of his allies.

When this was the case, the listener longed to hear their reply, so it is answered by His saying: ﴿They said﴾, that is, Adam and Hawwa' (Eve), peace be upon them, with the best of greetings and honour, [the speech of the elect in their hastening to repentance]: ﴿Our Lord﴾, that is, O You who are good to us and bestow favour upon us, ﴿we have wronged ourselves﴾, that is, we have harmed them by bringing them out of the light of obedience into the darkness of disobedience. So if You do not turn us back and accept our repentance, we will remain disobedient. ﴿And if You do not forgive us﴾, that is, erase what we have done, both its substance and its trace, ﴿and have mercy on us﴾, so that You raise our ranks, ﴿we will surely be among the losers.﴾ The verse thus indicates that they fled to submission through acknowledgment. They named their sin "wrong" (ẓulm), even though it was only a departure from what is more preferable (al-awlā), because it occurred through forgetfulness, as in Ṭaha. This is the custom of the great, who magnify the small slip committed by one of them. They did not dispute as Iblis did. In this there is an indication that hastening to acknowledge a sin is the act of the noble, because it is among the lofty qualities of character, and that nothing is its equal in securing pardon and removing turbidity. Disputing, by contrast, is the act of the base and among the blameworthy qualities of character, and it is among the things that bring about anger, which calls for expulsion.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 24:

When the soul had become eager for the answer of the Exalted, the Great, glory be to Him, it was answered with His saying: ﴿Go down⦆ — that is, to the abode of striving (mujahadah), contention (muqara'ah) and opposition (munakadah) — while ﴿some of you are enemies to others﴾. That is: you two and those you will beget are enemies of Iblis and of whoever is born (of him), and some of your offspring are enemies to others. There is no deliverance except by following what I have granted you of the guidance of reason and what I have sent down to you, confirmed by transmitted revelation (naql). In this there is a clear warning for anyone who has even the slightest measure of sense, by indicating the ugliness of the outcome of disobedience, even together with repentance, and an urging to constant vigilance (muraqabah) out of fear of the evil of punishment. ﴿And for you on the earth⦆ — that is, of its kind — ﴿is a dwelling-place⦆, that is, a place of settling, such as plains and the like, ﴿and enjoyment for a time⦆, that is, until the end of your lifespans and then the end of the lifespan of the world (al-dunya).

When this had become known, that the earth has an end for its existence, and among the philosophers of metempsychosis (al-tanasukhiyya) and others who affirm divine unity, there were those who said that souls are detached from corporeality and its attachments, and that when the body perishes the soul joins the higher beings, either with a star or something else, or descends into the ranks of the angels, and its attachment to the body is entirely nullified in every respect, so that it no longer connects to it, neither through governing it nor otherwise, nor through resurrection (according to those among them who affirm resurrection), it was as if it were said: "What will be after that?" So it was answered with His saying: ﴿He said﴾ [i.e., God, refuting what they believe about the nullification of attachment to the body, expressing by the address in the pronoun that refers to this specific structure as spirit and body] ﴿"Therein﴾ [i.e., in the earth, not in anything else] ﴿you will live﴾, i.e., first and second, [in the state you are in, both outwardly and inwardly, as bodies and spirits] ﴿and therein﴾ [i.e., likewise, not in anything else, as you witness for yourselves] ﴿you will die﴾, i.e., from the first life [as a whole, so that the spirits have some connection with the bodies in some respect, until the dead person sits in the grave and answers the questioning of the two angels, peace be upon them, and the bodies enjoy its pleasures and suffer its pains]. Thus the Gathering was alluded to along with a detailed account of the state of existence on earth, and the narrative was concluded with what it began with, namely the announcement of resurrection, by His saying: ﴿And from it﴾ [i.e., not from anything else, by the report of the Truthful One] ﴿you will be brought forth﴾, i.e., [in spirit and body] after your death therein and your return to what you were at first, dust, for recompense and for the manifestation of the fruit of sovereignty, by ruling justice between some of you and others, and by adorning oneself [with the attribute of] justice, so that what some of you used to do to others of oppression and tyranny, which none of your chiefs would accept even from the least of his slaves, will not go unpunished. It is known from this that the indication of the Gathering is the conclusion (fadhlaka) of the narrative, and this is clearer [than its mention] previously in His saying: ﴿So We will surely question those to whom messengers were sent﴾ [al-A'raf: 6].

When al-Biqa'i had explained earlier that what necessitated their expulsion from the Garden was the same thing that made their nakedness exposed, namely disobedience, and had finished with what followed from it, to the point of informing them that He had decreed their settling in this abode after that one, he began to warn us against our enemy, as He had warned our father (peace be upon him). He began with His words, as an explanation, because He had bestowed upon us in it everything we need in religion and in the world, and as a notice of the disgrace and distance from all good that exposing one's nakedness entails, and as an indication that concealment is a great gate of taqwa (God-consciousness): ﴿O children of Adam﴾.

Since the discourse concerned the exposure of nakedness, and since Adam (peace be upon him) lacked a covering until he resorted to leaves, it was fitting that what would happen in this regard be anticipated. So He said, opening with the particle of anticipation (qad): ﴿We have sent down﴾, that is, by Our majesty, ﴿upon you﴾, from the traces of the blessings of the heaven, either initially by creating it or by sending down its causes, such as rain and the like, ﴿clothing﴾, that is, which your father could not obtain in the Garden, ﴿to cover your private parts﴾, as guidance to the remedy for that ailment and as information that the very act of exposure is a deficiency unfitting for the presence of perfection. And He said: ﴿and as finery﴾, indicating that He—glorified is He—has added to us, beyond the covering, that by which there is adornment and beauty, metaphorically borrowed from the feathers of a bird, making attractive what keeps one far from sin and brings one near to the presence of the Lord.

When He mentioned the sensory clothing and divided it into a covering and an adorning, He followed it with the immaterial, saying, indicating by its separation from what precedes it in the reading of the majority (of reciters), and to the perfection of its magnitude, urging toward it and recommending it: ﴿and the clothing of taqwa﴾. Thus it is known that the covering of nakedness is both sensory and immaterial: the sensory is the clothing of garments, and the immaterial is adorning oneself with what stirs one toward fear of God. Then He increased the magnitude of the immaterial by His words: ﴿that is better﴾, that is, the clothing of taqwa is better than the clothing of garments. But He separated it with the demonstrative noun coupled with the particle of distance, as a hint to the loftiness of its rank and the goodness of its outcome, because it is the more important of the two garments, since its removal happens through the exposure of sensory and immaterial nakedness. For if a person adorns himself with the finest garments while not being God-conscious, he is entirely nakedness; and if he is God-conscious while having nothing on him but a small rag covering his private parts, he is in the utmost beauty, covering and perfection. Indeed, even if he is exposed in some states, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: «The veil between your private parts and the eyes of the jinn is that one of you, when he enters the privy, says: "In the name of God. O God! I seek refuge in You from the vile male and female devils."» Related by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah from Ali (may God be pleased with him).

[What is nearly certain regarding this is that sins are the cause of the descent of the nakedness from which comes the weakness of the body and the shortening of life, sensorily or in meaning, by the removal of blessing from it, because of what is understood from what preceded in al-Baqarah, at the beginning of creation, from the Torah, that God, exalted is He, said to Adam (peace be upon him): "Eat from all the trees of the Garden. But as for the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, do not eat from it, for on the day you eat from it you will surely die," a death that prepares you for death sensorily, and it will be decreed upon you to be occupied with the means of livelihood, so your life will be shortened in meaning through the departure of its blessing. And God knows best.]

When the wearing of clothing was part of the legislation distinguishing the human being from the rest of the animals, and of preparing its means that Adam (peace be upon him) did not find in the Garden, of grace, favor, and a sign of the greatness of the Bestower, His mercy, His power, and His choice in what is known, He said: ﴿That﴾, that is, the sending down of clothing, ﴿is among the signs of God﴾, that is, He who possesses the attributes of perfection indicating His grace and mercy toward His servants. Perhaps the shift (iltifat) from address to the third person ﴿so that they may remember﴾, even if only at the least degree of remembrance, is indicated by the assimilation (idgham) (of the letters). This is lest the contentious one say: the urging to remember is specific to the addressed, and he claims that they are the Muslims only. That is: We sent that down so that their state would be the state of one who remembers, and so knows that what is reprehensible from him is reprehensible from others as well.

When the purpose of mentioning the narratives, especially the narratives of the prophets, is to take a lesson from them, the explanation of what took place between Adam (peace be upon him) and Satan, of Satan's intense enmity, calls for warning against Satan. Since the situation was dangerous and escape from it difficult, he (Allah) pointed to this by emphasis and by explaining the hidden schemes and subtle means with which Satan was empowered, so that the one who is saved would know that he was saved only by pure divine guidance and mere kindness, and would therefore turn to gratitude, disowning any power or strength of his own. So He said, addressing them with words that convey tenderness, compassion, affection, gentleness and a sense of their weakness: ﴿O children of Adam﴾. That is: the one whom I created with My own hand, made to dwell in My Garden, and then sent down to the abode of My love, intending to raise you to the summit of My worship and to lower you to the depths of My disobedience. ﴿Let not Satan tempt you﴾, that is: let him not mingle with you in a way that inclines you away from moderation. ﴿Satan﴾, that is: the far removed one, burned by sins, who turns you away from what would be the means of your return to your homeland, by adorning for you the stripping off of the garment of piety, which leads to the exposure of nakedness and brings the disgrace of this world, thereby preventing you from entering the Garden and making you enter the Fire. ﴿As he drove your parents out of the Garden﴾, by the temptation with which he tempted them after they had dwelt in it, settled in it and made it their home. You know that prevention is easier than removal, so beware, then beware again! This verse is of the kind called ihtibak (a figure in which two complementary elements are mutually omitted): it mentions the temptation first, as an indication of its omission the second time, and the expulsion second, as an indication of the omission of its opposite or counterpart the first time.

Since he (Satan) had exerted great effort in expelling them, the commentator explains the expulsion, pointing to this, as continual whispering and persistent deceit and trickery, by using the present tense verb. So He said [in the position of a circumstantial clause referring to the subject "Satan"]: ﴿stripping off from them﴾, that is [by causation], through continual adornment and seizing them from a place of safety, ﴿their garment﴾ [that is, the garment with which Allah, glorified be He, had covered them as long as they were guarding themselves from committing what they had been forbidden, and this indicates that uncovering is incompatible with the Garden, by the reason stated in His words: ﴿to show them their private parts﴾]. For that is the beginning of abandoning modesty, and (modesty and faith are in one bond), as Al-Tabarani and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya reported from Ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), and (modesty brings nothing but good), as reported by the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) from 'Imran ibn Husayn (may Allah be pleased with them both).

Since Satan's prohibition of our being tempted is in reality a prohibition to us of being tempted by him, it carries the force of: so that your caution against his temptation may be intensified, for he is subtle in scheming, deep in his penetration, and marvellously skilled in deception. He gave the reason for this by His words: ﴿Indeed, he sees you﴾, that is, Satan, ﴿he and his tribe﴾, that is, his soldiers, ﴿from where you cannot see them﴾. Malik ibn Dinar said: "Indeed, an enemy who sees you while you do not see him is a severe burden, except for the one whom Allah protects."

Since it was as if it were said: Why were they given such great power over us, a power by which hardly anyone is safe? He said, lightening the matter and in reality weakening their scheming: ﴿Indeed We﴾, that is, We did that, because We, with the greatness We possess, ﴿have made the devils﴾, that is, those burned with wrath and far from mercy, ﴿protectors﴾, that is, companions and associates, ﴿for those who do not believe﴾, that is, who do not renew their faith. This is because there is a natural affinity between them in temperament, which necessitates following. As for Our protégés, whom We protected by Our power from him, or whom We tested slightly through them and then freed them from them by Our kindness, they are not protectors for them; rather, they are enemies to them, and their sign is that they believe. The meaning is that We enabled them to deceive you by hiding them from you while you could see them, and by this We gave them power over those whom We have decided do not believe, by their adorning for them and their whispering and their emboldening, so that they would help them in some situations and bring them to some of their aims. We did this so that the perfect man, who deserves the highest ranks and whom the angels visit with greetings and gifts, would be distinguished from others. So take your precautions, for the matter (p-383) is dangerous and escape from it difficult. In other words: We have set for you a path and placed on both its sides enemies who see you while you do not see them, and We have empowered them over some of you. Whoever follows the right way is saved, and whoever deviates is captured by the enemy. Whoever approaches the edges by following doubts comes close to the enemy, and whoever comes close to him is led astray by him; so the nearer he comes to him, the more able he is to capture him. Anyone who is captured after having been freed should be on guard. Our not seeing them in general does not necessitate the impossibility of seeing them; moreover, it is established that they can take forms in dense bodies, and that the sons of Adam can see them in those bodies, like the devil whom Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him) saw when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded him to guard the charity; and likewise Ubayy ibn Ka'b (may Allah be pleased with him); the story of Khalid ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) concerning the devil of al-'Uzza is well known in the biographies; likewise the story of Sawad ibn Qarib (may Allah be pleased with him) concerning the guidance given to him by his jinn companion; likewise the account of Ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) concerning the like of this, and others. In my commentary on my versified version of the Sira there is much of this. Likewise is the story of the 'Ifrit who slipped upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with a flame of fire in order to cut off his prayer, but Allah humiliated him and enabled the Messenger of Allah to seize him. The Prophet (ﷺ) said:

"Had it not been for the supplication of my brother Solomon (peace be upon him), he would have been left tied to a pillar of the mosque, with the children of the people of Medina playing with him."

Abu Hayyan said: Except that seeing them in their forms is rare, just as the angels (peace be upon them) appear in forms, as in the hadith about Gabriel (peace be upon him).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 28:

When He made their sign of being under the sway of Satan the lack of faith, He linked to that another sign, saying: ﴿And when they commit an immorality﴾, that is, a matter extremely ugly, such as polytheism and exposing the private parts during the circumambulation (tawaf), ﴿they say﴾, giving as a reason for their committing it, ﴿"We found our fathers upon it"﴾, that is, upon the immorality. Since this reason was clearly evident in its shamefulness and manifest in its defect, they added to it, by way of fabrication, something that could serve as a cause, so they said, referring to the Greatest Name without showing restraint regarding His majesty, greatness and perfection: ﴿"And Allah has commanded us to it."﴾

Since the first reason was discarded, and the knowledge of its falsehood was self-evident (badihi), because it is known that if they had found their fathers foolish in acquiring wealth they would not have followed them, He turned away from it, pointing to that, and commanded an answer to the second, which is a fabrication against the Supreme King, even though they claimed to be the furthest of people from any kind of lying and the most scrupulous in seeking the truth. He said: ﴿Say, "Indeed, Allah does not command immorality"﴾, that is, Him to whom all perfection belongs does not command anything of this kind.

Since lying is ugly in itself, and among them it is the most ugly of all ugliness absolutely, how much more so when it is attributed to one of their great ones, and how much more so when it is attributed to the Greatest of the great! He said, disapproving of them, rebuking them and threatening them: ﴿"Do you say about Allah that which you do not know?"﴾, that is, the One who possesses all greatness, ﴿because you did not hear that from Allah without intermediary, nor was it transmitted to you by a sound channel from any of the prophets, peace be upon them.﴾ And in it (p-385) is a severe threat against ignorance and against saying about Allah on the basis of conjecture.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 29:

When their justification by the command of God necessarily implied that, when He commands something, He follows His command by bidding them to convey His command, which He brought, the proof of reason being reinforced by decisive transmitted evidence, He said: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to these people who have cast off the Law and customary decency, ﴿"My Lord has commanded justice"﴾, He who has done good to me by imposing on me the obligation of the noblest deeds to which lofty resolves call, ﴿"justice"﴾, which is the middle course between what is grossly excessive by going beyond the limit, and what is deficient by falling short of it. And since the implied sense is: "So be just, following what He has commanded," or since justice (al-qist) is a verbal noun that resolves into "that you be just," He coordinated with it: ﴿"and set your faces [upright] at every place of prayer"﴾, sincere, not committing any form of injustice, ﴿"at every place of prayer"﴾, that is, at every place, time and state in which prostration is fitting, and let no one restrict himself to a place or a time by saying, when prayer has overtaken him: "I will go and pray in my mosque." ﴿"And call upon Him"﴾ at all of that, with the call of worship, ﴿"sincerely devoted to Him in religion"﴾, that is, do not associate anything with Him.

Since the meaning is: whoever does not do this, He will punish him after returning him to life after death, he expressed this by stating the proof for it, giving as a reason: ﴿"As He originated you"﴾, that is, in the first creation, so you are originated, We shall bring you back after death, so you ﴿"will return"﴾ as two groups:

[Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 30:]

﴿A party He guided﴾, that is, He created guidance in their hearts, so the reward of guidance became due to them. ﴿And a party﴾ [He] misguided. He then explained "misguided," which must be understood in the accusative case, with His words ﴿error became due upon them﴾, that is, it was established and became necessary. ﴿Error became due upon them﴾ means that He misguided them, so they will be gathered on the basis of what they were upon in the world, in their religions and in their bodies. It has become clear that there are two instances of ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which one term is omitted from each of two parallel clauses and the other clause supplies the missing term). In the first, He affirmed "He begins" as evidence for the omission of "He restores," and mentioned "you return" as evidence for the omission of "you are brought forth." In the second, He affirmed "guided" as evidence for the omission of "misguided," and mentioned "the due portions of error" as evidence for the omission of "the due portions of guidance."

When He, glorified is He, repeated the mention of resurrection, as wisdom calls for, in order to establish what the addressee denies, to make him comfortable with it, to break his pride, to strengthen his conviction, and to subdue his fury, He concluded with what is more indicative of it than what came before, from His words ﴿and from it you will be brought forth﴾ (Qur'an 20:55). He then gave the reason for what He concluded this evidence with, concerning the due portions of error, that is, their necessity, meaning the necessity of its consequences upon them, through His words: ﴿Indeed, they took﴾, that is, they burdened themselves in opposition to what the primordial fitrah (the innate human disposition) had called them to, by taking ﴿the devils as allies﴾, that is, as close associates and helpers, ﴿besides God﴾, that is, the Supreme King who has no equal. ﴿And they suppose﴾, that is, while they are in fact thinking, because of the weakness of their minds, ﴿that they are guided﴾. By this He indicated that they deserved punishment, because they were content, in the foundations, where certainty must be sought through earnest striving, with mere conjectures.

When Allah, glorified is He, commanded justice and facing the right direction at every place of worship, He commanded them what is fitting during that facing: covering the nakedness, which was previously urged, and explaining the ugliness of exposing it and the evil of its effect, expressing it with the word *zīnah* (adornment). This was to encourage it, to permit adornment, and to show that it is not something to be scrupulously avoided. This is based on his ﷺ saying: "Allah loves that when He expands sustenance for a servant, the effect of His blessing should be seen upon him." Narrated by Aḥmad, al-Tirmidhī (p-387), and Ibn Manī', from Abū Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him. He followed this with the greatest of what the son of Adam should observe in moderation in eating and drinking, saying, repeating the call to show compassion and to display great tenderness, and to remind them of the story of their father Adam, peace be upon him, which expelled him from the Garden despite his being Allah's chosen one, so that caution would be intensified: ﴿O children of Adam﴾, that is, the one whom We adorned, whom Satan deceived, and then We protected him from his evil by what We bestowed upon him of a good repentance and a great turning toward Us. ﴿Take your adornment﴾, that is, that which was previously expressed by *rīsh* (plumage) for covering the nakedness and for beautifying oneself at the gathering for worship, ﴿at every place of worship﴾.
