Abu Hayyan said: He negated these two attributes from it specifically, rather than the rest of the attributes of divinity, because the negation of speech [entails] the negation of knowledge, and the negation of guidance to a way entails the negation of power, and the negation of these two attributes entails the negation of the rest of the attributes.

Since this was a matter very great and very unlikely to occur, especially from a people whose prophet was among them, and especially since He had shown them of the blessings and signs whose lights filled the horizons, it was deserving of emphasis, so God, exalted is He, said: ﴿They took it﴾, i.e., with the utmost earnestness, energy and desire, ﴿and they were﴾, i.e., by disposition and nature, along with what was established for them of the lights, ﴿wrongdoers﴾. i.e., their state is the state of one who walks in darkness, or the intended meaning is that wrongdoing is an inseparable attribute of theirs, so it is no wonder when they do the like of that.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 149:

Since this came within the context of ﴿That is because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them﴾ [Al-A'raf: 146], which implies that whoever lies in this manner will be destroyed, the listener awaited news of their swift destruction. Instead, it informed him that He prevented them from that and deprived them of the opportunity to hasten to repentance. Because the listener's eagerness for this news had grown intense, He advanced it before its cause, which is Musa's (ʿalayhi al-salam) return to them and his rebuke of them. Also, because the context concerns their hastening into wickedness, it does not mention the acceptance of their repentance, as in al-Baqarah. Since it was known that they would soon realise the evil of what they had committed, because their Prophet was among them, He used an expression that conveys the sense that the implied meaning is: "they were overcome with regret." He joined to it, in the manner of something well known, ﴿And when they were overcome with regret﴾. That is, their teeth fell (into their hands), some of them out of remorse, a falling as if it were without choice, because of the intense grief and sorrow that overwhelmed them and removed their reflection. For this reason, the verb was put in the passive form. ﴿And when they saw that they had gone astray﴾, that is, from the clear path. ﴿They said﴾ in repentance and return to Allah, as their father Adam (ʿalayhi al-salam) said: ﴿If our Lord does not have mercy upon us﴾, that is, the One who never cut off His kindness from us, so how (could He be) angry and (yet) continue His kindness? ﴿And forgive us﴾, that is, erase our sins both in essence and in effect, lest He take vengeance upon us in the future. ﴿We will surely be among the losers﴾, that is, He would take vengeance upon us for our sins.

(p-٨٨) When He informed of the reason for delaying retribution against them, even though they were equal to those upon whom the punishment fell, in terms of what calls for retribution, He, glorified be He, informed of the state of Musa, peace be upon him, with them when he returned to them in anger for God's sake and in rebuke of those who opposed him, together with what it contained of mercy and humility. He said: ﴿And when Musa returned to his people, angry and grieved﴾, i.e., from the private communion [with God]. ﴿Angry﴾, i.e., in the state of his return, when God the Exalted had informed him about them regarding the worship of the calf. ﴿Grieved﴾, i.e., of intense anger and sorrow. ﴿He said: "Evil is what you have done as my successors"﴾, i.e., evil is the succession by which you succeeded me, for you stood in my place and acted in my place and behind me.

Since this might have given the impression that they did it in his absence, while he was present at the edge of the camp, He said: ﴿after me﴾, i.e., when you worshipped other than God, O worshippers, and when you did not suffice [as guardians] for them, O monotheists, after my departure to the mountain for the divine appointment, and after you had heard from me the declaration of God's oneness, and singling Him out from His creation in worship, and negating partners from Him. You saw when I restrained you and forbade you from worshipping other than Him, when you said: ﴿Make for us a god as they have gods﴾ [al-A'raf: 138]. It is the right of successors to follow the conduct of the one who appointed them and not to oppose him in anything.

Since he had commanded them not to introduce any innovation until he returned to them, he denounced their failure to wait for him and said: ﴿Have you hastened﴾. Al-Saghani said in al-Majma': "you outran," and others said: "he hastened from the command" when he left it incomplete, and it is implicitly meant as "outran." So the meaning is: (p-٨٩) outrunning ﴿the command of your Lord﴾, i.e., the appointed term, which He had continued to bestow favour upon you; that is, you did this before the arrival of the term of the appointment, which my Lord extended, namely the ten days, by my returning to you at its limit. So you assumed that I had died, and you changed as the nations changed after the death of their prophets. Abu Abd Allah al-Qazzaz also said: "you hastened" means "you outran," and from this you say: "I hastened so-and-so," meaning I outran him. Ibn al-Tayyani attributed this to al-Asma'i.

﴿And he threw down the tablets﴾, i.e., those containing the Torah, out of anger for God and to frighten his people. This indicates that the anger reached a level in him that he could not control, and that was for God the Exalted. ﴿And he seized his brother by the head﴾, i.e., by his hair, ﴿dragging him toward him﴾, i.e., on the presumption that he had fallen short, and to inform them that his anger over this act had reached a degree beyond description, because it was the uprooting of the religion from its foundation.

Since Harun, peace be upon him, had not fallen short in forbidding them, he began to inform Musa, peace be upon him, of that, specifying "the mother" even though he was his full brother, as a reminder to him of the kinship that calls for tenderness and softness, especially since she was a believer and had suffered fears on his account. So He, glorified be He, resumed the report of that with His saying: ﴿He said: "O son of my mother"﴾. The particle of address and the ya' of possession were omitted because the situation calls for brevity. The majority read the mim with a fatha, as an assimilation [lahu] to "khamsata 'ashar" (fifteen), and with the alif that replaced the ya' of possession deleted. Ibn 'Amir, Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr on the authority of 'Asim read the mim with a kasra, presuming the deletion of the ya' of possession for lightness: ﴿Indeed the people﴾, i.e., the calf-worshippers, whose standing in matters they intend is known, ﴿have considered me weak﴾, i.e., they regarded me as weak and created my weakness by their intimidation of me, ﴿and they nearly killed me﴾, i.e., they came close to doing so because of my denunciation of what they did [so the obligation fell from me].

Since his release followed from this, he feared that anger would prevent that [the explanation] from being fixed in his mind and established in his heart. So he said: ﴿So do not let the enemies gloat over me﴾, i.e., do not make them rejoice at what you do to me, so that I would be blamed by them and by you. When he appealed to him by reminding him of the gloating, which is also a gloating at him, he followed it with a harm that specifically concerns him, and said: ﴿And do not place me﴾, i.e., by your punishment of me, ﴿with the wrongdoing people﴾, i.e., so that you would cut me off by counting me among them and putting me in their company rather than among those whom You love of the righteous, and joining me to those whom You hate of the corrupt, who did the deed of one who is in darkness, placing worship in other than its proper place, without any doubt or confusion at all.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 151:

When it became clear to him what befits the noble station of his brother, namely that he had not fallen short in calling them to God nor slackened in forbidding them from error, and he saw that the anger which had appeared was a deterrent to his people and a restraint holding them back from what they had committed, (Moses) made a supplication for himself and for his brother, while acknowledging his inability and that none can suffice except through pardon. God, glorified is He, placed this in the manner of a reply to a question, with His words: ﴿He said: "My Lord,"﴾ that is, O You who have shown kindness to me, ﴿"forgive me"﴾ that is, for what the anger for Your sake moved me to do to my brother, of casting him down, ﴿"and my brother"﴾ that is, for his not having attained what I had wanted from him of striving against them.

When he prayed for the erasure of the shortcoming, he followed it with honour, saying: ﴿"And admit us"﴾ that is, (p-91) myself, my brother, and everyone who is joined with us, ﴿"into Your mercy"﴾ so that it may envelop us and surround us. And since the implied sense was: "You are the best of forgivers," he joined to it ﴿"and You are the most merciful of the merciful,"﴾ that is, because You bestow what neither effort can count nor reckoning can enumerate, without any benefit reaching You and without any harm befalling You by doing so or by not doing so.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 152:

Since the verse concerns him (Musa) and his brother (Harun), who are both protected from sins, it omitted what relates to forgiveness and mentioned what relates to mercy. This is unlike what comes in the supplication made for him and for the seventy of his people, for there it reversed that arrangement. And since the innocence of the Caliph (Harun) was established, and it was indicated that he, despite that, was in need of forgiveness, the soul turned to the state of the corrupters, and so (Allah) said, informing about that: ﴿Indeed, those who took the calf﴾, meaning: they desired with a complete desire to take it as a god, in opposition to what was fixed in the original nature (fitrah), and what al-Kalim (ﷺ) (Musa) called them to, peace be upon him. ﴿Will surely attain﴾, meaning: by a promise that will not be broken, ﴿anger﴾, meaning: a punishment in which there is expulsion or removal. Perhaps it is what they were commanded regarding the killing of themselves. It also indicated that in it there is gentleness toward them and good upbringing, so that those who remain among them may repent, by His saying: ﴿from their Lord﴾, meaning: the One besides whom there is no one who does them good, who overtakes them in this world and follows them in the Hereafter. ﴿And humiliation in the life of this world﴾, meaning: a recompense for them for their fabrication, and likewise for whoever approved of their deed, especially if he was of their descendants, such as Qurayzah, al-Nadir and the people of Khaybar. ﴿And thus﴾, meaning: and the like of their recompense, ﴿We recompense the fabricators﴾, meaning: those who rely upon falsehood. This is a text that every fabricator is humiliated, as is observed, even if some of them display boldness.

(p-92) When he mentioned those who persist in disobedience, he followed it with those who repent, encouraging others to be in their state, and said: ﴿And those who did evil deeds﴾. He expressed it with "doing" (ʿamal) as an indication of pardon, even if they committed them knowingly; and he used the plural to inform that no sin is too great for Him, however great it is, however much it multiplies, and however long its time lasts. For this reason he joined with the particle of distance, saying: ﴿then repented﴾, and he confirmed the matter and negated metaphor with his words: ﴿after them﴾. Then he mentioned the foundation without which no deed is accepted, in a way that makes clear there is no difference between whether there was apostasy in the evil deeds or not; so he said: ﴿and believed﴾. Then he answered the subject with his words: ﴿indeed your Lord﴾, meaning: the one who does good to you by accepting the repentance of the repentant, for what He has made you travel of that, because you are kind and merciful to them. ﴿after them﴾, meaning: after the repentance, ﴿is Forgiving﴾, meaning: One who erases the sins of the repentant, both their essence and their trace, however great and numerous they are. ﴿Merciful﴾, meaning: He acts toward them as the merciful acts, with righteousness, honor, kindness and bounty. It seems that the persisters were those who were killed when Musa, peace be upon him, ordered them to kill themselves; when the persistent ones were destroyed and the rest repented, and the innocence of his brother was established, and he remained at his rank of commanding good, forbidding evil, and striving in the matter of Allah, the reason for anger ceased, so He, glorified is He, informed of what follows it, and said:

﴿And when the anger subsided﴾, i.e., it ceased. He likened anger to a speaker who had been urging Musa, peace be upon him, on and inciting him toward what it required and demanded. When it had satisfied his rage, it calmed down and cut off its speech, and its opposite, which is contentment, took its place. ﴿The anger went out from Musa﴾, and it is the seething of the heart from that which pains the soul. ﴿He took up the tablets﴾, i.e., those which he had brought from God, after he had thrown them down. ﴿And in their inscription﴾, i.e., while the matter written in them was ﴿their inscription﴾. Nuskha is an form (fi'la) in the sense of a passive (mafu'la). It is reported from Ibn Abbas that when he threw them down, he fasted, as he had fasted for the conversation (with God), forty more days, and so they were returned to him on two tablets in place of those that had broken.

﴿Guidance﴾, i.e., something that clarifies the purposes. ﴿And mercy﴾, i.e., a cause of honor. ﴿For those who, toward their Lord﴾, i.e., not toward other than Him, ﴿are fearful﴾, i.e., they are worthy of fearing with a great fear that tears hearts apart and compels flight, and they persist in that.

An explanation of what is in these verses, from the words ﴿I will show you the abode of the defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-A'raf: 145], from the wonders of the Torah. The translator says in its Fifth Book, after he had rebuked them for some of what they had done, which had made anger and punishment due to them through the wandering (in the wilderness), and urged them to adhere to God's command so that He would help them:

"As for the commandments which I command you today, keep them and act upon them, that you may live and multiply and inherit the land which God swore to your fathers. Then you shall remember all the way which the Lord your God led you in, and who has humbled you these forty years in the wilderness, to test you and to know what is in your hearts, whether you would keep His commandments or not. He humbled you and made you hungry and fed you with manna, which neither you nor your fathers had known, so that He might make known to you that man does not live by bread alone, but that he lives by what proceeds out of the mouth of God. Your garments did not wear out and your feet did not swell these forty years. Keep the commandments of the Lord your God, walk in His ways and fear Him, for the Lord your God is the one who brings you into a fertile land, a land of many springs and fountains which flow in the deserts and mountains, a land of wheat and barley, in which there are vines, figs, pomegranates, olives, oil and honey. A land in which you shall eat your bread without poverty and in which nothing will be lacking for you, a land whose stones are iron, and from whose mountains you shall extract copper. So be watchful; do not forget the Lord your God, and keep His commandments and His laws which I command you today. Do not be arrogant. When you have eaten and been satisfied and have built houses and dwelt in them, and your flocks and herds have multiplied and your wealth has increased, your hearts will swell and you will forget the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt and rescued you from slavery, and who led you in the great and dreadful wilderness, where there are fiery serpents and scorpions, in places of thirst, where you had no water. He brought forth water for you from the flinty rock and fed you with manna which your fathers did not know, to humble you, to test you, and to do you good in the end. Be careful, lest you say in your hearts: 'My power and the might of my hand have gotten me this wealth.' But remember the Lord your God, for it is He who gives you power to get wealth, so that He may confirm the covenant which He swore to your fathers. If you forget the Lord your God and follow other gods and serve and bow down to them, I testify against you today that you shall surely perish, just as the nations which the Lord destroyed before you, so you shall perish. Hear, O Israelites! [You are passing over the Jordan today to dispossess nations greater and mightier than you, and to conquer great cities fortified up to the heavens, and a great and mighty people, the sons of the giants.] You know and have heard that no man can stand before the giants. Know this day that the Lord your God is the one who passes before you as a consuming fire, and He will destroy and defeat them before you. Do not say in your hearts: 'The Lord has brought us in to inherit this land because of our righteousness,' for the Lord destroys these nations because of their sins, and to confirm the word which He promised to your fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Know that it is not for your righteousness that God gives you this fertile land, for you are a stiff-necked people. Remember and do not forget that you provoked the Lord your God in the wilderness from the day you left the land of Egypt until you arrived at this place. You have continually provoked the Lord your God. At Horeb also you angered the Lord, and the Lord was angry with you and wanted to destroy you, when I went up the mountain and took the two tablets of the covenant which the Lord made with you. I remained on the mountain forty days and nights, I ate no bread and drank no water. The Lord gave me two tablets of stone written with the finger of God, and on them were all the words which the Lord spoke to you from the mountain on the day of the assembly. At the end of the forty days He gave me the two tablets of the covenant. The Lord said to me: 'Arise, go down quickly from here, for your people whom you brought out of the land of Egypt have corrupted themselves and turned aside quickly from the way which I commanded them, and they have made for themselves a molten god.' The Lord also said to me: 'I have seen this people, and behold, they are a stiff-necked people. Let Me alone, that I may destroy them and blot out their name from under heaven, and I will make you a leader of a nation greater and mightier than they.' I turned and came down from the mountain, while the mountain was burning with fire, with the two tablets of the covenant in my hands. I saw that you had sinned before the Lord your God quickly. I took hold of the two tablets of stone and threw them out of my hands and broke them before your eyes. I prayed before the Lord as I did at first, forty days and nights; I ate no bread and drank no water, because of all your sins which you committed, doing evil in the sight of the Lord to provoke Him. For I was afraid of the anger and wrath of God, that He was determined to destroy you. But the Lord listened to me at that time as well. As for the calf which you made, I took it and burned it in the fire, crushed it and ground it very fine until it was like dust, and I cast its dust into the brook that runs down from the mountain. At Taberah, at Massah and at Kibroth-hattaavah you provoked the Lord. When the Lord sent you from Kadesh-barnea, saying: 'Go up and possess the land which I have given you,' you rebelled against the command of the Lord your God and did not believe Him nor obey His voice. You have been rebellious against the Lord from the day I knew you. I prayed before the Lord forty days and nights, because the Lord had said He would destroy you. I prayed and said: 'O Lord God, do not destroy Your people and Your inheritance whom You have redeemed through Your greatness and brought out of Egypt with a mighty hand. Remember Your servants Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Do not look at the stubbornness of this people, their wickedness and their sin, lest the people of the land from which You brought us say: The Lord was not able to bring them into the land which He promised them, and because He hated them He has brought them out to slay them in the wilderness.' They are Your people and Your inheritance, whom You brought out by Your great power and outstretched arm. At that time the Lord said to me: 'Hew for yourself two tablets of stone like the first two, and come up to Me on the mountain, and make an ark of acacia wood.' [In another version: sant wood.] I hewed the two tablets of stone like the first two, and went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hand. And the words of the covenant were written on the two tablets, the Ten Commandments which the Lord spoke to you on the mountain out of the fire on the day of the assembly, and the Lord gave them to me. I came down from the mountain and put the two tablets in the ark which I had made, and I left them there, as the Lord had commanded me. The children of Israel journeyed from Beeroth of the sons of Jaakan to Moserah. There Aaron died and was buried, and his son Eleazar ministered as priest in his place. From there they journeyed to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land of brooks of water. At that time the Lord separated the tribe of Levi to bear the ark of the covenant of the Lord, to stand before the Lord to minister to Him and to bless in His name until this day. Therefore the Levites have no portion or inheritance with the rest of Israel, for the Lord is their inheritance, as He said to them. I remained on the mountain as in the first days, forty days and nights, and the Lord listened to me at that time also. The Lord your God did not destroy you. And the Lord said to me: 'Arise, go forward before the people, that they may enter and possess the land which I swore to their fathers to give them.' And now, O Israel, what does the Lord your God require of you? He requires only that you fear the Lord your God, walk in all His ways, love Him, and serve the Lord your God with all your heart and soul, and keep the commandments of the Lord which I command you today for your good. Heaven and the heaven of heavens belong to the Lord your God, and the earth and all that is in it. Yet the Lord set His affection on your fathers only, and loved them, and chose their descendants after them, above all peoples, as it is this day. Circumcise the foreskin of your hearts and stiffen your necks no more, for the Lord your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, a great, mighty and awesome God who shows no partiality nor takes bribes. He executes justice for the fatherless and the widow, and loves the stranger, giving him food and clothing. So love the stranger, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt. Fear the Lord your God, serve Him, cling to Him, and swear by His name. He is your praise and your God, who has done for you these great and awesome things which your eyes have seen. Know that your fathers went down to Egypt with seventy persons, and now the Lord your God has made you as numerous as the stars of heaven. Love the Lord your God and keep His charge, His statutes and His commandments always. Know this day, for I speak not with your children who have not known or seen the chastening of the Lord your God, His greatness, His mighty hand and His outstretched arm, His signs and His works which He did in Egypt against Pharaoh the king of Egypt and all his land, what He did to the army of Egypt, to its horses and chariots, when He made the waters of the Red Sea overflow them as they pursued you, and the Lord destroyed them to this day, and what He did for you in the wilderness until you came to this place, and what He did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab the son of Reuben, whom the earth opened its mouth and swallowed, with their households, their tents, and everything that belonged to them, in the midst of all Israel. But your eyes have seen all the great works of the Lord which He did. Keep, therefore, all the commandments which the Lord commands you today, that you may be strong, enter and possess the land to which you go over, and that you may prolong your days in the land which the Lord swore to your fathers to give them and their descendants after them." And its completion will come, God willing, the Exalted, at

﴿And We certainly settled the Children of Israel in a good settlement﴾ [Yunus: 93]. (p-100) Among its ambiguous (mutashabih) expressions is His saying "the mouth of God" and "the finger of God." The first, because it is not permissible to apply it literally in our law, is interpreted as speech, and the second as power.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 155:

When He, glory be to Him, had finished mentioning the promise of the appointed time, the purpose of which was the striving of Kalim (the one who spoke with Allah), peace be upon him, in guiding them to the path of Allah, and had mentioned their striving in misguiding themselves from the way through taking the calf, and the conclusion of that was what appeared from Musa, peace be upon him, of compassion for his brother and then for all the people by taking the tablets upon finishing, out of the anger required for Allah, He returned the speech to mention something Musa did at the appointed time, intended for their preservation on the path of Allah by transferring them, through his sharing with them in hearing the speech of Allah, from knowledge of certainty (ʿilm al-yaqin) to the eye of certainty (ʿayn al-yaqin), rather to the truth of certainty (haqq al-yaqin), out of compassion for them and mercy toward them, so that their report of what they saw would confirm what he reported, and that would be a cause of their protection from the like of what they fell into of worshipping the calf. Yet despite that, disobedience came from them by asking for what was not fitting for them of seeing, in a manner of obstinacy. So He said: ﴿And Musa chose﴾, i.e., he exerted effort in taking the choice, ﴿from his people﴾; then he substituted from them his saying: ﴿seventy men﴾, indicating that whoever is other than them is nothing, and the name "people" does not apply to them in the sense he intended. This is similar to what the Prophet ﷺ said, as recorded by al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both: "People are like a hundred camels, among which you hardly find a riding camel." Then he mentioned the reason for the choosing, saying: ﴿for Our appointed time﴾, i.e., he chose only one who he saw was fit for what We desire of Our greatness at the time We appointed for him, and he brought them near to the Presence of address (al-hadrah al-khitabiyyah) on the mountain, he and Harun, peace be upon them both, and he appointed Yusha' ibn Nun, peace be upon him, as successor over the Children of Israel. All of that was by Allah's command to him. And in this speech there is a conjunction with His saying: ﴿And We appointed Musa thirty nights﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 142], so the appointed time would be the first one, and this is the apparent meaning of the Torah, as its explanation passed in al-Baqarah. It is also permissible that it be a conjunction with His saying: ﴿And the people of Musa took﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 148], or with His saying: ﴿took up the tablets﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 154], and then this appointed time would be other than the first appointed time. This is supported by what is transmitted, that Harun, peace be upon him, was with them. And it seems that when they heard the speech of Allah, some of them asked to see Him, making it a condition for their faith, so they said: ﴿We will not believe you until we see Allah openly﴾ [al-Baqarah: 55], as the twelve chiefs did when he sent them to spy out the condition of the tyrants, and most of them broke their word, so the quake seized them and they died. Musa, peace be upon him, feared that the Children of Israel would accuse him of their deaths, as a single soul. ﴿So when the quake seized them﴾, i.e., seized them by overpowering force, ﴿the quake﴾, i.e., that which was caused by the thunderbolt that preceded in al-Baqarah, so their hearts were shaken and it caused them to die. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that these were other than the seventy who said: ﴿Show us Allah openly, so the thunderbolt seized them﴾ [al-Nisa': 153], and that those were before these. The apparent cause of the quake is what they saw when hearing the speech of the majesty of Allah and the greatness of His awe, from the cloud that covered the mountain, and the smoke, the lightning, the sounds of the horns, and other things, to the extent that the quake, which is a trembling, nearly separated their joints from one another. ﴿He said﴾, i.e., Musa, in supplication to his Lord, glory be to Him: ﴿My Lord﴾, i.e., O You who have done good to me, ﴿If You had willed, You would have destroyed them﴾, i.e., caused them to die.

Since the destruction of them was not all-encompassing of the past, he introduced the preposition, saying: ﴿before and me﴾, i.e., Your power over me and over them before we drew near to this holy Presence, while we were in the presence of our people, is like Your power over us when You honor us with it, and You have let down upon us the hem of Your pardon and lavished upon us Your blessing while we were not in the Presence, and You did not destroy us. So Your bounty toward us while we are in the Presence of holiness and the carpet of nearness and intimacy is more fitting.

Then, since the situation called for saying: "Have you not seen what they dared against?", and it was as if he had said: "Only some of them, foolish ones, said that", he indicated that by his saying, seeking compassion: ﴿Will You destroy us﴾. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that their quake was because they had not forbidden the worship of the calf, even though they had not been pleased with it. And it seems that Musa, peace be upon him, expressed himself with this phrase, which requires the destruction of all, because he considered that just as He destroyed these, He might destroy others for another shortcoming connected to that, such as not waging jihad, for example, until destruction encompasses them all: ﴿for what the foolish among us did﴾. So it was as if he, ﷺ, accepted that if the pardon did not include them, the pardon be specified for those who had not sinned in deed, and that He pardon those who fell short by silence. And on the assumption that the appointed time was other than the first, it is permissible that it was after their taking the calf, as passed earlier from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both. Then Musa, peace be upon him, feared that their destruction would be a trial for the Children of Israel and a cause of their disbelief, just as his delay from them by adding ten days to the thirty in the first appointed time was a cause of their taking the calf. It is then permissible that by the deed of the foolish is meant the taking of the calf, and this is supported by the expression of "deed" rather than "saying," and what has been transmitted from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, has already passed.

Since his saying this may have implied his approval of the destruction of the wrongdoers, he said, alluding to asking for pardon for all: ﴿It is only Your trial﴾, i.e., Your testing and examination, ﴿by which You lead astray whom You will﴾, i.e., You manifest in the world of witnessing those whose misguidance was already known to You in the unseen world, ﴿and guide whom You will﴾, i.e., You manifest what is in Your knowledge of that.

Since he established that all is in His hand, he resumed his request that He do for them what is best, saying: ﴿You are﴾ [i.e., You alone] ﴿our Protector﴾, i.e., we believe that none other than You can accomplish our benefits, and You have no benefit or harm from either of the two matters; rather all is in relation to You on one equal footing, and we are certain that Your acts are not caused by purposes. Your pardon of us benefits us, and Your vengeance upon us harms us. We are in Your presence, having cut ourselves off to You and unloaded the baggage of our need before You.

Since he established that He is the Doer of what He wills, and that there is no protector for them other than Him, and since it is the nature of a protector to bring benefit and repel harm, he based on His being the sole Protector his saying, beginning with the repelling of harm: ﴿So forgive us﴾, i.e., erase our sins, ﴿and have mercy upon us﴾, i.e., raise us up. Since the implied sense was: "So You are the best of the merciful," he joined to it his saying: ﴿And You are the best of the forgivers﴾, i.e., because others forgive sin for praise or reward, or to avoid a base attribute, such as rancor and the like, while You are exalted above that.

It is as if he had kindly pardoned them, so he said, linking to his request in it: ﴿And prescribe for us﴾, that is, during the span of Your giving us life, ﴿in this world﴾, that is, the present and lowly world, ﴿good﴾, that is, a contented and pure life, ﴿and in﴾ the life ﴿to come﴾, that is, likewise. Then he gave the reason for that in his saying: ﴿Indeed we have turned back (hudna) to You﴾, that is, we have repented, ﴿to You﴾, that is, from what is not befitting Your presence, just as You commanded us to report what might befall us of error by hastening to repentance. So he began by mentioning the might of Lordship (rububiyyah) and followed it with the humility of servanthood (ubudiyyah), and these two are the strongest causes of happiness. This is an instruction to them, a teaching, a warning against the like of what they fell into, and an urging towards submission. As their sin was boldly speaking of what is not befitting Him, glorified be He, namely seeking the vision, he expressed it with this word, or with what indicates its meaning, as an alert to them that their name indicates repentance, returning to the truth, arriving at righteousness, gentleness, softness of voice, humbleness in speech, and silence about what is not befitting. And Yahudha (Judah), whose name was taken from that, was named and attributed to it only as an omen for them, so that they would hasten to repentance.

And since his words (peace be upon him) contained [an denial] of destroying the obedient for the sin of the disobedient, even though that was only in the manner of seeking compassion and pleading, while knowing that it is His justice, and that He may do whatever He wills, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿If You had willed, You would have destroyed them before, and me﴾ [al-A'raf: 155], He, glorified be He, resumed informing about the answer to his words in a manner that alerts the masses that He has absolute disposal, by His saying: (p-105) ﴿He said: My punishment﴾, that is, My vengeance, which removes all sweetness from whoever it befalls, ﴿I afflict with it﴾, that is, in this world and the Hereafter, ﴿whom I will﴾, that is, whether he has sinned or not, ﴿and My mercy﴾, that is, My bounty and My honour.

And since bringing into existence is part of mercy, for it is better than non-existence, it is a kindness in general. He said: ﴿encompasses all things﴾, that is, this is its nature and attribute in reality, even if [things] reach whatever evils they may reach. This is the meaning of the hadith of Abu Hurayrah in the Sahih (the authentic collection): "Indeed My mercy precedes (in another narration: overcomes) My wrath." Whether we say that "precedence" means "overcoming," or we say it is on its own basis, the first is because the scope of mercy is greater, since everything to which wrath attaches, mercy also attaches to it by bringing it into existence and bestowing provision upon it, but not the reverse, such as dumb animals, inanimate objects, the people of happiness among the believers, the angels, the houris, and others of the hosts of God that cannot be counted. And since He made known that His mercy is vast and His power all-encompassing, and that this widens hope, he based on that his saying, mentioning the condition for completing that mercy, as a warning to whoever is lax in attaining that condition: ﴿So I will prescribe it﴾, that is, I specify its continuance by a promise that admits no breach, for the sake of My full power over what I will, its matter being decreed by writing, ﴿for those who fear (yattaqun)﴾, that is, this quality which moves them to every good is found in them, and it does not impair His capacity that I prevent its continuance after bringing it into existence from others, for if all of them entered it forever, it would not be too narrow for them. It is in itself vast, but I do what I will.

(p-106) And since He mentioned their looking to the Creator by refraining from what He forbade and complying with what He commanded, He followed it with their looking to creation, saying: ﴿and who give the zakat﴾. Perhaps He singled it out because its obligation was in this appointed time, as previously mentioned in al-Baqarah, and because it is a trust between the creatures and the Creator, just as the attributes of the Prophet (ﷺ) which He wrote for them, and made the acceptance of their deeds conditional upon following him, are likewise. Then he generalized by mentioning the fruit of taqwa, saying, excluding whoever has these two qualities in general but not in full generality: ﴿And those who in Our signs﴾, that is, all of them, ﴿believe﴾, that is, they affirm with the heart, acknowledge with the tongue, and act in accordance with that affirmation with the limbs, so they do not disbelieve in some and believe in others.

[Since the Jews sometimes claimed this out of obstinacy, and to make the matter fully clear, He said]: ﴿Those who follow﴾, meaning with the utmost of their effort, ﴿the Messenger﴾. Since this description alone does not specify the intended person, nor explicitly state that he is a messenger from God, nor that he is human, He said: ﴿the Prophet﴾, meaning the one to whom revelation comes from God. He began with the most noble attribute, then mentioned what distinguishes him: that he is sent by God and is one of the children of Adam, not one of the angels.

Since the intended meaning was still not complete, He said, explaining the greatest of the miracles, namely that his knowledge came without a human teacher: ﴿the unlettered﴾, meaning the one who, despite that all-encompassing knowledge, is in the state of the unlettered. The nation of the Arabs neither writes nor reads, and he did not mix with the scholars to be taught by them, but rather to teach them. The description thus fits the one described, together with an indication of the exalted qualities and an arousal of longing for the one described. [He did not use a conjunction, lest it give the impression of enumerating the described person.] The meaning is: I will not forgive anyone of the Children of Israel or of others, unless he follows Muhammad (ﷺ). This following is sometimes only in potential, for those whose death preceded his time; and sometimes the potential becomes actual, for those who lived to the time of his call. Whoever God knows will not follow him when he reaches him, God will not forgive him, even if he performs all other acts of obedience. He made him known to them by all his distinguishing features, so that no doubt would reach them when he came and no pretext would be offered concerning his matter. For this reason He followed it with: ﴿whom they find﴾, meaning the scholars of the Children of Israel. Since the listener's longing was intensified by the mention of finding, He said: ﴿written﴾. Then He brought the matter closer with: ﴿with them﴾. Then He explained that it is something in which there is no doubt, with: ﴿in the Torah and the Gospel﴾, meaning the two books that they know are from God by their clear description, as was explained earlier in the discussion of their pretexts concerning altering them in al-Baqarah, [﴿And when Abraham was tested by his Lord﴾ (2:124)], and in Āl ʿImrān at: [﴿Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah﴾ (3:33)], and in al-Nisāʾ at: [﴿And they did not kill him, with certainty﴾ (4:157)]. Also in the Torah, among such texts, in the eleventh chapter of the Fifth Book (Deuteronomy): "When you enter the land which the Lord your God gives you, do not do like the abominations of those nations, and let there be found among you none who seeks the teaching of the diviners," then he said: "For these nations whose land you will inherit used to obey the diviners and the astrologers; but as for you, the Lord your God does not give you thus; rather He will raise up for you a prophet from among your brethren like me, so obey that prophet, as you asked of the Lord your God at Horeb on the day of the assembly, and you said: 'Let us not hear the voice of the Lord our God, nor see this great fire, lest we die.' The Lord said: 'They have spoken well. I will raise up for them a prophet from among their brethren like you; I will put My words in his mouth, and he will tell them whatever I command him. Whoever does not heed the words of that prophet who speaks in My name, I will require it of him and of his tribe.'" End of quotation. Thus I saw it translated in some copies of the Torah. Then I saw that Samawʾal ibn Yahya al-Maghribi translated it in his book in which he mentioned the cause of his conversion to Islam, and he was among the great scholars of theirs, indeed among the foremost of their scholars, saying: "A prophet I will raise up for them from among the midst of their brethren, like you; to him let them believe." End of quotation. He means that this prophet is Muhammad (ﷺ), because he is from the children of Ishmael, brother of Isaac, and he brought an independent law that has no connection with the law before it nor dependence upon it. In the expression there are two words: "like" and "brethren." The real sense of "brother" is the son of one of the two parents, and this cannot apply to any of their prophets. The nearest metaphor to its real sense is to take it as the brother of the father, who is Ishmael, peace be upon him. The usual usage in such cases, if one of them is intended, is to say "from among themselves," not "from among their brethren." The real sense of "like" is a counterpart in the most distinctive attributes. The most distinctive attributes of Moses, peace be upon him, are messengership and the Book with an independent law, and no one came among them after him who has this attribute; for Jesus, peace be upon him, abrogated from the law of Moses, peace be upon him, only some rulings. Even if one claims that he abrogated in general, and that this is granted, the intention cannot be attained by this text, for two reasons. The first is that he is not from their men except through his mother; so the correct wording concerning him would be "from among the sons of their sisters," the plural of sister. And if the forefathers of his mother are intended, the metaphor concerning them is further than the metaphor concerning the children of Ishmael, for the reason mentioned earlier; and one does not move to the more distant meaning except with an indication that turns away from the nearer one. And God knows best.

Samawʾal ibn Yahya, one of their rabbis (ḥibr, scholar), said in the cause of his conversion: The Jews say that this good news was revealed concerning Samawʾal, one of their prophets who came after Moses, because he was like Moses, peace be upon him, in that he was from the tribe of Levi. He said: He saw Samawʾal, peace be upon him, in a dream, and he handed him a book, in which he found this good news. So he said to him: "Congratulations to you, O prophet of God, for what God has singled you out with!" Then he looked at him angrily and said: "Did God intend this for me, O fool! The geometric proofs have not benefited you then!" I said: "O prophet of God! Then who did God intend by this?" He said: "The one He intended in His saying: Hūfīʿ Mīhār Fārān," and its interpretation is an indication of a prophethood promised to descend upon the mountains of Fārān. So I knew that He means the Chosen One (ﷺ), because he was sent from the mountains of Fārān, which are the mountains of Makkah. Then he said: "Did you not know that God did not send me to abrogate anything of the Torah, but I was sent to remind them of it, to revive its laws, and to deliver them from the people of Philistia?" I said: "Yes, O prophet of God!" He said: "Then what need have they that their Lord should command them to follow one who has not abrogated their religion and has not changed their law? Did you see them needing to be commanded to accept the prophethood of Daniel, or Jeremiah, or Ezekiel?" I said: "No, by my life!" So he took the book from my hand and departed angrily. I was terrified by his anger, was rebuked by his admonition, and I awoke in alarm.

He said in his book: The ultimate aim in refuting the Christians and the Jews is that God applies the term brethren to people other than the Children of Israel, as He said concerning the children of Esau, son of Isaac, peace be upon him, in the first part of the Fifth Book, whose meaning is: "You are passing through the borders of your brethren, the children of Esau." So if the children of Esau are brethren of the Children of Israel, because Esau and Israel were the two sons of Isaac, then likewise the children of Ishmael are brethren of all the sons of Abraham, peace be upon them. He said: In the third part of the first book of the Torah, in the mention of the good news to Abraham, peace be upon him, is the following, whose meaning is: "As for Ishmael, I have heard your prayer. Behold, I have blessed him, and will make him fruitful and multiply him exceedingly, exceedingly." He said: "Exceedingly, exceedingly" in the Hebrew language is interpreted as "mād mād." If we count the letters of these two words by the abjad reckoning (ḥisāb al-jummal, the system of assigning numerical values to letters), they come to ninety-two, and that is the numerical value of the letters of the name Muhammad (ﷺ). That is, it is fixed that this is what is meant by them, because they are in the good news of the multiplication of Ishmael, peace be upon him, and among his descendants there is none whom God multiplied by it except Muhammad (ﷺ), and no other whose name totals this number. He said: This was placed in this location as a riddle, because if it had been stated explicitly, the Jews would have altered it or removed it from the Torah, as they did with other things. End of quotation.

At the end of the sections of the Torah: Moses, the servant of God, prayed for the Children of Israel before his death, saying: "Our Lord came from Sinai, and shone forth for us from Mount Seir, and appeared to us from the mountain—and in one copy: the mountains—of Fārān, with Him the myriads of the holy ones at His right hand. He gave them and endeared them to the peoples, and blessed all His holy ones, and [they] follow your traces and transmit your words." And in another copy, instead of: "with Him the myriads of the holy ones," to the end: "and He came from the myriads of holiness with the law of His light from His right hand for them, and He also chose a people; all His elect are in your obedience, and they will follow your traces, and will transmit your words." End of quotation.

Therefore, the one who appeared from the mountains of Paran is Muhammad (ﷺ), because they acknowledge that it is Mecca. With him are groups of the pure (ruba'at), and his community has been made beloved to the nations, because each of the two groups of the People of the Book prefers its own community over the other. No one has accepted all of the words of Moses (peace be upon him) and followed all of his traces in his good tidings of one who would come after the others.

As for the Gospel, its good tidings are more numerous, and many of them have already been mentioned. They are almost explicit in Surat al-Nisa' concerning the story of his (peace be upon him) being raised up (to heaven). (p-112) Among what is in it also is what is in the Gospel of Matthew and elsewhere, and most of the context concerns him: "Many who are first will become last, and the last will become first. The kingdom of the heavens is like a man, a master of a house, who went out early in the morning to hire laborers for his vineyard. He agreed with the laborers on a denarius a day and sent them into his vineyard. Then he went out at the third hour and saw others standing idle in the marketplace, and he said to them, 'Go you also into my vineyard, and I will give you what is right.' So they went. He went out again at the sixth and the ninth hour and did likewise. He went out at the eleventh hour and found others standing, and he said to them, 'Why do you stand here all day idle?' They said to him, 'Because no one has hired us.' He said to them, 'Go you also into the vineyard, and you will receive what is right.' When evening came, the lord of the vineyard said to his steward, 'Call the laborers and give them their wages, beginning with the last and ending with the first.' Those hired at the eleventh hour came and each received a denarius. When the first came, they supposed they would receive more, but each of them also received a denarius. And when they received it, they murmured against the master of the house, saying, 'These last have worked one hour, and you have made them equal to us, who have borne the burden of the day and its heat!' He answered one of them, 'Friend, I do not wrong you. Did you not agree with me on a denarius? Take what is yours and go. I wish to give this last one the same as you. Is it not lawful for me to do what I wish with my own money? Or is your eye evil because I am good?' So the last will be first, and the first last, for many are called but few are chosen."

(p-113) And he said: "He entered the Temple, and the chief priests and elders of the people came to him and said to him, while he was teaching, 'By what authority do you do these things? And who gave you this authority?' Jesus answered and said to them, 'I will ask you one question, and if you tell me, I will tell you by what authority I do these things. The baptism of John, from where was it? From heaven or from men?' They reasoned among themselves, saying, 'If we say, From heaven, he will say to us, Why did you not believe him? But if we say, From men, we fear the crowd.' Luke said: 'If we say, From men, all the people will stone us, for they are certain that John is a prophet.' Matthew said: 'Because John was to them like a prophet.' Mark said: 'Because all of them were saying that John is a prophet.' Matthew said: 'They answered, We do not know. He said, Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.' Mark said: 'He began to speak to them in parables, saying:' Matthew said: 'What do you think of a man who had two sons? He came to the first and said, Son, go today and work in the vineyard. He answered and said, I will not. But afterward he regretted and went. He came to the second and said the same. He answered, Yes, Lord, I go, but he did not go. Which of the two did the will of the father?' They said to him, 'The first.' Jesus said to them, 'Truly I say to you, the tax collectors and the prostitutes go into the kingdom of God before you. John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him, but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him. And you, when you saw that, did not even repent afterward so as to believe him.' Hear another parable: There was a householder who planted a vineyard, put a hedge around it, dug a winepress in it, built a tower, and leased it to tenants, and went away (Luke said: 'for a long time'). When the season of the fruits drew near, he sent his servants to the tenants to receive its fruit. The tenants seized his servants, beat some, killed some, and stoned some. He sent again other servants, more than the first, and they did the same to them. At last he sent to them his son, saying, 'Perhaps they will respect my son.' When the tenants saw the son, they said, 'This is the heir; come, let us kill him and take his inheritance.' They seized him, cast him out of the vineyard, and killed him. When the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those tenants?' They said to him, 'He will destroy those wicked men and lease the vineyard to other tenants who will give him the fruit in its season.' Jesus said to them, 'Have you never read in the Scriptures: The stone which the builders rejected has become the cornerstone; this was from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes? Therefore I say to you, the kingdom of God will be taken from you and given to a nation producing its fruits. Whoever falls on this stone will be broken, and whoever it falls on will be crushed.' When the chief priests and the Pharisees heard his parables, they knew that he was speaking about them. They sought to arrest him, but they feared the crowds, because he was to them like a prophet." He also said: "The kingdom of heaven is like a king who made a wedding feast for his son, and sent his servants to call those who were invited to the wedding, but they would not come. Again he sent other servants and said, 'Tell those invited: Behold, my dinner is prepared, my oxen and fattened animals are slaughtered, and everything is ready; come to the wedding.' But they were careless (p-115) and went away: one to his field, another to his business. The rest seized his servants, insulted them, and killed them. When the king heard, he was angry, sent his troops, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city. Then he said to his servants, 'The wedding is ready, but those invited were not worthy. Go to the crossroads, and whomever you find, invite to the wedding.' Those servants went out into the roads and gathered all whom they found, both evil and good, and the wedding hall was filled with guests. When the king came in to look at the guests, he saw there a man who did not have on a wedding garment. [He said, 'Friend, how did you come in here without a wedding garment?'] But he was silent. Then the king said to the attendants, 'Bind his hands and feet and cast him into the outer darkness; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.' Many are called, but few are chosen." Luke's version of this is: "A man made a great banquet and invited many, and he sent his servant to say to those invited, 'Come, for everything is now ready.' But they all began to make excuses. The first said, 'I have bought a field, and I must go out and see it; please excuse me.' Another said, 'I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to test them; please excuse me.' Another said, 'I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.' The servant came and informed his master. Then the master of the house was angry and said to his servant, 'Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in the poor, the crippled, the blind, and the lame. Go out to the roads and the hedges, and compel them to come in, so that my house may be filled; for I tell you, none of those who were invited will taste my supper.'"

And John said: "Truly I say to you, whoever does not enter the sheepfold by the door, but climbs in some other way, is a thief. He who enters by the door is the shepherd of the sheep, and the gatekeeper opens to him, and the sheep hear his voice, and his own sheep follow him because they know his voice. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep. But the other, who is not a shepherd and to whom the sheep do not belong, when he sees the wolf coming, leaves the sheep and flees, and the wolf snatches and scatters the sheep. The hireling flees because he is a hireling and does not care for the sheep. I am the good shepherd, and I have other sheep that are not of this fold; I must bring them also, and there will be one flock and one shepherd." Then a division arose again among the Jews because of these words. Many of them said, "He has a demon and is mad; why do you listen to him?" Others said, "These are not the words of a madman."

In the beginning of the Sirat Ibn Hisham, Ibn Ishaq said: (p-117) "What has reached me of what Jesus son of Mary put in the Gospel, from what came to him from God, concerning the attributes of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), among what was preserved, is that Yahnas the disciple, when he copied the Gospel for them, said: 'Whoever hates me hates the Lord. Had I not done among them works which no one before me has done, they would have had no sin; but now they have grown proud and think they are honoring me and also the Lord. But it must be that the word in the Law be fulfilled: They hated me without cause' — that is, in vain. 'But when the Munhamna comes, whom God will send to you from the Lord, the Spirit of Holiness, who proceeds from the Lord, he will bear witness concerning me, and you also, because you have been with me from the beginning. I have told you this so that you will not doubt.'" Al-Munhamna in Syriac is Muhammad, and in Greek it is the Paraclete. End of quotation.

When God, glory be to Him, indicated him (ﷺ) by his attributes within himself and in the divine books, He indicated him by his law, saying: ﴿He enjoins on them what is right﴾, that is, everything they recognize from the Torah and the Gospel, and what they recognize in them, namely that he would abrogate their law and come from God with what is mentioned. ﴿And forbids them what is wrong﴾, that is, everything they disapprove of in them. Thus his messengership is established, for since he was unlettered and did not know the right and the wrong in them, except by being truthful about the Knower of the unseen. Then, (p-118) after the establishment of his messengership, He began to explain to them what is in his message of favor to them, in lightening what they had borne as the burden of its prohibition. They had continued to disobey God by violating His sacred limits and turning away from its consequences. So He said: ﴿And He makes lawful for them the good things﴾, that is, those which had been forbidden to them as a punishment, such as fats; ﴿and makes unlawful for them﴾ [and He expressed with the plural form, indicating that the bad is more numerous than the good in every aquatic thing, so He said] ﴿the bad things﴾, that is, everything the sound nature finds repugnant or that leads to corruption, such as wine, which leads to intoxication, and bribery, which leads to the Fire after shameful disgrace. ﴿And relieves them of their burden﴾, that is, the load which had been laid upon them, making them like one imprisoned and prevented from movement by its weight. ﴿And the shackles which were upon them﴾, that is, all the burdens they had carried which, because of their weight and the souls' aversion to them, were like a shackle binding the hand to the neck and removing strength. ﴿So those who believe in him﴾, that is, they created by means of him safety from denying any of God's signs. ﴿And honor him﴾, that is, they restrained him from everyone who wished him harm, and they strengthened his hand with a great strengthening against everyone who plotted against him. In the Qamus (the dictionary) it is said: "Ta'zir is a beating below the prescribed limit, or it is the most severe beating; and tafkhim and ta'zim are its opposites; and iana (aid) is like 'azr, taqwiyah (strengthening), and nasr (support)." End of quotation.

Abd al-Haqq said: "Al-'Azr is prevention. You say, 'I restrained so-and-so from such-and-such,' that is, I prevented him." End of quotation. So the whole root revolves around this meaning, and the beating is clearly in it for honoring, and what is similar in meaning is preventing whoever plots against him. ﴿And support him﴾, that is, they strengthened him (p-119) and suppressed his opponents. ﴿And follow the light﴾, that is, the revelation from the Qur'an and the Sunnah, ﴿which was sent down with him﴾, that is, its sending down accompanied his sending. It was called light because it makes the one who follows it, by clarifying the path of truth, like one walking in the light of day. ﴿Those are the ones who are successful﴾, that is, specifically, the ones who prosper, the ones who attain every hoped-for thing.

When the verses followed one another, and the narratives about Musa (peace be upon him), with the explanation of his great virtues and his mighty achievements, were prolonged, this may have led some souls to think that he was the highest of the messengers in rank and the greatest of them in station. So God, glory be to Him, arranged these verses in this order, in which He makes clear that the highest of them in degree and the purest of them in virtues is the one whom He singled out with His mercy, among those of His creatures who believe in him, in power or in action. He placed this within the account of the Children of Israel, out of concern for it and to hasten it, along with what will be mentioned that shows his excellence and clarifies his perfection through his story with his people at the beginning, middle and end of his affair, in the surahs al-Anfal and Bara'ah in their entirety.

Mention of some of the burdens that were upon them, which would have been lifted from them had they entered Islam through the blessing of his (ﷺ), beyond what I have already noted at the end of al-Baqarah at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Our Lord, do not lay upon us a burden like that which You laid upon those before us﴾ [al-Baqarah: 286], and in al-Ma'idah at His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Let the people of the Injil judge by what God has revealed in it﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 47]. In the second book of the Torah (the Pentateuch), it says: [And] the Lord said to Musa: Take fragrant spices, until he said: and let it be a compound of incense, pure and holy; grind it, pound it, and burn some of it before the Ark of the Testimony in the Tent of Meeting, where I will meet with you there; it shall be most holy for you. Whoever makes a like incense to smell it, that man shall be cut off from his people. And in the third book he said: Then the Lord spoke to Musa, saying to him: Speak to Harun and his sons and to all the congregation of the children of Israel, and say to them: This is what the Lord has commanded: any man of the house of Israel who slaughters an ox, a lamb or a goat in the camp, or who slaughters it outside the camp, and does not bring it to the door of the Tent of Meeting to offer it to the Lord, that man shall be cut off from among his people, as one who sheds blood, and he shall be guilty of bloodshed. And the Lord spoke to Musa, saying: Speak to Harun, and say to him: Whoever of your descendants throughout their generations has a blemish, let him not approach to offer the bread of his God. For any man who has a blemish shall not approach: a man who is blind or lame, who has a flat nose or something superfluous, or a man who has a broken foot or a broken hand, or a hunchback, or a dwarf, or a man with a defect in his eye, or with scurvy or eczema, or who has damaged testicles. No man of the descendants of Aharon the priest who has a blemish shall come near to offer the offerings of the Lord made by fire; he has a blemish, so he shall not approach to offer the bread of his God. And in the fourth book, which is among the proofs that the Torah was not revealed all at once: And the Lord spoke to Musa in the wilderness of Sinai in the second year after they came out of the land of Egypt, in the first month, saying: Let the children of Israel keep the Passover at its appointed season. On the fourteenth day of this month, at twilight, you shall keep it at its appointed season, until he said: So they kept the Passover, and those men who were defiled by a dead body could not keep the Passover on that day. They approached Musa and Harun on that day, and those men said to him: We are defiled by a dead body; why are we kept from presenting the offering of the Lord at its appointed time among the children of Israel? Musa said to them: Stand still, and I will hear what the Lord will command concerning you. And the Lord spoke to Musa, saying: Speak to the children of Israel, saying: If any man of you or of your descendants is defiled by a dead body, or is on a distant journey, he may still keep the Passover to the Lord. On the fourteenth day of the second month at twilight they shall keep it; they shall eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs. And the man who is clean and is not on a journey, and yet fails to keep the Passover, that person shall be cut off from his people, because he did not present the offering of the Lord at its appointed time; that man shall bear his sin. And before that he said: And the Lord spoke to Musa, saying to him: Command the children of Israel that they put out of the camp everyone who has a leprous disease, or a discharge, and whoever is unclean through contact with the dead, both male and female, you shall put them outside the camp, that they may not defile their camp, where I dwell among them. Then he mentioned the man whose wife goes astray and is unfaithful to him: he shall bring her to the priest and he shall make her stand before the Lord, and he shall pronounce a curse upon her; when he has written it, he shall take holy water in an earthen vessel and put into it some of the dust that is on the floor of the tabernacle, and he shall give her the water to drink. If she has defiled herself, her belly shall swell and her thigh shall rot, and she shall become a curse among her people; and if she has not defiled herself, she shall be cleansed and bear a male child. Then he commanded them to slaughter a cow and burn it until it becomes ashes, and the priest who slaughtered it shall wash his garments and his hands. Whoever touches a dead person shall be unclean for seven days, and he shall be sprinkled with that water on the third day and on the seventh day, and he shall be clean; if he is not sprinkled in this way, he shall not be clean. Whoever touches a dead person and does not sprinkle himself with that water has defiled the tabernacle of the Lord, and that person shall be cut off from Israel, because the water of purification was not sprinkled on him; he is unclean, and his uncleanness remains upon him. And this is the law when a man dies in the tent: all who come into the tent and all who are in the tent shall be unclean seven days, and every open vessel that has no covering on it is unclean, and whoever touches a corpse, or a bone of a man, or a grave, shall be unclean seven days. For the unclean they shall take some of the ashes of the burnt sin offering and running water shall be added to it in a vessel, and a clean person shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it on the tent, on all the vessels, and on the persons who were there, and on the one who touched a bone or a slain person or a grave. The clean person shall sprinkle the unclean on the third day and on the seventh day, and on the seventh day he shall purify him; and he shall wash his clothes and bathe in water, and at evening he shall be clean. Whoever is unclean and does not purify himself, that person shall be cut off from the midst of the assembly, because he has defiled the sanctuary of the Lord; the water of purification has not been sprinkled on him, he is unclean. And whoever sprinkles the water of purification shall wash his clothes, and whoever touches the water of purification shall be unclean until evening, and whoever touches anything the unclean person touched shall be unclean until evening; then he said: Then the Lord spoke to Musa and said to him: Command the children of Israel and say to them: My offering, my food for my offerings made by fire, a pleasing aroma to me, you shall take care to offer to me at its appointed time. Then he mentioned to him much about the matter of offerings, then he mentioned their times: the Sabbath day and the new moons. Then he said: On the fourteenth day of the first month at twilight is the Passover of the Lord; and on the fifteenth day of this month is a feast; for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread. On the first day you shall have a holy convocation; you shall do no ordinary work. On the seventh day there shall be a holy convocation; you shall do no ordinary work. On the first day of the seventh month shall be a holy convocation; you shall do no ordinary work; it is a day of blowing trumpets for you. And you shall offer burnt offerings, and he described them and likewise the other days. Then he said: Thus you shall do on the first day of every month. In the tenth day of the seventh month you shall have a holy convocation; you shall afflict yourselves; you shall do no work. And on the fifteenth day of this seventh month there shall be a feast of booths for seven days to the Lord. On the first day there shall be a holy convocation; you shall do no ordinary work. Then he said: On the eighth day you shall have a holy convocation and present an offering made by fire to the Lord; it is a solemn assembly; you shall do no ordinary work. And he went on at great length about these matters, the details of their observance being, apart from knowledge of them, the greatest hardship. Then he said: You shall offer to the Lord at your feasts, apart from your vows and your freewill offerings which you offer to the Lord. Then he said, addressing the warriors in Midian: And you shall camp outside the camp for seven days; whoever has killed a person or touched a corpse shall be sprinkled with the water of purification on the third and seventh day. He commanded them about other burdens, then he said: And you shall purify yourselves with water on the seventh day, and after that you shall come into the camp. Then he said in the fifth book: These are the statutes and judgments which you must observe in the land which the Lord your God gives you as an inheritance, all the days that you live. You shall destroy all the places where the nations you dispossess served their gods, on the high mountains and on the hills and under every green tree; you shall break down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, and burn their Asherah poles with fire; you shall cut down the carved images of their gods and destroy their names from that place. You shall not worship the Lord your God in such ways; but to the place which the Lord your God chooses from among all your tribes to put His name there, you shall seek His dwelling, and there you shall go, and there you shall bring your burnt offerings and your sacrifices. Eat there before the Lord your God, you and your households, rejoicing in all that you undertake; you shall not do as we are doing here today, every man doing what is right in his own eyes, before you have come to the rest and the inheritance. Then he said: Take heed that you do not offer your burnt offerings in every place that you see, but in the place which the Lord chooses in one of your tribes, there you shall offer your burnt offerings. Then he said: When you build a new house, you shall make a parapet for your roof, so that you do not bring the guilt of blood upon your house if anyone falls from it. You shall not sow your vineyard with two kinds of seed, lest the whole yield be defiled. You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey together. You shall not wear a garment of wool and linen woven together. You shall make tassels on the four corners of the cloak with which you cover yourself. Then he said: If a man takes a wife and goes in to her and then dislikes her, and accuses her of misconduct and brings a bad name upon her, saying: I took this woman, and when I came near her I did not find in her evidence of virginity; then the father of the young woman and her mother shall take and bring out the evidence of her virginity to the elders of the city at the gate; and the father of the young woman shall say to the elders: I gave my daughter to this man as wife, and he dislikes her; now he has accused her of misconduct; but if she was a virgin, the man shall pay the father fifty shekels of silver, and she shall be his wife; because he has violated a virgin of Israel, he shall not be permitted to divorce her all his days.

And no one born of an illicit union shall enter the assembly of the Lord; even to the tenth generation none of his descendants shall enter the assembly of the Lord. No Ammonite or Moabite shall enter the assembly of the Lord; even to the tenth generation none of their descendants shall enter the assembly of the Lord forever; because they did not meet you with bread and water on the way when you came out of Egypt, and because they hired against you Bil'am the son of Be'or from Pethor of Aram Naharaim, to curse you. But the Lord your God would not listen to Bil'am; instead the Lord your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, because the Lord your God loves you. You shall not seek their peace or their prosperity all your days forever. You shall not abhor an Edomite, for he is your brother; you shall not abhor an Egyptian, because you were a sojourner in his land. And if there is a man among you who is unclean because of a nocturnal emission, he shall go outside the camp and shall not come inside the camp; but when evening comes he shall bathe himself in water, and when the sun sets he may come into the camp. You shall have a place outside the camp where you go to relieve yourselves; with your tools you shall dig a hole and cover up your excrement. Because the Lord your God walks in the midst of your camp, to deliver you and to give up your enemies before you; therefore your camp must be holy, so that He may not see anything indecent among you and turn away from you. Then he said: If two brothers dwell together and one of them dies and has no son, the wife of the dead shall not be married outside the family to a stranger; her husband's brother shall go in to her and take her as his wife and perform the duty of a husband's brother to her; and the first son she bears shall succeed to the name of his dead brother, so that his name will not be blotted out of Israel. But if the man does not wish to take his brother's wife, then his brother's wife shall go up to the gate to the elders and say: My husband's brother refuses to raise up a name for his brother in Israel; he is not willing to perform the duty of a husband's brother. Then the elders of his city shall summon him and speak to him; and if he persists and says: I do not wish to take her, then his brother's wife shall come to him in the presence of the elders, pull his sandal off his foot, spit in his face, and declare: So shall it be done to the man who does not build up his brother's house. And his name shall be called in Israel: The house of him whose sandal was pulled off. And if men fight with one another, and the wife of one comes near to rescue her husband from the hand of him who is striking him, and puts out her hand and seizes him by his private parts, then you shall cut off her hand; your eye shall not pity her. End of quotation. And all these burdens were also upon the Christians, as long as there is no text in the Injil abrogating them.

(p-127) When the Exalted has completed what He arranged within these narratives of the noble qualities of this noble Prophet, urging belief in him and making it obligatory on the basis that it is known from him that he is the Messenger of Allah to every accountable person, whether his time came before or after, He commanded him (p-127) to state explicitly what had been alluded to before, and to state explicitly what He had taken as the covenant of the Messengers concerning him, to confirm the universality of his message and the comprehensiveness of his call. So He said: ﴿Say﴾, and used the particle of distance, because it is its proper place: ﴿O people﴾. It has already passed in al-An'am that their derivation is from al-nawS (oscillation/swaying), and that Imam al-Subki said: this implies the inclusion of the jinn and the angels among them. What was mentioned earlier at ﴿And do not diminish people's things﴾ [al-A'raf: 85] in this surah is beneficial here. ﴿Indeed I am the Messenger of Allah﴾, that is, the One to whom belongs all dominion. ﴿to you all﴾, that is, there is no distinction between those who met me and those who came after me or before me, in that all of them are required to believe in me and follow me. This is the meaning of his (ﷺ) saying, related by the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) and others, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), when a foreleg was brought to him and he took a bite of it: "I am the lord of people on the Day of Resurrection." Al-Darimi, at the beginning of his Musnad, related from Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I am the leader of the Messengers, and no boasting; I am the seal of the Prophets, and no boasting; I am the first intercessor and the first whose intercession is accepted, and no boasting." Al-Tirmidhi, in the chapter on virtues, related from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I am the first of people to come out when they are resurrected, I am their leader when they are brought in delegations, I am their orator when they are silent, I am their intercessor when they are held back, I am their bearer of good news when they despair; the banner of praise on that day is in my hand, and I am the most honoured of the children of Adam before my Lord, and no boasting." He said: a hasan gharib hadith. He also has, in the chapter on virtues as well, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, I will be the imam of the Prophets, their orator, and the holder of their intercession, not boasting." He said: hasan sahih gharib. Al-Tirmidhi and al-Darimi related from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Behold! I am the beloved of Allah, and no boasting; I am the bearer of the banner of praise on the Day of Resurrection, under it is Adam and whoever is below him, and no boasting; I am the first intercessor and the first whose intercession is accepted on the Day of Resurrection, and no boasting; I am the most honoured of the first and the last, and no boasting." Al-Tirmidhi said: hasan. He related from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I am the lord of the children of Adam on the Day of Resurrection, and no boasting; the banner of praise is in my hand, and no boasting; there is no Prophet on that day, from Adam onward, except that he is under my banner." Al-Fakhr (boasting) is the claim of greatness, pride and nobility. That is, I do not say it out of vanity, but out of thankfulness and to speak of the blessing. He never gathered with them in any assembly except that he was their imam, before his death and after it. He gathered with them on the night of the Isra' at Bayt al-Maqdis and led them in prayer as imam; then he gathered with them in the heavens and led all the people of the heavens in prayer as imam.
