As for the Day of the Great Gathering and the Greatest Distress, all will refer to him and believe in the message. Some of the great ones referred to others only because they knew that the seal would be through him.

(So that it may be more manifest in acknowledging his trustworthiness and submitting to his obedience; for the one who refers to a referrer of a thing is himself a referrer to that thing. Had anyone among those before 'Isa (peace be upon him) referred to his paths, there would be a possibility. The sum is that on that station he (ﷺ) manifests his message in act to all creation, and thus the secret of this verse becomes evident: ﴿who follow the Messenger﴾ [al-A'raf: 157]. And Allah is the Granter of success.)

When the attribution to the Name of the Essence, which indicates all the attributes, indicated the universality of his call and the comprehensiveness of his message, even to the jinn and the angels, He confirmed this with His saying: ﴿He to whom belongs﴾, that is, alone, ﴿the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, it is no wonder that He sends him to all who are in them, and what is in them.

Since among what he (the earthly king) fears is that in the king's realm there may be someone who contends with him, or who is close to him, such as a crown prince or the like, who may at times reject some of his command under the guise of advice or otherwise, He negated that by saying, clarifying the completeness of His dominion: ﴿There is no god but Him﴾, that is, all are submissive to His command and subject to Him, because there is no existent, actual or possible, that is fit for divinity other than Him. Then He gave the reason for that by His saying: ﴿He gives life and causes death﴾, that is, these two attributes belong to Him exclusively, and whoever is thus is singular in what has been mentioned. If you consult what will come, God willing, at the beginning of al-Furqan, along with what has passed at the beginning of al-An'am, there will remain no doubt in your mind about the inclusion of the angels (peace be upon them) in the universality of the call.

Since it was established that He has no contender, the command to submit to His Messenger was made consequent upon that, so He said: ﴿So believe in Allah﴾, that is, because of what is established for Him of greatness and of encompassing the attributes of perfection and of all things; for belief in Him is the foundation upon which nothing of the religion is built except upon it.

Since the closest of the original branches to Him is the Messenger, He said: ﴿and His Messenger﴾, that is, because he is His Messenger. Then He described him with what indicates his nearness, saying: ﴿the Prophet﴾, that is, the one who informs him of what He wills of great matters, unseen and witnessed, and who exalts him above every creature by informing him of his sending. And since his superiority over every scholar, though he did not learn from any human, is the strongest proof of his truthfulness, He said: ﴿the unlettered﴾, that is, the one who, despite not being skilled in writing or reading, but rather being upon the first, sound nature that no desire has mixed with, nor has any portion or appetite tarnished, is such that he is sought and followed to be emulated, for what he has gathered of the knowledge of this world and the Hereafter and of being characterized by the attributes of perfection.

Since by this attribute He indicated that the cause of faith is deliverance from desire through being upon the first nature, He said, drawing attention to the obligation of believing in him, because he is the first doer of what he calls to: ﴿who believes in Allah﴾, that is, for the sake of what His Essence, the Exalted, requires of worship to Him because of His greatness. So whenever there is renewed for him a knowledge of the knowledges of the Essence, according to his ascent in the ranks of perfection, from a perfect rank to one more perfect than it, to what has no end, He renews for him a faith commensurate with it, which negligence does not afflict and inattention does not mix with, nor any taint of slackness. ﴿And His words﴾ likewise: whenever there is renewed for him knowledge of an attribute among them, he renews faith in it. Among them are the miracles that occurred at his hands, each one of which is a word, because his manifestation was through the Word, just as 'Isa (peace be upon him) was named a word for that reason.

Since it was established that he complied with what he was commanded, and thereby his message was confirmed, he deserved to be an exemplar, so He said: ﴿And follow him﴾, that is, in everything he says and does, of what he forbids or commands or permits, ﴿that you may be guided﴾, that is, so that your state becomes that of one for whom there is hoped the attainment of what was asked in al-Fatihah of guidance, that is, the creation of guidance in the heart together with its continuance.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 159:

When the enumeration of the faults of the Children of Israel had become extensive, and He concluded it by singling out those who follow this noble Prophet for guidance and for the mercy that results from it, and since among them (the Children of Israel) there were those who stood firm upon what their Lord had prescribed for them, who held fast to what was incumbent upon them, the people of obedience to Him and His party, whether that was among the attributes of the Prophet ﷺ or other than them, together with acceptance of all of that, He drew attention to it as a return to completing their accounts. Then (He mentioned) what occurred in the days of Musa (Moses), peace be upon him, and after him, of their evildoers, as consolation and solace for this noble Prophet, and to comfort his pure soul and to console him, and it, together with what follows it of proofs, (comes after) ﴿I will turn away from My signs﴾ [al-A'raf: 146]. Thus He, exalted is He, said, conjoining it to: ﴿And the people of Musa took, after him,﴾ [al-A'raf: 148] ﴿and among the people of Musa is a community﴾, that is: a people deserving to be followed, because they do not act arrogantly in the earth without right, but rather (p-132) ﴿they guide﴾, that is: they bring about guidance, which is clarification, ﴿by the truth, and by it﴾, that is: specifically, ﴿they do justice﴾, that is: they make the disputed matters in dispute into an equilibrium so that satisfaction is achieved through them, and no injustice occurs from them in any of them. And among them are those who followed the Prophet ﷺ, such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and Mukhayriq, may Allah be pleased with them both.

And when He praised them, He began to remind them of some of the blessings He had bestowed upon them, for the sake of these guided ones, concerning the multiplication after their small number and the honor after their humiliation, by making them among those who are followed, as an appeal to others. He also mentions some of their punishments as a warning. He said: ﴿And We divided them﴾, meaning We separated them into persons, after they had been one water from one person, namely Israel, peace be upon him. He stated the multitude explicitly after having hinted at it through the word "division," by saying ﴿twelve﴾, and He put the noun it specifies, which is the singular form that is the specification of "ten," in the plural, to indicate that each tribe (sibt, plural asbat, meaning a grandson's offspring, and a clan among the Jews; this root revolves around multiplicity and extension) comprises, because of its large number, several clans, by saying ﴿tribes﴾. He clarified their greatness and the extent of their dispersion and diversity by saying ﴿nations﴾, meaning they were worthy of people seeking them out because of their numbers, strength and religion. Or it means that each nation among them was followed in a religion different from what the others among other peoples followed.

When He described them with this multitude, and this was a pathway to mentioning the favor bestowed upon them in sufficiency of food and drink, He mentioned a blessing that broke the usual pattern concerning water. He began with it because it is the foundation of life. It is of the same kind as their division from one soul, indicating their wrongdoing and their haste in apostasy. He said: ﴿And We inspired to Musa when﴾, meaning at the time when ﴿his people asked him for water﴾, meaning they requested of him, in a desert with no water, that he give them drink. That was during the wandering (tih) in the wilderness. The mention of "his people" indicates their rebuke, in that they were a strong people yet did not follow Musa, peace be upon him, in patience until God, who had commanded them on this journey, brought relief. Rather they asked him for this in the manner mentioned in al-Baqarah, with the display of anxiety and grumbling. ﴿Strike with your staff﴾, meaning the one We made a sign for you, with which you struck the sea and it split, ﴿the rock﴾, meaning any rock of this kind that you wish. Glory be to Him explained the swiftness of Musa's compliance, peace be upon him, and the swiftness of the effect of his striking, by omitting "so he struck it," and by His words pointing to it: ﴿and there gushed forth﴾, meaning it split, appeared and sprang forth. [That is sufficient for censuring them and blaming them for their disbelief after being granted this favor. This context, which is to explain their haste in apostasy, does not preclude that it was in the manner of a gushing forth, and in that case the censure would be even stronger.] ﴿From it, twelve springs﴾, according to the number of the tribes. He indicated the intensity of their separation by His words: ﴿Every people knew their drinking place﴾, meaning each of the tribes. Since no food was mentioned previously, and this was not the context of gratitude, He did not mention what completed this verse in al-Baqarah.

When He mentioned the cooling of hearts with water, He followed it with cooling by shade, and said: ﴿And We shaded them﴾, meaning in the wilderness, ﴿with the clouds﴾, so that they would not be harmed by the sun. When He completed the cooling of hearts, He followed it with nourishment of bodies, and said: ﴿And We sent down upon them the manna﴾, meaning bread, ﴿and the quails﴾, meaning condiment. Al-Samaw'al ibn Yahya said: it is a small bird resembling the quail, whose property is that eating its flesh softens hard hearts; it dies when it hears the sound of thunder, just as the swift (khuttaf) is killed by cold. God, Mighty and Majestic, inspires it to dwell on the islands of the sea where there is no rain or thunder, until the time of rain and thunder passes; then it leaves the islands and spreads over the earth.

When He mentioned its greatness in this, He mentioned its result and said: ﴿Eat of the good things with which We have provided you﴾, meaning with the attribute of overpowering majesty, of what We desire, of what you have not processed in any kind of processing. He indicated that they met this kindness with transgression, wrongdoing and aggression by His words, as a conjunction to what is understood as an implied meaning: "So they turned away from the permitted good things, and ate the vile things that We had forbidden them through hunting on the Sabbath, as will come, and did other forbidden things, thus wronging themselves by that." ﴿And they did not wrong Us﴾, meaning, not with anything in which they met kindness with ingratitude. ﴿But they were wronging themselves﴾, meaning constantly, by disposition and nature, ﴿themselves﴾, meaning specifically. ﴿They used to wrong﴾. This, together with being one of the proofs of ﴿I will turn away from My signs﴾ [al-A'raf: 146] and what follows, is evidence for the correctness of describing this Messenger as a prophet; for whoever knows these details of their accounts, while being unlettered and not having mixed with any of their scholars, (p-135) would be truthful about the Knower of the unseen, without any supporter. And likewise what follows.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 161:**

When he had mentioned what He bestowed upon them in the deserts, He followed it with His favor upon them on their arrival at the dwelling-place, saying: ﴿And when﴾, i.e., remind them of this, so that they may believe you, or so that they may reach the extreme of wrongdoing like the People of the Sabbath and thus anticipate a punishment like theirs. Remind them of what you were not present for and did not learn from them, and that was the time of "when" [wa-'adala 'ani al-ikram bi-al-khitab wa-nun al-'azamah; li-anna al-siyaq lil-isra' fi al-kufr, fa-qala:] ﴿it was said to them: Dwell﴾, i.e., enter it settled in the manner of residence [wa-la yusamma sakinan illa ba'da al-tawattun bi-khilaf al-dukhul, fa-innahu yakunu bi-mujarrad al-wuluj fi al-shay' 'ala ayyi wajhin kana] ﴿this town﴾. This is another proof of the two matters: the diversion (al-sarf) and the truthfulness (al-sidq). He expressed it here in the passive form in ﴿it was said﴾, turning away from giving them the pleasure of direct address, as a notice that this context is for anger at them because of their falling into disbelief and their turning away from gratitude, from whatever speaker it came and in whatever form the statement was delivered and in whatever state it was. It also serves to show the greatness, since even a slight gesture from Him sufficed for their dwelling in the lands and their settling in them as conquerors over its people, whose hearts were filled with awe, until they said: ﴿Indeed, we will never enter it as long as they are in it﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 24].

When the bounty of eating in this context was free of what the context of al-Baqarah called for of consequence (al-ta'qib), which is supplication (al-isti'tf), it was mentioned with the conjunction "wa" (and), which indicates general association and is not contrary to that. So He said: ﴿And eat from it﴾, i.e., from the town, ﴿wherever you wish﴾, and He omitted "raghad" (abundant ease) for this reason. And He placed first: ﴿and say: Hittah﴾, so that it would be the first thing striking the hearing of what they were commanded regarding worship, indicating the great burden of sins they had carried, as a notice of what these narratives were brought for in this surah of the station.

When they were commanded with "hittah" as speech, they were commanded to accompany it with an action, so that their sins might be removed from them. The placing first here is not contrary to the delaying in al-Baqarah, because the "wa" (and) does not imply order. So He said: ﴿And enter the gate﴾, i.e., the gate of Bayt al-Maqdis, while you are ﴿prostrating; We will forgive you﴾.

Since the context here is to show their rapidity in disbelief, the plural of multiplicity (jam' al-kathrah) in His saying "khataya-kum" ("your sins") in the recitation (qira'ah) of Abu 'Amr suited that. As for the recitation of Ibn 'Amir, "khati'atakum" (in the singular), and the recitation of others, "khataya-tikum" (the plural of paucity, jam' qillah), it is to indicate that they are few in comparison with His pardon, exalted is He. Likewise the form "tughfar" (it will be forgiven) in the passive, feminine and masculine, all of this is for hope for them and for supplication toward repentance. For this reason, He, glorified is He, placed what follows in the manner of a question for one who seems to say: This hope has been realized; is there with forgiveness any honor? So He said: ﴿We will surely increase﴾, i.e., by a promise without any failing, soon, and this is not contrary to the affirmation of the "wa" in al-Baqarah, ﴿the doers of good﴾, i.e., those who excel in this attribute, (p-137) and according to the context I have described, He restricted His saying:

So that it is not supposed that they were among those who had joined them, [the verse says] ﴿Then those who did wrong replaced﴾ [the word] ﴿of them﴾ ﴿a saying other than what﴾ [they had been told].

Since it is known that the one who speaks the command is the one who has authority over them, [the verb] was put in the passive form and [the verse] says ﴿it was said to them﴾, and [it] says ﴿So We sent﴾, meaning with the majesty We possess, ﴿upon them﴾ — with the pronoun used to make the matter awe-inspiring, since the punishment could be general — ﴿a scourge from the sky﴾. The word "wrongdoing" (zulm) in His saying ﴿because they used to do wrong﴾ — in what it implies, namely that they never cease to be in a state of darkness, either absolutely or together with the renewal of the act of the one who is engaged in it — is more terrifying than the word "transgression" (fisq), which implies the renewal of going out from what should be steadfastly kept to. Likewise, the word "sending" (irsal), when followed by "upon" ('ala), is in relation to the word "sending down" (inzal) in the same way.

When he had finished exposing their deeds during the days of Musa (peace be upon him) and what followed them, he followed it with another disgrace, worse than the previous one, which occurred some time after that, a time known to no one except from their side or from Allah. And when the first is negated, the second is established. So He said: ﴿And ask them﴾, that is, the Children of Israel, rebuking them and establishing the fact against them, ﴿about the town﴾, that is, the populous city, ﴿which was by the sea﴾, that is, on its shore, and it was Ayla. Perhaps He expressed it with a question, and did not say, "And when the town transgressed..." and the like, because their dislike of being informed of this scandal was greater than what passed, and it is a sign of sincerity and truthfulness. Since the question was about the account of the people of the town, He said (p-138), substituting for "the town" a substitution of inclusion: ﴿when﴾, that is, at the time when ﴿they transgressed﴾, that is, they went beyond the limit which Allah had commanded them, ﴿in the Sabbath, when﴾, that is, the transgression at the time when ﴿their fish came to them﴾. He increased the rebuke by alluding to their hastening into disbelief through the attribution in His saying ﴿their fish﴾, indicating that they were created for them; so if they had been patient they would have obtained them while being obedient, as in the hadith of Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him), traced to the Prophet: "Between the servant and his provision there is a veil; if he is patient, it comes out to him, and if not, he tears the veil and obtains only what has been decreed for him." ﴿On their Sabbath day﴾, that is, the day which they honoured by abstaining from occupying themselves with anything other than worship, ﴿appearing openly﴾, that is, near and prominent to them, visible on the surface of the water in abundance; it is the plural of shari'a and shari'; that is, near. ﴿And on the day when they did not keep the Sabbath﴾, that is, when there was no Sabbath, and perhaps He expressed it this way to indicate that if they had honoured Sunday as though it were a Sabbath, it would have come to them on it, and it is from: "the Jews kept the Sabbath," when they honoured their Sabbath. ﴿It did not come to them﴾, that is, as a trial from Allah for them; and if they had been patient, Allah would have removed this habit, and they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet.

Since this was a great trial, He said, answering a question from one who seemed to say, due to the intensity of his amazement at this matter: Has anything like this happened? indicating that it did happen, and not limiting himself to it, but rather similar things happened to them, to manifest what is in the unseen world from them into the visible world: ﴿Thus﴾, that is, like this great trial, ﴿We test them﴾, that is, We renew their testing every little while, ﴿because of﴾, that is, the cause of what ﴿they were﴾, that is, by nature and disposition, ﴿transgressing﴾, that is, they renew in Our knowledge the transgression, which is going out from what is (p-139) fit for settling in of acts of obedience.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 164:

When he had informed that wickedness (fisq) was their habit, he emphasized it with his saying, coordinating it with ﴿when they transgress﴾ [al-A'raf: 163], ﴿and when﴾, that is: ask them about their news when ﴿a community among them said﴾, that is: a group of those whose counsel is regarded and sought, from the righteous admonishers who admonished until they despaired of a other community among them that would not desist from admonition, as a warning to those being admonished of what they overstep, ﴿Why do you admonish a people﴾, that is: relying upon their strength, ﴿whom God﴾, that is: He to whom belongs all sovereignty, ﴿will destroy﴾, that is: without doubt, because they do not desist from corruption and do not heed admonitions, ﴿or punish with a severe punishment﴾, that is: for the enormity of what they commit and their persistence in it. ﴿They said﴾, that is: the other community of admonishers: we admonish ﴿as an excuse to your Lord﴾, that is: the Benefactor to you, by guarding against what they have fallen into of sin, and by turning to admonition, so that if we are asked about our conduct regarding their disobedience, we can say: we exerted our utmost effort regarding their affair. This is if they do not return. ﴿And perhaps they will fear God﴾, that is: so that their state becomes the state of one whose fear of God is hoped for, and so that he returns from his error.

When they had returned to this admonition, so that it would be a deterrent to the disobedient, and they did not heed it, he informed that their assumption was confirmed in the occurrence of both matters together: the severe punishment and the destruction. So He said: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of﴾, meaning: they acted in their turning away from it as one who forgets does, and they abandoned it as one abandons what is forgotten; that is, [forgot] that God does not leave them unattended, just as a person cannot leave unattended anyone under his authority, so as to do whatever he wishes without objection. ﴿We saved﴾, meaning: by Our might, ﴿those who forbade﴾, meaning: those who persisted in forbidding ﴿evil﴾, meaning: the forbidden. ﴿And We seized﴾, meaning: a seizing of overpowering and subjugation, ﴿those who did wrong﴾, meaning: by transgressing on the Sabbath, ﴿with a severe punishment﴾, meaning: extremely severe, ﴿because they used to defy (God)﴾, meaning: by nature and disposition, ﴿and they used to defy﴾, meaning: because of their persistence in continually renewing their defiance.

When he had mentioned the severe punishment with which he threatened them, he followed it with destruction, saying: ﴿So when they became insolent﴾, i.e., they were arrogant through boorishness and hardness, refusing to desist, ﴿from what they had been forbidden﴾, i.e., after being seized by the severe punishment. They went beyond this to daring against all the sins, out of obstinacy and arrogance, with utmost impudence and indifference. Their persistence in that sin, and their being granted respite together with admonition, earned them this, and their hearts became hardened against fear despite the deterrence of punishment. From ʿataa yaʿtoo ʿutuwwan, meaning when one turns to sins; so he is ʿatin. ʿAbd al-Haqq said in Kitabat al-Wa'i: It is said: when one proceeds in all his affairs, and from it this verse. It is said: the ʿatī is one who goes to extremes in committing sins. It is said: the rebel, for whom admonition and warning are of no avail. From it is His saying: ﴿So they defied the command of their Lord﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 44], i.e., they exceeded the measure and limit in disbelief. End of quotation.

Its literal meaning: they went beyond the command to the prohibition, or went beyond obeying His command. The root returns to coarseness, harshness and hardness. ﴿We said to them﴾, i.e., by the great power We possess, ﴿Be apes﴾, i.e., in the form of apes, while you are ﴿despised﴾, i.e., humiliated and expelled, distanced from mercy as the dog is driven away.

(p-141)

And when the preceding passage has made clear their boldness in sin and their haste in it, and that they deserve the lasting disgrace and humiliation, He informed that He had done this to them in a manner that necessarily establishes that they are entangled in misguidance and committing evil deeds for as long as that punishment remains upon them. So He said: ﴿And when﴾, which is conjoined to ﴿and ask them﴾ [al-A'raf: 163]. That is: and mention to them the time when ﴿your Lord proclaimed﴾, that is, announced with a great and deliberately emphasized proclamation, ﴿your Lord﴾, that is, the One who nurtures you, prepares the proofs for your law, and grants you victory over whoever opposes you.

Since what was said operates in the manner of an oath, it took the lam of emphasis, so it is as if it were said: He proclaimed, swearing by His might, His greatness, His knowledge and His power: ﴿He will surely send﴾, that is, from a far place. It conveyed that this is the sending of punishment by means of the particle of elevation (ʿalā, "upon"), which implies that the meaning is: He will surely impose upon ﴿them﴾, that is, the Jews, and He extended the period of this imposition, so He said: ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾, which is the greatest decisive day, ﴿those who will inflict upon them﴾, that is, will constantly bring down on them ﴿the worst torment﴾ through humiliation, belittlement, the imposition of the jizya (the poll tax levied on non-Muslim subjects) and contempt. And so Allah, glorified is He, did: He set over them nations and scattered them across the earth in every dispersal since they denied the mission of the Messiah, peace be upon him, as the true promise in the Torah brought to them, and the translation of this is present in their hands now in His saying at the end of the First Book: "The scepter shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be" (in one copy: "the all"), and the peoples await him; "binding his foal unto the vine, and his ass's colt unto the choice vine" [Genesis 49:10–11]. And Samawʾal said at the beginning of his book Ghayat al-Maqsud: We say to them: In the Torah that is in your hands there is nothing whose interpretation is: "The rule shall not depart from the house of Judah, nor the ruler from among them, until the Messiah comes," so they cannot deny it. We say to them: If you know that you were the people of a state and a kingdom until the appearance of the Messiah, and then your kingdom ended, then [the matter is clear] – end of quote.

And from the days of the mission of the Messiah, Allah set the nations over them and scattered them across the earth, so they were at one time under the rule of the Babylonians, and at another [under the hands of the Magians, and at another time under the subjugation of the Romans from the sons of Esau, and at another] in captivity to others, until the Prophet (ﷺ) came and imposed the jizya upon them, he and his community after him.

Since the context concerns punishment and what necessitates it, He gave the reason for that with emphasis, saying: ﴿Indeed your Lord﴾, that is, the one who does good to you by humiliating your enemies, those who are the most hostile of nations toward you and toward those who believe in you, ﴿is swift in punishment﴾, that is, He punishes immediately after the sin by retribution, inwardly through the black spots upon the heart, and outwardly – if He wills – through what He wills. This is contrary to what is in al-An'am, for there it is in the context of favor, by making them successors (khalaʾif).

Since He instilled fear, He encouraged with His saying: ﴿And indeed He is Forgiving﴾, that is, the eraser of sins, both in essence and in trace, for whoever repents and believes, ﴿Merciful﴾, that is, the honorer and bestower of favor through granting success in what He is pleased with, and then through what becomes a means for him to elevation in this world and the Hereafter.

[168–169] Mention of some of what they were threatened with in the Torah for disobedience, rebellion and transgression, other than what preceded in al-Ma'idah at His saying: ﴿whom Allah has cursed and with whom He became angry﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 60] and other verses. He said in the Fifth Book: "And if you do not keep and do all the commandments and statutes that are written in this book, and fear the Lord your God, and fail to hold His glorious and awesome name, the Lord will bring upon you severe plagues and afflict you with them, and afflict your seed after you, and they will continue upon you; and there shall remain of your seed a small number after their multitude, which had become like the stars of heaven; and you will be removed from the land which you are entering to possess it; and the Lord will scatter you among the peoples, and there you will serve other gods, which were made of stone and wood, and you will not dwell among those peoples; but the Lord will make your hearts there fearful and trembling, saying in the morning: 'Would God it were evening!' and in the evening: 'Would God it were morning!' because of the fear of your hearts and your dread and your lack of resources; and the Lord will return you to the land of Egypt with ships, by the way of which the Lord said: You shall not see it again; and you will be sold there [as slaves] and maidservants, and there will be no one to buy you." These are the words of the covenant which the Lord commanded Moses to make with the children of Israel in the land of Moab, apart from the covenant which He made with them at Horeb. Then Moses summoned all the children of Israel and said to them: "You have seen all that the Lord did in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh and all his servants and all his land; the great trials which your eyes saw, the signs and the wonders you witnessed; yet the Lord has not given you a heart to understand and know, nor eyes to see, nor ears to hear, to this day. And He led you through the wilderness forty years; your clothes did not wear out upon you, nor did your sandals wear out on your feet; you did not eat bread, so that you might know that I am the Lord your God, and that I brought you to this land. So keep the words of this Torah and do them, and complete all the works in obedience to God and perfect them; for you have all known that we were dwellers in the land of Egypt and passed among the nations, and you saw their filth and their idols. Lest there be among you today a man or woman, or a clan or tribe, whose heart turns away from the worship of the Lord our God and who seeks to worship the gods of those nations; and he hears these words of the covenant and says, 'Peace will be mine, though I follow the desire of my heart'; the Lord will not be willing to forgive him, but rather the anger and wrath of the Lord will burn against him, and every curse written in this book will fall upon him, and the Lord will blot out his name from under heaven, and the Lord will separate him from all the tribes of the children of Israel for evil and calamities. And the next generation, your children who rise up after you and the strangers, will say, when they see the plagues of that land and the sicknesses with which the Lord has afflicted it: 'Why has the Lord done thus? Why this great burning anger?' And they will say: 'Because they forsook the covenant of the Lord, the God of their fathers, therefore the anger of the Lord was kindled against this nation, and He brought upon it every curse written in this book.' And the Lord will uproot them from their land in anger, with great wrath and rebuke, and will cast them into another land, as it is today." The hidden things and secrets belong to the Lord our God, but the revealed and manifest matters belong to us.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 168:

When He, glorified be He, informed of the proclamation (al-ta'adhdhun), it was as if it had been said: "So We hastened their punishment for their sins, and We sent against them those who would inflict upon them the worst torment, by killing and taking captives." Then He followed it with His saying: ﴿And We divided them﴾ — that is, because of the captivity that resulted from the punishment, by Our might, into many divisions, by scattering them greatly ﴿in the earth﴾ while they were ﴿communities (umaman)﴾, one following another, so that in every town there were only a few of them, who had no strength and could not defend themselves against injustice.

Then, as if it had been said: "Did they, after this punishment, unite upon goodness?" It is said: "No. Rather, their religions divided them, much like the division of their bodies." ﴿Among them are the righteous﴾ — that is, those who remained steadfast in their religion until the abrogating (al-nasikh) came, and then they followed it in compliance with the call of their Book. ﴿And among them are others below that﴾ — that is, given to wickedness at times and to disbelief at other times. ﴿And We tested them﴾ — that is, We dealt with them as one who tests, so that it would become manifest to people what We know of them ﴿with good things﴾ — that is, blessings ﴿and evil things﴾ — that is, retributions ﴿so that they might return﴾ — that is, so that their state would be that of those whose return from their error is hoped for, out of desire or out of fear.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 169:

Since the punishment whose announcement had been made was [extended] until the Day of Resurrection (p-146), his saying ﴿so there succeeded﴾ followed from it. That is, there arose [a generation]. Since they were not totally absorbed in the length of time, he used the preposition and said ﴿after them there succeeded a successor﴾, that is, a people who were worse in condition than they. ﴿They inherited the Book﴾, that is, that which is a blessing, namely the Torah. It became a curse for them, because it testified against them to the ugliness of their deeds, for it remained in their hands after their forefathers, as they read it but did not act upon what is in it. Ibn Faris said: "Al-khalf is what comes after, whether it is vocalized with a fatha on the lam or is sukun." Abu 'Ubayd al-Harawi said in al-Gharibayn: "It is said: khalf su' (with sukun) and khalaf sidq." Al-Zubaydi said in Mukhtasar al-'Ayn: "Al-khalf is the bad successor after his father, and al-khalaf is the righteous one." Ibn al-Qatta' said in al-Af'al: "And khalafa khalf su' means: they came after a righteous people, and khalf su' (with sukun)." Al-Akhfash said: "Both are the same," meaning in the sense that some people use sukun and some use fatha in both, and some say khalaf sidq (with fatha) and khalf su' (with sukun), intending by that to distinguish between them. Whenever it is in construct (idafah), the sukun is for corruption and the fatha for righteousness. In al-Qamus he said: "Khalf is the opposite of quddam (front), and a generation after a generation. From it: these are a bad successor (khalf su'), and a bad speech. With fatha, it is a righteous son. When he is corrupt, you make the lam sukun. Sometimes each of them is used in place of the other. It is said: he is a righteous successor (khalaf sidq) to his father when he takes his place (p-147), or khalf with sukun and fatha are the same." Al-Layth said: "Khalf (with sukun) is specifically for the wicked, and with fatha its opposite." The root returns to khalf, which is the opposite of quddam, as I have explained in the chapter on the mudtarib in my marginal notes on the Sharh Alfiyyat al-'Iraqi.

Since what is expected of those who inherit the Book is good, it was as if it were said: "What did they do of good with what they inherited?" He answered, resuming: ﴿they take﴾, or they renew the taking constantly. He belittled what they took by informing that it is something that passes away and does not last, but is perishable, so he said ﴿this trifling goods﴾. He added to its lowliness by the indication of the near, so he said ﴿this﴾, and he made the intended meaning explicit with his saying ﴿the lower﴾, that is, of the two existences, which is the world. ﴿And they say﴾, that is, constantly, without repentance.

Since what benefits is forgiveness without regard to a specific [offense], they framed their saying in the passive: ﴿we shall be forgiven﴾, that is, without doubt. Thus they proceeded to evil and were certain of the occurrence of what makes its future occurrence remote, [a judgment about one who judges and is not judged]. He stated explicitly what their persistence implied, marveling at them for their certainty of forgiveness despite that, with his saying ﴿and if﴾, that is, while the state is that if ﴿a similar trifling good comes to them﴾, that is, in baseness and lowliness, and in forbiddenness like bribery, ﴿they will take it﴾.

[Since this is great, he rebuked them emphatically] for the sake of reproach, with his saying, resuming (p-148): ﴿Was not the covenant of the Book taken from them﴾. He framed it in the passive, indicating that a covenant must be fulfilled in every case. Then he magnified it with his saying ﴿the covenant of the Book﴾, that is, the emphatic covenant [in the Torah], ﴿that they should not say﴾ [that is, any saying at all, even if little] ﴿about God﴾, that is, the One who has perfection and greatness, ﴿except the truth﴾, that is, what is known to be firm. And it is not among what is known to be firm to affirm forgiveness with certainty without repentance; rather, that is a departure from the covenant of the Book.

Since it might occur to the mind that the covenant was taken from their forefathers and these people did not act upon it, he negated that with his saying ﴿and they studied what is in it﴾, that is, what is in that covenant, through repeated recitation for memorization. ﴿And the Last Abode﴾, that is, they did what was mentioned before of turning away from piety, while the Hereafter is ﴿better﴾, that is, than what they take, ﴿for those who fear God﴾, that is, while they know that by the information of their Book. For this reason he rebuked them with his saying ﴿Will you not then reason?﴾, that is, when they took what makes them wretched and perishes in exchange for what makes them happy and lasts. According to the recitation of Nafi', Ibn 'Amir and Hafs with the second person, the intended meaning is to inform of the extreme of anger.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 170:

When he had explained the state of the corrupters, that they "said about God other than the truth," and so "it will not be forgiven them," he explained the state of the righteous mentioned in His words: ﴿And among the people of Moses is a community who guide by the truth and by it act justly﴾ [al-A'raf: 159]. He said, connecting it to its implied sense: "Those, their deeds have been nullified in what they studied of the Book, and what they committed of corruption will not be forgiven them." Then: ﴿Those who hold fast﴾, that is, who hold fast with a firm grip that is renewed continuously [kull] in every way, and this is an indication that adherence to the Sunnah is extremely difficult, especially when corruption appears. ﴿to the Book﴾, that is, so they do not speak about God except the truth. Among the continuous forms of their holding fast is their moving away from that Book when the abrogating text (al-nasikh, i.e. naskh, abrogation) arrives, because it speaks to that.

And God is the Granter of success.

When holding fast to the Book at the revelation of this discourse included their moving away from their religion to Islam, as the command to this had occurred in the passages whose explanation has preceded, he expressed the establishment of the prayer known to them with the past tense rather than the present, lest they make it an argument for steadfastness in their religion, which would produce the opposite of the intended meaning. So he said: ﴿and they establish the prayer﴾. He singled it out as an indication that the earlier ones had abandoned it, as stated in the verse about Maryam, and as an honouring of its status, explaining that it is among the greatest rites of the religion. Since the implied construction, as a predicate about the subject, was: "We shall give them their rewards for their reform," he placed in its position, for generality, His words: ﴿Indeed We do not allow to be lost﴾, that is, in any way whatsoever, ﴿the reward of the reformers﴾.

ولَمّا ذَكَرَ الكِتابُ أنَّهُ رَهَّبَهم مِن مُخالَفَتِهِ ورَغَّبَهم في مُؤالَفَتِهِ، وكانَ عَذابُ الآخِرَةِ مُسْتَقْبَلًا وغائِبًا، وكانَ ما هَذا شَأْنُهُ يُؤَثِّرُ في الجامِدِينَ، أمَرَهُ أنْ يُذَكِّرَهم بِتَرْهِيبٍ دُنْيَوِيٍّ مَضى إيقاعُهُ بِهِمْ، لِيَأْخُذُوا مَواثِيقَ الكِتابِ لِغايَةِ الجِدِّ مَعَ أنَّهُ لا يَعْلَمُهُ إلّا عُلَماؤُهُمْ، فَيَكُونُ (p-١٥٠) عِلْمُ الأُمِّيِّ لَهُ مِن أعْلامِ نُبُوَّتِهِ الظّاهِرَةِ فَقالَ: ﴿وإذْ﴾ أيِ: اذْكُرْ لَهم هَذا، فَإنْ لَمْ يَتَّعِظُوا اذْكُرْ لَهم إذْ ﴿نَتَقْنا﴾ أيْ: قَلَعْنا ورَفَعْنا، [و] أتى بِنُونِ العَظَمَةِ لِزِيادَةِ التَّرْهِيبِ ﴿الجَبَلَ﴾ عَرَّفَهُ لِمَعْرِفَتِهِمْ بِهِ، [وعَبَّرَ لِدَلالَةِ لَفْظِهِ عَلى الصُّعُوبَةِ والشِّدَّةِ دُونَ الطُّورِ - كَما في البَقَرَةِ - لِأنَّ السِّياقَ لِبَيانِ نَكَدِهِمْ بِإسْراعِهِمْ في المَعاصِي الدّالَّةِ عَلى غِلَظِ القَلْبِ].

ولَمّا كانَ مُسْتَغْرِقًا لِجَمِيعِ الجِهَةِ المُوازِيَةِ لِعَساكِرِهِمْ، حَذَفَ الجارَّ فَقالَ: ﴿فَوْقَهُمْ﴾ [ثُمَّ بَيَّنَ أنَّهُ كانَ أكْبَرَ مِنهم بِقَوْلِهِ:] ﴿كَأنَّهُ ظُلَّةٌ﴾ أيْ: سَقْفٌ، وحَقَّقَ أنَّهُ صارَ عَلَيْهِمْ مُوازِيًا لَهم مِن جِهَةِ الفَوْقِ كالسَّقْفِ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿وظَنُّوا﴾ هو عَلى حَقِيقَتِهِ ﴿أنَّهُ واقِعٌ﴾ ولَمّا كانَ ما تَقَدَّمَ قَدْ حَقَّقَ العُلُوَّ، لَمْ يَحْتَجْ إلى حَرْفِ الِاسْتِعْلاءِ، فَقالَ مُشِيرًا إلى السُّرْعَةِ واللُّصُوقِ: ﴿بِهِمْ﴾ أيْ: إنْ لَمْ يَأْخُذُوا عُهُودَ التَّوْراةِ، قالُوا: ولَمّا رَأوْا ذَلِكَ خَرَّ كُلٌّ مِنهم ساجِدًا عَلى حاجِبِهِ الأيْسَرِ، وصارَ يَنْظُرُ بِعَيْنِهِ اليُمْنى إلى الجَبَلِ فَزَعًا مِن سُقُوطِهِ، وهي سُنَّةٌ لَهم في سُجُودِهِمْ إلى الآنِ، يَقُولُونَ: هَذِهِ السَّجْدَةُ الَّتِي رُفِعَتْ عَنّا بِها العُقُوبَةُ.

ولَمّا كانَ كَأنَّهُ قِيلَ: فَقالُوا: أخَذْنا يا رَبِّ عُهُودَكَ، قالَ مُشِيرًا إلى عَظَمَتِهِ لِيَشْتَدَّ إقْبالُهم عَلَيْهِ إشارَةً إلى أنَّهُ عِلَّةُ رَفْعِ الجَبَلِ: ﴿خُذُوا ما آتَيْناكُمْ﴾ أيْ: بِعَظَمَتِنا، فَهو جَدِيرٌ بِالإقْبالِ عَلَيْهِ وأنْ يُعْتَقَدَ فِيهِ الكَمالُ، وأكَّدَ ذَلِكَ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿بِقُوَّةٍ﴾ أيْ: عَزْمٍ عَظِيمٍ عَلى احْتِمالِ (p-١٥١) مَشاقِّهِ؛ ولَمّا كانَ الأخْذُ لِلشَّيْءِ بِقُوَّةٍ رُبَّما نَسِيَهُ في وقْتٍ، قالَ: ﴿واذْكُرُوا ما فِيهِ﴾ أيْ: [مِنَ الأوامِرِ والنَّواهِي وغَيْرِهِما] فَلا تَنْسَوْهُ ﴿لَعَلَّكم تَتَّقُونَ﴾ أيْ: لِيَكُونَ حالُكم حالَ مَن يُرْجى تَقْواهُ، فَدَلَّ سُبْحانَهُ بِهَذا عَلى تَأْكِيدِ المَواثِيقِ عَلَيْهِمْ في أخْذِ جَمِيعِ ما في الكِتابِ الَّذِي مِن جُمْلَتِهِ ألّا تَقُولُوا عَلى اللَّهِ إلّا الحَقَّ ولا تَكْتُمُوا شَيْئًا مِنهُ، قالُوا: ولَمّا قَرَأ مُوسى عَلَيْهِ السَّلامُ [الألْواحَ وفِيها كِتابُ اللَّهِ لَمْ يَبْقَ عَلى الأرْضِ شَجَرٌ ولا جَبَلٌ ولا حَجَرٌ إلّا اهْتَزَّ، فَلِذَلِكَ لا تَرى يَهُودِيًّا يَسْمَعُ التَّوْراةَ إلّا اهْتَزَّ وانْقَضَّ رَأْسُهُ].

When he had mentioned that He bound them to the rulings of the Book in this overpowering, compelling, coercive manner, which is among the greatest of covenants for those who receive them, and that He emphasized the covenants upon them in many sections of the Book, and all of this was specific to them, He commanded him to tell them that He had constituted in them, within this human species in general, intellects, and had set up, from among the clear proofs for the matter, a clarity like the clarity of what is witnessed to the witness, such that if the one who abandons it and neglects it were punished, his punishment would proceed according to the methods and be fitting to the intellects. But because His mercy preceded and His compassion prevailed, He did not take them to account for that until He joined the Messengers to it, sent down the Books with them, increased the covenants in them, and added to the disclosure and clarification. The reference to this is by the name "the Lord," for whoever has knowledge is more blameworthy than the ignorant. So He said: ﴿And when﴾, that is: and mention to them when ﴿He took﴾, that is: created by His word and His power, ﴿your Lord﴾, that is: the one who has been good to you (p-152) by preparing you for your mission, just as lice are taken from the head with a comb.

Since the context concerns the taking of covenants and taking with strength, He mentioned the taking of the offspring from the strongest type of the human species, namely the males, and so He said: ﴿from the children of Adam﴾. He also mentioned that He placed them from the most sturdy of the limbs, and so He said: ﴿from their loins﴾, each one from the back of his father, ﴿their offspring﴾. This is an indication that when He emphasized the covenants upon them and made them binding, and commanded them to hold firmly to them, He gave them the strength in composition and temperament by which they would be obedient to that. Thus it is a charge within capacity. He also gave them intellects according to the one who said it is upon its literal meaning, like the ant of Solomon, peace be upon him. ﴿And He made them testify concerning themselves﴾, that is: He made clear to them, through proofs, through the bounty of intellects together with the creation of the heavens and the earth and what is in them in this pattern, which bears witness to His oneness and the perfection of His knowledge and power, and through the sending of Messengers supported by miracles, that they were like witnesses that there is no lord besides Him. [And this meaning has been mentioned by the Imam Hujjat al-Islam al-Ghazali in his discussion of the intellect in the section on knowledge of the Ihya'. For he said: The meaning of this verse and its intent is the acknowledgment of their souls, not the acknowledgment of their tongues, for they divided in the acknowledgment of the tongues when the tongues and the persons existed. Then he mentioned that souls were created with the knowledge of things as they are, due to the nearness of readiness for perception.]

Since it became clear that He is singular with no partner, so none can repel His command, and that He is Lord, so none is more kind or more merciful than Him, this was more conducive to obedience to Him, out of fear of His might and hope for His mercy. Thus they were, by this, in the position of one who is asked about the truth and acknowledges it. Therefore He said: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾, that is: the one who has been good to you by creation and by nurturing you with provision and other things. ﴿They said: Yes, we bear witness﴾, that is: our knowledge of that was witnessed knowledge. This is because they reached, after the clarification, a limit at which the answer could only be that, so it is as if they said it. So it is — and God knows best — [from] the same vein as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And to God prostrate whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly and unwillingly﴾ [al-Ra'd: 15], and His saying: ﴿And to God prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth of creatures, and the angels, and they are not arrogant﴾ [al-Nahl: 49].

Since it was as if it were said: Why did He do that? It was said: as an indication that what precedes is only by way of illustration, making their being enabled to reason like the making them witness. He did it lest ﴿you say on the Day of Resurrection﴾, that is: if proofs were not set up for them, ﴿We were indeed unaware of this﴾, that is: of Your oneness and Your lordship, ﴿heedless﴾, that is: due to the absence of proofs, and therefore we associated others with You.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 173:

﴿Or [lest] you say﴾, meaning: even if We had not sent the messengers to them, ﴿"Indeed our fathers associated [others with Allah] before, and we were [only] offspring after them."﴾ That is, before we came into existence (p-154). ﴿"And we were offspring after them. We knew of no lord for ourselves other than them, so we were followers of them, and our following them occupied us from reflection, and no messenger came to alert us."﴾ From this there follows their denial in their saying: ﴿"Will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?"﴾, that is, what our forefathers did. Abu Hayyan said: The meaning is that the disbelievers, if no covenant had been taken from them, and no messenger had come to them with what the covenant contained of the Oneness of Allah and worshipping Him, would have had two arguments: the first, "We were heedless," and the second, "We were followers of our ancestors." So how much more so, when the sin belongs only to the one who led us astray and misguided us. End of quotation.

Among what supports the sense of the parable is the hadith of Anas in the Sahih: "Allah says to the least punished of the people of the Fire: 'If you had everything on earth, would you ransom yourself with it?' He says: 'Yes.' He says: 'I asked you for what is easier than this while you were in the loins of Adam: that you not associate anything with Me. But you refused except to associate.'" This is because explicitly mentioning the fathers contradicts the covenant being taken in its literal sense, whereas taking it while in the loins is only by establishing the proofs and affirming the truth in a manner that prepares the intellect for inference, by the composition of reason according to the rule that leads to the goal, when free of desires and impurities. What has been given as the interpretation (ta'wil) of the verse is not opposed by the hadith of questioning in the realm of atoms (alam al-dharr), assuming its authenticity. It has been narrated through very many chains, which I mentioned in my book Sirr al-Ruh, including in the Muwatta, the Musnad of Ahmad, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, Muhammad ibn Nasr al-Marwazi, Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili, the Mustadrak of al-Hakim, and the Kitab al-Mi'atayn of Abu Uthman al-Sabuni, from Companions and Successors, both as marfu' and mawquf, among them Umar, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Abu Hurayrah, Hakim ibn Hizam, Abdullah ibn Salam, Abdullah ibn Amr, Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with them, and from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, Ata ibn Yasar, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, and Abu al-Aliyah, may Allah have mercy on them. It is not opposed to it because in some of its chains, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, may Allah be pleased with him, [Allah], glorified is He, said after questioning them: "Indeed I call the seven heavens and the seven earths to witness against you, and I call your father Adam to witness against you, lest you say on the Day of Resurrection: 'We were heedless of this.' So do not associate anything with Me, for I send to you My messengers who remind you of My covenant and My pledge, and I send down to you My books." They said: "We testify that You are our Lord and our God; there is no lord for us other than You." So the questioning in the hadith is on its literal basis, as a lesson for our father Adam, peace be upon him, and for whoever was present of the creation, and as a making them stand before the wonder of His power and the greatness of His knowledge. The calling to witness of what was called as witness among the creatures means that He placed in them proofs by which the establishment of the argument against them would be, through their violation, if they associate, like the testimony of a witness that cannot be rejected. Nothing in the narrations contradicts this. The summary is that two covenants were taken from us: one is a state (hali), to which the intellects are guided, which is the establishing of proofs; and the other is verbal (maqali), which the messengers informed of. All of this is to announce the greater care given to this human kind because of its noble rank, and by it is intended a great matter (p-156). And Allah is the Granter of success.

When it was as if it were said, to draw attention to the greatness of these verses: "Consider how We have detailed these verses with these outstanding details and brought them forth in these elegant styles," He said: ﴿And thus﴾, that is, and like that detailed explanation that is wondrous, majestic and exalted, ﴿We detail the verses﴾, that is, all of them, so that they do not fall into what is unbecoming on Our part out of ignorance due to the lack of evidence, ﴿that perhaps they may return﴾, that is, so that their state is that of those whose return from error is hoped for, toward the perfection to which the guides call, soon, if heedlessness occurs and they fall into it. This is among the proofs of ﴿And the good land yields its plants only by the permission of its Lord, and that which is bad, [its vegetation] comes out only sparse﴾ [al-A'raf: 58], and ﴿And We found most of them not upholding any covenant﴾ [al-A'raf: 102], and: ﴿I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant upon the earth﴾ [al-A'raf: 146].

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 175:

When He had mentioned to them the particular covenant that was taken from them in their Book, which they abandoned, and followed it with the general covenant by which He cut off their excuses, He followed both with an explanation of what they know about the state of the one who withdrew from the signs, whom Allah removed from the register of the fortunate. He (ﷺ) was commanded to recite it to them, because it, along with fulfilling their rebuke, is among the proofs of his prophethood, which obligates them to follow him. So He reminded him of what had happened to him in casting off the covenant and withdrawing from the pact, after he had been given the signs and had been endowed with the Spirit. He said: ﴿And recite﴾, i.e., read one thing after another, ﴿to them﴾, i.e., the Jews and the rest of the disbelievers, indeed all of creation, ﴿the tidings of him who﴾, and He magnified what He had bestowed upon him by the manifestation of greatness and by the word "giving," after He had magnified his report with the word "tidings." He said: ﴿We gave him﴾ (p-157) Since Allah, exalted is He, had bestowed upon him, among the answering of supplications, the soundness of visions, and other things that Allah, glorified is He, willed, a great matter, to the extent that He indicated to him an indication about which there is no doubt, and since all the signs were equal in their power to indicate, though some of them were stronger than others, He said: ﴿Our signs﴾. He is Bal'am, without doubt, for the sake of precedence and sequence. It is also said: he was a man whom Musa, peace be upon him, sent to the king of Madyan, and he bribed him, so he followed his religion, and people were tempted by him. It is also said: he is Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt al-Thaqafi, about whom the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "His poetry believed, and his heart disbelieved." This was said by Abdullah ibn Amr, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, and Zayd ibn Aslam. It is also said: he is Abu Amir the monk, whom the Prophet (ﷺ) named the wicked one. It is also said: it was revealed concerning the hypocrites among the People of the Book, who knew the Prophet (ﷺ) and then denied him.

Since what emboldened them against His greatness, glorified is He, was the favour He had bestowed upon them by giving them the Book, thinking that He would not thereafter make them wretched, He instilled fear in them by explaining that the cause of this wretchedness for him was the giving of the signs. So He said: ﴿Then he withdrew from them﴾, i.e., he departed from them by stripping off, just as the snake sheds its skin. This was because, being one whose supplication was answered, the king of his time asked him to pray against Musa and his people, and he refused. The king kept urging him until he opposed the command of Allah in following the desire of his own soul. Thereupon Satan gained mastery over him and advised him to send to them women adorned, and to order them not to refuse anyone. So Allah made him wretched. This is the meaning of: ﴿So Satan overtook him﴾, i.e., his deception overtook him, and he became his companion (p-158). ﴿So he was﴾, i.e., as a consequence of Satan overtaking him, he became ﴿among the deviators﴾, i.e., the astray, those who follow the desires of their souls. In this story He used the expression ﴿recite﴾ [al-Ankabut: 45] rather than ﴿and ask them about﴾ [al-A'raf: 163], as in the case of the town earlier, because this report is one they love to mention, since his being stripped of the signs was for their sake, so it is an honour for them. Had He asked them about it, they would have hastened to report it and would not have hesitated. Therefore his (ﷺ) recitation of it after that, of what was revealed concerning him, does not fall in the place of what he would have reported to them had he told them of it beforehand. Perhaps the greatest purpose of this verse and the one before it is to argue against their claim in their saying: ﴿We shall be forgiven﴾ [al-A'raf: 169], by what they themselves profess, so it is of the mode of argument by obligation, as if it were said: You yourselves say that whoever associates partners with Allah is not forgiven, because he abandoned what proofs were set up for him, to the extent that you say: ﴿There is no blame on us regarding the unlettered﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 75] on that account. Why then do you extend forgiveness to yourselves for abandoning what the particular covenant was taken from you regarding, while you have narrowed it for others in abandoning what the general covenant was taken from them regarding? That is nothing but mere desire. If you say: the matter of the foundation of monotheism is greater, so it is not to be analogized upon, it is said to you: Did not the One worshipped forbid all of them? And even on supposition, it is recorded in your Book that the affair of Bal'am was that he went astray, and he had been greater than your rabbis. We gave him the signs without any intermediary messenger, and the cause of his destruction, as you know, and his departure from the bond of the religion, and the permitting of his blood, was his counsel to the king of his time that he send (p-159) women to the army of the Children of Israel, adorned and not refusing anyone who desired them. That is among the subsidiary matters, which are lighter than the matter of wealth. So you have been exposed in your lie in your saying: ﴿We shall be forgiven﴾ [al-A'raf: 169], and that you followed in it nothing but desire, as Bal'am followed it. So consider what was done to him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 176:

Since this context could mislead one whose foot has not been firmly planted in faith into thinking that Satan has an independent influence in leading people astray, He negated that out of zeal for this station, in the aspect of majesty, and said: ﴿And had We willed﴾, meaning: had We willed to raise him through them, by the greatness We possess, whoever approaches its precincts without permission is destroyed, ﴿We would have raised him﴾, meaning: in rank, a lasting elevation, ﴿by them﴾, meaning: by the verses, so that he would continue to act upon them.

Since He attached the matter to the will, as an alert that the will is the true cause, and that what He does not will does not happen, and the implied sense was: "But We did not will that, and We willed for him disbelief, so We made him dwell [on the earth]," and so on to the end, He expressed it this way to teach good manners in attributing good to God and evil to other than Him, even though all of it is His creation, and to protect the minds of the weak from the impression of deficiency or from introducing confusion. He said, attributing the deficiency to him: ﴿but he clung﴾, meaning: he did the act of one who causes perpetuity, the khuld (perpetuity, lasting), and brought it about, ﴿to the earth﴾, meaning: he threw himself down into this world with a throw, out of greed for its animal pleasures and the appetites of the soul, ﴿and followed﴾, meaning: a strong following (p-160) ﴿his desire﴾, so he turned away from holding fast to what God had given him of the verses, giving precedence to the call of his self over the call of his spirit. This is because the heart, which is the outcome of both in the world of command, has two faces: one toward the lofty, spiritual Spirit, which is the father, and to which belongs the masculinity suited to elevation; and one toward the self, which is the animal spirit, which is the mother, and to which belongs the affinity to the earth through femininity, and through the fact that its origin is from dust, which by the arrangement of its natural constitution has the property of settling. The sense is: he lowered his self with a great lowering, because We did not will to raise him by what We had given him of the verses, but rather We made it a burden upon him. So let no one be deceived by what he has been given of knowledge, or what he has gathered of glories and subtleties, for the lesson lies in the endings. And for Us, after that, is that We do what We will.

Since this was his condition, there followed from it the statement of the Exalted: ﴿So his likeness﴾, meaning: together with what he was given of knowledge, in following mere desire without evidence, after the command to oppose desire, ﴿is like the likeness of the dog﴾, meaning: in the state of constant panting.

Since [as if] it was said: "His likeness in what states?", He said: in its being ﴿if you attack it, it pants, or if you leave it, it pants﴾, meaning: if you drive it away. So if the attack on it obliges it to think that its panting, because of the fatigue it has exerted in that, turns you away from it, then its panting in ease, so you will know then that it has no cause except following desire. So the follower of desire is like the dog, as He explained. The example of this one who has cast off [the verses] is the ignorant one, who cannot be imagined to follow anything other than desire, for he follows desire even while being given the verses; so after casting them off, it is more fitting. Thus the likeness of such a one has been made clear as being the likeness of the dog, not the likeness of such a one to the dog. This story shows (p-161) that whoever has more of God's blessings toward him, when he turns away from Him, his distance from God is greater and more immense.

Since the two likenesses have been established, and each of them applies to the condition of every denier, the result is His saying: ﴿That﴾, meaning: each of the two likenesses, ﴿is the likeness of the people﴾, meaning: the mighty, what they attempt, ﴿who denied Our signs﴾, meaning: in that their abandonment of them is merely by mere desire, because the signs have such manifestness and greatness through their attribution to Us that it is not hidden from anyone who has even a little insight. ﴿So relate the stories﴾, meaning: so inform with the great information by which you have traced the sites of events and the traces of persons, so that you leave no confusion in any of them for everyone who hears you, from among the Jews and others. This is the verbal noun of qassa al-shay', when one follows its trace and investigates thoroughly. ﴿That perhaps they may reflect﴾, meaning: so that their condition may be that of one whose reflection on these signs is hoped for, so they will know that he does not bring the like of them without a teacher from among people except a prophet, and that will return them to the right course, as a warning against the likeness of this one's condition.

Having made clear that the likeness of the dog, which has acquired from the thing it is compared to such baseness and filth that none knows its full extent except Allah Most High, is the likeness of those who deny Our signs, He brought forth, as an emphatic rebuke and warning against them, His words: ﴿Evil is the example of the people﴾, i.e., the example of the people ﴿who denied Our signs﴾. That is, had they not been ones for whom it was fitting, in their conduct, that this example should be sent down upon them, it would still have been the greatest deterrent for anyone possessing even the least degree of honour; for they descended from what (p-162) is due to whoever follows them of greatness to what this example has shown of baseness. How much more so, when they harm their own souls by this and harm no one but themselves. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿and themselves﴾, i.e., exclusively, ﴿they used to wrong﴾, i.e., this was in their nature and innate disposition, which none other than Allah can change.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 178 (part 1 of 2):

When that became a cause of wonder for those who turn away from the path after it had been made so clear and so thoroughly explained, he said, as an answer to one who seems to have said: "Then what is wrong with them that they do not believe?", elaborating on His saying: ﴿And had We willed, We would have raised him by them﴾ [al-A'raf: 176], ﴿Whomever Allah guides﴾, i.e., whoever Allah creates guidance in his heart, the Supreme King with whom no one has any command, ﴿he is the one guided﴾, i.e., not anyone else.

Since this was in the context of proving that most of creation is destined for ruin through wickedness and breaking the covenant, he made ﴿the one guided﴾ singular, looking to the wording of ﴿whom﴾ (man), and he made the one who is led astray plural, looking to its meaning, so he said: ﴿And whoever He leaves astray, those are they who are﴾, i.e., the distant, the hateful, specifically and no others, ﴿the losers﴾, since there is no action at all for anyone other than Him. The verse is a summary (fadhlaka) of what came before. How excellent its conclusion with loss, as an admonition to one who abandons the Hereafter by devoting himself to the profits of this world and its perishable goods; then following it with the creation of Hell, of whom none are more losing.

Mention of the story of Balaam from the Torah. In the Fourth Book of it, after relating their fighting against Sihon, king of the Amorites, it says:

And the Moabites feared greatly (p-163) the people, because they saw that it was a great nation; and the Moabites were distressed and their hearts trembled with fear of the children of Israel. And the king of Moab said to the elders of Midian:

"Know that this assembly will devour our fields and will leave no one but destroy him, and will devour everyone around us as the ox devours the grass of the earth." At that time the king of the Moabites was Balak son of Zippor. He sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor, the diviner and interpreter of dreams, who used to dwell by the bank of the river near the land of the children of Ammon, to call him to himself so that he might seek his help:

"I inform you that a people has come out of the land of Egypt, and it has covered the face of the whole earth, and they have camped against our mountains. So I beg you to come and curse this people, for it is stronger and mightier than us, perhaps we shall be able to fight it and destroy it from the face of the land, for I know that the one you bless is blessed, and the one you curse is cursed." The elders of Moab and the elders of Midian departed, with gifts and rewards in their hands, and came to Balaam and told him the words of Balak. He said to them:

"Stay here tonight, and I will tell you what the Lord says." The princes of Moab stayed with Balaam. The angel of God came to Balaam and said to him:

"Who are these men who have come to you?"

Balaam said to the angel:

"Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, sent to me and said:

'A people has come out of the land of Egypt and has filled the face of the earth; so come to us that you may curse it, perhaps I shall be able to fight it and destroy it.'" The angel said to Balaam:

"Do not go with the people, and do not curse the nation, for it is blessed." Balaam said in the morning to the leaders of (p-164) Balak:

"Go to your master, for the Lord has not willed to let me go with you." The leaders of Moab rose and came to Balak and said to him:

"Balaam has not desired to come with us." Balak again sent messengers more numerous and more honourable than the first, [and they came to Balaam and said to him:

"Thus says Balak son of Zippor:

Do not refuse to come to me,] for I will greatly honour you and reward you, and whatever you say to me I will do; and come to us [that you may curse for us] this people." Balaam answered the messengers of Balak, saying:

"Even if Balak gave me his house full of gold and silver, I could not go beyond the word of my Lord and my God, nor deviate from any of His words, small or great. So stay here with me tonight as well, until I see what the angel of God tells me about your matter." The revelation of God came to Balaam at night and said to him:

"If these men have come to call you, arise and go with them, but beware, do nothing except what I tell you."

Balaam rose in the morning, saddled his she-ass and went with the leaders of Moab. The angel of the Lord stood in the way as an adversary to him. The she-ass saw the angel of God standing in the way with his sword drawn in his hand, so she turned aside from the way and went into the field. Balaam struck her to turn her back to the way. The angel of the Lord stood in a narrow path between two vineyards, and the she-ass saw the angel of the Lord and pressed against the wall and crushed Balaam's foot against the wall (p-165), so he struck her again. Then the angel of the Lord came back and stood in a narrow place where there was no room to turn right or left. When she saw the angel of the Lord she lay down under Balaam, so Balaam's anger burned and he struck the ass with a staff. The Lord opened the mouth of the ass and she said to Balaam:

"What have I done to you that you have struck me three times?"

Balaam said:

"Because you have mocked me; if there were a sword in my hand I would have killed you now." She said:

"Am I not your she-ass that you have ridden since your youth until today? Did I ever do such a thing before?" He said to her:

"No."

The Lord uncovered Balaam's eyes, and he saw the angel of God standing in the way with his sword drawn in his hand, so he bowed and fell on his face prostrate. The angel of the Lord said to him:

"Why have you struck your ass three times? I came out to be an adversary to you, because you have taken a path contrary to my command. When the ass saw me she turned aside from me three times; if she had not turned aside from me, I would have killed you and spared her." Balaam said to the angel of the Lord:

"I have sinned and done wrong; I did not know that you were standing against me in the way. So now, if my going is displeasing to you, I will turn back." The angel of the Lord said to Balaam:

"Go with the men, but beware that you do nothing except what I tell you!"

So Balaam went, and Balak heard and came out to meet him, and Balak said:

"Did you not come to me?" He said:

"I have indeed come to you now. Do you think that I am able to say anything except the word that God puts on my tongue? That is what I shall speak." (p-166) When it was the next day, Balak went to Balaam and took him up to the house of Baal the idol, and from there he saw the farthest parts of the camp of the children of Israel. Balaam said to Balak:

"Build for me here seven altars, and prepare for me seven bulls and seven rams." Balak did as Balaam told him, and Balak offered the rams and the bulls upon the altar as a sacrifice. Balaam said to Balak:

"Stand here by your offerings while I go [myself, perhaps the Lord will reveal to me what He desires, and I will declare to you what He reveals], so he went." God appeared and inspired him with a word, and said to him:

"Go to Balak and say this word to him." He came to him while he stood by his offerings and all the princes of Moab with him. Balaam raised his voice with his parables and said:

"Balak king of the Moabites has brought me from Aram, which is in the east, and said to me:

'Come, curse Jacob and destroy the House of Israel.' How shall I curse whom God has not cursed? How shall I destroy whom the Lord does not wish to destroy? For I see him from the tops of the mountains, and I look at him from the hills; and behold, he is a people dwelling alone, not reckoned among the nations. Who can count the dust of Jacob, or number the fourth part of the children of Israel? Let my soul die the death of the righteous, and let my end be like theirs." Balak said to Balaam:

"I summoned you to curse my enemies, (p-167) and behold, you have blessed them and kept blessing them." He answered and said:

"Whatever the Lord puts into my mind and speaks through my tongue, that I must observe, and that is what I shall speak."

Balak said to him:

"Come with me to another place from which you can see them; you shall see only their last part and not see them all, and curse them for me from there." He took him to the field of Zophim, set him at the top of the hill, built there seven altars, and offered the bulls and rams upon them. Balaam said:

"Stand here by your offerings while I go, and see what is said." The Lord appeared to Balaam and put a word in his mouth and said to him:

"Go to Balak and tell him this word." He came to him while he stood by his offerings, with the princes of Moab with him. Balaam raised his voice with his parables and said:

"Arise, Balak, and hear; give ear to my testimony, O son of Zippor! Know that God is not like a man who lies, nor like a son of man who changes his mind. When He has said a thing, will He not do it? When He has spoken, will He not fulfil it? Behold, I have received a command to bless; He has blessed, and I cannot reverse it. He has not beheld iniquity in Jacob, nor has He seen perversity in Israel. The Lord their God is with them, and the shout of a king is among them. God brought them out of Egypt; he is for them like the strength of a wild ox. Surely there is no enchantment against Jacob, nor divination against Israel; now it shall be said of Jacob and of Israel, what God has done! Behold, a people rises like a lioness, and like a lion it lifts itself up; it shall not lie down until it devours the prey and drinks the blood of the slain." Balak said to Balaam:

"Neither curse them at all nor bless them at all." Balaam answered Balak:

"Did I not tell you, 'All that the Lord speaks, that I must do'?" Balak said:

"Come now, let me take you to another place; perhaps it will please God that you may curse them for me from there." He took him to the top of Peor, which overlooks the wilderness, and he commanded him to offer the same sacrifices as before. Balaam saw that the Lord was pleased to bless Israel, so he did not go, as he had done on other occasions, to seek omens, but turned his face toward the wilderness and lifted his eyes; he saw Israel encamped tribe by tribe, and the Spirit of God came upon him. He raised his voice with his parables and said:

"The oracle of Balaam son of Beor, the oracle of the man whose eye was opened; the oracle of him who hears the words of God and sees the vision of the Almighty, who falls down with eyes uncovered: How good are your tents, O Jacob, your dwelling places, O Israel! Like valleys that stretch out, like gardens beside a river, like aloes planted by the Lord, like cedars beside the waters. Water shall flow from his buckets, and his seed shall be in many waters; his king shall be higher than Agag, and his kingdom shall be exalted. God brings him out of Egypt; he has the strength of a wild ox. He shall consume the nations, his adversaries, and shall break their bones and pierce them with his arrows. He couches, he lies down like a lion, and like a lioness; who dares rouse him? Blessed be everyone who blesses you, and cursed be everyone who curses you." Then Balak's anger burned against Balaam, and he struck his hands together and said:

"I called you to curse my enemies, and behold, you have blessed them these three times. Now flee to your place. I had intended to honour you greatly, but behold, the Lord has kept you back from honour." Balaam answered Balak:

"Did I not tell your messengers whom you sent to me that even if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the word of the Lord, to do either good or bad of my own will? What the Lord says, that I will speak. And now, behold, I am going to my people; come, let me advise you what this people will do to your people in the latter days." He raised his voice with his parables and said:

"The oracle of Balaam son of Beor, the oracle of the man whose eye was opened; the oracle of him who hears the words of God and knows the knowledge of the Most High, who sees the vision of the Almighty, who falls down with eyes uncovered: I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near. A star shall come out of Jacob, and a scepter shall rise out of Israel, and shall crush the forehead of Moab and destroy all the sons of Sheth. Edom shall be a possession, Seir also, his enemies, shall be his possession, while Israel does valiantly. And one out of Jacob shall have dominion and destroy the survivors of the city." — and similar words, containing that which would be a cause of his stripping away from the signs. But the commentators mention that he advised him to mix the women of his land with the children of Israel, adorned and not refusing whoever of them desired them, so that they would commit fornication with them, whereupon the plague would descend upon them; and that happened to them. This is the correct view, because the allusion to it will come in the Torah at the conquest of Midian, in his saying:

"Why have you spared the women? They were the cause of the children of Israel's stumbling, by the word and counsel of Balaam" (p-170). And that will come shortly. As for what is mentioned there of revelation, it is to be understood as a dream or something else that is fitting. Then he said:

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 7, verse 178 (part 2 of 2)

Bil'am rose and returned to his own land, and Balaq also returned to his house. The Children of Israel settled in Shittim, and the people began to commit fornication with the daughters of Moab. They invited the people to the sacrifices of their gods, and the people ate of their sacrifices and prostrated to their gods. The Children of Israel joined themselves to the worship of Ba'lyun the idol, so the wrath of God intensified against the Children of Israel. The Lord said to Musa:

"Take all the Children of Israel and expose them." Musa said:

"Let every man among you kill everyone who has sinned and prostrated to Ba'lyun." Then a man from the Children of Israel came, openly and boldly, before his brothers, without being ashamed. He entered upon a Midianite woman while Musa and the Children of Israel were weeping at the door of the Tent of Meeting (Qubbat al-Amid). Finhas ibn Eleazar ibn Harun, the rabbi (ḥabr), saw him. He rose from the assembly in anger for God, took a spear in his hand, entered the tent of the two of them, and thrust them through with the spear, killing them both. Then the spreading plague was lifted from the Children of Israel. The number of those who died in the sudden plague was twenty-four thousand.

The Lord spoke to Musa and said to him:

"Finhas has turned My wrath away from the Children of Israel and was zealous for God among them, and He purified the Children of Israel." The name of the slain man who was killed along with the Midianite woman was Zimri ibn Salu, who was a leader [in the tribe of Shim'un.
