(p-171) The Midianite woman was Kozbi, daughter of Zur, and her father] was one of the chiefs of the people of Midian. Some exegetes (mufassirun) said:

"He went out raising the spear toward the sky, having leaned with his elbow on his side, and he propped the spear against his beard. Therefore, from that place the Children of Israel give the son of Finhas, from every sacrifice, the foreleg, the jaw, the stomach, and the firstborn from all their property and their persons, because he was the firstborn of Izar ibn Harun."

Then the Lord spoke to Musa and said to him: "Harass the people of Midian and destroy them as they harassed you, and they deceived you." Then He said: "Then the Lord spoke to Musa and said to him: Indeed I am avenging against the Midianites what they did among the Children of Israel. Then you will take vengeance on your people." Then Musa said to the people: "Let some of you arm themselves for war, so that they may avenge the Lord against the Midianites, and let them be twelve thousand." Musa selected a thousand from the Children of Israel from each tribe, twelve champions armed, and sent them out. He appointed as their commander Finhas ibn Eleazar the rabbi, and with him were the vessels of holiness and the horns he blew. They prevailed over Midian as the Lord had commanded Musa, and they killed every male in it, and they killed the kings of Midian along with the slain. Bil'am ibn Ba'ur was also killed with them in the battle. The Children of Israel took captive the women of Midian, plundered their livestock, seized all their beasts and property, and destroyed all the villages and dwellings. They brought what they had plundered to Musa. Musa went out with all the leaders of the assembly and met them outside the camp. Musa became angry with the chiefs of the priests and the commanders of thousands and hundreds who had come from the battle, and he said to them:

"Why have you spared the females? They were a stumbling block to the Children of Israel through the word and counsel of Bil'am. They led astray, deceived, and rebelled against the Lord in the matter of Fa'ghur." (In the Septuagint version: "These ones were a thing for the Children of Israel, for the people of Bil'am, that they should turn away and disregard the word of the Lord on account of Fa'ghur," [so the wrath struck the congregation of the Lord. (And in the other version: "death prevailed over the congregation of the Lord")] suddenly.) "Now kill every male among the boys, and every woman who has reached maturity and has known a man, kill her. But spare all the women who have not known men. As for you, camp outside the camp for seven days," and so on to the end of what passed earlier in the Asar (Numbers' passages).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 179:

When these stories came to an end and revealed that most of creation is destined for ruin, he stated this explicitly, saying, swearing an oath because it is hardly believed that a human being could be more astray than the beasts, and conjoining it to what is implied by the sense: these whose accounts we have related to you, We have created for Hell: ﴿And indeed﴾, by My might and My majesty, ﴿We have created﴾, that is, We brought into being by Our greatness, produced, dispersed and spread out, ﴿for Hell many﴾, that is, and We drove them (p-173) toward it, and did not place between them and it any barrier.

Since they used to exalt the jinn and fear them, and go astray through them, he began with them, saying: ﴿of the jinn﴾, that is, by their setting themselves up as gods, through their misleading of mankind into adorning the worship of other than God. So in reality they are the ones worshipped, not the stones and the like. ﴿And of mankind﴾, that is, through their worship of those who are not fit for it. It is known that the verse is suitable to be conjoined to the sentence preceding it, so it is a summary (fadhlaka) of what came before.

Since it is as though it had been said, "What is wrong with them, that they accepted for themselves the path of Hell?", it is said: ﴿They have hearts with which they do not understand﴾. Since the context is that of reflection, he began with the hearts, saying: ﴿hearts with which they do not understand﴾, that is, the understanding (fiqh) they were charged with, which is contemplation of the proofs of tawhid (Oneness of God), the establishment of prophethood, and what branches from these, and which is the understanding that brings felicity (al-fiqh al-musid). Anything other than it is counted as absence, because it did not benefit them the benefit that was truly intended. How excellent is the expression "understanding" in the context of establishing proofs, among which is the sending of messengers and the sending down of books.

Since sight is more general than hearing, for the small child who does not understand speech benefits from it, and likewise everyone in that condition, he put it first, saying: ﴿And they have eyes﴾. Since useful sight in the enduring Hereafter is not consequent upon them, he negated their sight, even though they were the sharpest of people in sight, saying: ﴿with which they do not see﴾, that is, the signs visible, seeing with reflection and consideration. ﴿And they have ears﴾. Since no beneficial result follows from hearing them, he negated it in the same manner as before, saying: ﴿with which they do not hear﴾, that is, the signs heard and what indicates them, hearing with remembrance and contemplation. When these meanings were stripped from them, the result was: ﴿Those﴾, that is, the remote ones from human meanings, ﴿are like cattle﴾, that is, in lacking understanding. Since they had added to that the neglect of the benefit of hearing and sight, he said: ﴿Rather they are more astray﴾, because they are either obstinate or ignorant of what harms and benefits them. Cattle flee when they hear a disagreeable sound, seeing with their own eyes that it entails harm to them, and they seek what benefits them of water and pasture and head toward it. Cattle have no capacity for what follows from these faculties of understanding. But these, despite their capacity for that, neglected it, [so they descended a rank below them, just as whoever seeks perfection and strives for it, amid the conflict of desires, rises above the rank of the angels by what he endures of struggle].

Since they shared with cattle this heedlessness and exceeded them in it, that produced, by way of definitive restriction: ﴿Those﴾, that is, the remote, the hateful, ﴿they are﴾, that is, exclusively, ﴿the heedless﴾, not the cattle, for although cattle are heedless of what is intended for them, they are not eternal in punishment, and so they did not share with them in blindness and deafness to what benefits them, nor in heedlessness of the everlasting loss. The verse has thus indicated the preference of man over the angel, as the Surah of al-Tin requires, because he was placed in his creation as a middle state between the angel, who is pure intellect, and the animal, which is pure appetite. If his intellect predominates, he is higher, by what he treats of the struggle against desires, and he is in: ﴿the best of stature﴾ [al-Tin: 4]. If his appetite predominates, he is lower than the animal, by what he has wasted of his intellect, and he becomes ﴿the lowest of the low﴾ [al-Tin: 5].

(p-175) Since this [i.e., the preceding argument] yielded that they have the worst names, and that their worshipped objects are worse than these, he connected to it, to repel the notion of one who imagines, through the judgment of misguidance and the sending to Hell, something unfitting, and to alert that what necessitates entry into Hell is heedlessness of the remembrance of God and calling upon Him, [His saying]: ﴿And to God belong the most beautiful names﴾. That is: to the Supreme King, who alone encompasses all attributes of perfection. ﴿The names﴾ [and since the ism (name), when its relation is considered, has the meaning of a ṣifa (attribute), the feminine is used in His saying]: ﴿the most beautiful﴾, that is, all of them, by His being characterized, to the exclusion of others, by attributes of perfection, each of which is the finest and most beautiful of things, and by His being exalted above admixtures of deficiency and marks of createdness. Thus all His acts are wise. [And] He was specified with that only because other things are contingent, since they are subject to change, and every contingent being is in need, and the least that it needs is a determiner that determines its existence. By this we know the existence of the determiner, and we know that its determining is by way of soundness and choice, not necessity, for otherwise the world would have endured by its own permanence. By this His power is established, and His acts are firm; His knowledge is established, so His life, hearing, sight, speech, will and oneness are established, for otherwise there would occur conflict, and then disorder. So knowledge of His exalted attributes is not on one level but in graded order. It is known from this that perfection belongs to Him essentially, whereas for others their perfection is through Him, and in themselves they are drowned in the sea of annihilation and fallen into the depths of deficiency. ﴿So call upon Him by them﴾, that is: describe Him, name Him, and ask Him by them, ﴿that you may be saved from Hell and attain everything whose outcome is praiseworthy; for when the heart is heedless of the remembrance of God, it turns to the world and its appetites, and so falls into the fire of greed and the frost of deprivation, and it does not cease (p-176) from desire to desire until no deliverer remains for it. But when it turns to the remembrance, it is delivered from the fires of calamities, and it perceives through knowledge of God until it is freed from the bondage of appetites, so it becomes free and thus is made happy with all desired things. And the multiplicity of names does not detract from tawhid; rather it indicates the greatness of the Named.

﴿And leave﴾, that is: abandon in a state of withdrawal, ﴿those who deviate﴾, that is: incline away from what has been set as limit for them [by adding, so that they resemble (others), or by subtracting, so that they nullify], ﴿concerning His names﴾, that is: they apply them to other than Him, by naming an idol "god", which then necessitates that they apply to it all attributes of God. Thus they have deviated in part in act and in the rest by necessary implication. Or [deviation is] by naming Him with what He has not permitted; and what He has not permitted is sometimes permitted in general, such as a harmful one, which may not be mentioned except together with a beneficial one; and sometimes not, such as applying "Father" to Him, or "body"; likewise everything that gives an impression of deficiency is not the best. Because some of His derived forms have been applied to Him, such as "Teacher" from the name ʿAlīm, it is not permissible to say it for that reason; likewise, because of their love for them, it is not permissible to say, for example, "O Creator of worms and monkeys". Likewise it is not permissible to mention a name whose meaning the speaker does not know, even if people understand from it praise, as some Bedouin say: "O white-faced one! O father of noble deeds!" For all that is deviation. This verb is used unaugmented, as one says "laḥada fī kadhā" and "alḥada fīhi" with the same meaning, namely: to turn away from the truth and to introduce into it what is not part of it. Abū Ḥayyān transmitted this from Ibn al-Sikkīt. And the Imam Abū al-Qāsim ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar ibn al-Qaṭṭāʿ said in the Kitāb al-Afʿāl: "laḥada al-mayyit laḥdan and alḥadahu": he dug the grave for him; "ilā al-shay', ʿanhu, fī al-dīn": he inclined; and it was read with both forms in that manner.

Since it was as though it had been said: "What will be done to those who deviate?"—and the intent of the threat is the imposition of the requital, not its being from a specific source—he said, with the passive construction: ﴿They will be recompensed﴾, that is: in this world and the Hereafter, by a promise without breach, ﴿for what they used to do﴾, that is: by their innate natures; ﴿they will be made to do﴾, that is: there will be done to them of kinds of humiliation and punishment what necessitates describing them with the most vile attributes, the opposite of what they used to hear in this world from those who were near to them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 181:

When Allah, exalted is He, informed about the creation of Hell from the two kinds (of people), the listener was eager to know the state of those remaining from them. So He stated the news about them plainly, conjoining it to ﴿And We had certainly created﴾ [Al-A'raf: 179], and using *min* (مِنِ التَّبْعِيضِيَّةِ), the partitive *min*, to indicate their being a portion, in confirmation of His saying: ﴿And We found most of them to be defiantly disobedient﴾ [Al-A'raf: 102]. ﴿And among those We created﴾, meaning, by what We possess of greatness, ﴿a nation﴾, meaning a community that recognised the one fit to be followed and guided by, so it sought him and took light from his lights, and thus it became itself fit to be sought and to be followed.

When the word "nation" conveyed this, He made it explicit in His saying: ﴿who guide by the truth﴾, meaning the established truth to which reality conforms, ﴿and by it﴾, meaning by the truth alone, ﴿they act justly﴾ (p-178), meaning they make matters balanced, with no excess in any of them beyond what is proper and no deficiency, because We granted them success and uncovered from their insights the veil of heedlessness which We had imposed upon those (others). Most of the exegetes (al-mufassirun) said: they are the nation of Muhammad (ﷺ). Some of them narrated this from the Prophet (ﷺ), and after the people of Musa (peace be upon him) had been specified, He left the matter vague out of exaltation of them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 182:

When he had explained the state of the guiding and rightly guided, and the original context was that of the misguided and those who misguide, he followed it with the remainder of the discourse concerning them, in a manner that hints that the cause of guidance is divine success (tawfiq). So he said, conjoining it to its implied supposition: "Thus We raise their affair and make their remembrance good." ﴿And those who denied﴾, meaning they attributed falsehood to the Messengers because of their bringing ﴿Our signs﴾, as is witnessed of their magnitude, ﴿We will lead them step by step﴾, meaning We will bring them down and draw them near, by a promise that does not fail, to what We intend for them of great evil, degree by degree (istidraj), because whenever they commit a transgression We lavish upon them a blessing, and when they perform an act of obedience We withhold from them the bestowal, or We strike them with the whip of retribution. Thus they suppose that sins are the cause of blessings, and so they slip away from the religion. Therefore He said: ﴿from where they do not know﴾, meaning they commit what is astonishing to approach, let alone to engage in and endure, for anyone with the least insight, until what We intend of sins from them is complete. This is among the proofs of ﴿I will turn away from My signs﴾ [al-A'raf: 146]. [And He came] in istidraj with the particle of greatness, and in imla' (respite) with the pronoun of the singular, so He said: ﴿And I give them respite﴾ [al-A'raf: 183], meaning: I grant them a respite, by a firm promise, for a long time, and I extend to them while they disobey, until they suppose that Allah loves them, so that they increase in that, because they do nothing except by My will, and they cannot escape Me. He did not bring the two on a single pattern, because istidraj occurs through an intermediary and without one. So it is as if He said: "I will lead them step by step by Myself, without intermediary, at times, and through whomever among My servants and soldiers the blessings are made available to them by his hand, at other times." As for imla', which is the prolonging of the term, it cannot be conceived except from Allah, exalted is He.

Since this (the persistent disbelievers' condition) necessarily leads them to persist in sins until they reach what has been decreed for them of the Fire, He said, beginning a new statement: ﴿Indeed, My plan is firm﴾, meaning: My action, whose outward appearance is elevation and whose inner reality is loss; its outward appearance is kindness, and its inner reality is abandonment, ﴿is firm﴾, meaning: strong and powerful, such that no one can sever it.

The Imam (al-Razi) said, after an interpretation by the Mu'tazilah, which their insistence on the obligation of "ri'ayat al-aslah" (the duty of God to do what is best for His servants) compelled them to: "I am greatly astonished at the Mu'tazilah. They see the Qur'an as an endless sea filled with these verses, and the compelling rational proofs agree with them, and then they are content, in interpreting them (i.e., regarding the statement that He, exalted is He, wills evil), with these weak aspects. However, my knowledge that what God willed has come to pass removes this astonishment."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 184:

Since the context from the beginning of the surah was about warning them (al-indhar), and since the soundness of the warning requires the soundness of the message (al-risalah), and [the surah] concluded with the matter of gradual enticement (al-istidraj), and they had committed sins that none would dare to commit except one whose insight is obliterated, and they held that whoever said that they were in a bad state—despite the manifest blessings they were in—was mad (majnun), and the reasoning (al-taqdir) served as proof of the soundness of the istidraj: [the verse is] ﴿Have they not reflected?﴾ Consider how they proceed in what no rational person would approve for himself: their worship of a stone, their arrogance toward the most perfect of mankind, their describing him with madness, their describing the most excellent speech as sorcery and lies, and other things that anger the One in whose hand alone is benefit and harm, and yet He continually bestows blessings upon them and repels calamities from them. Is that not istidraj? He says, rebuking them, linking it (ʿatfan) to what the context guides toward, and the linking to something not previously mentioned implies its supposed antecedent: ﴿Have they not reflected?﴾ That is, let them exercise their thoughts and examine the arrangement of premises, so that they would know that no criticism that would produce doubt in any respect is directed at them. He clarified the intended meaning of this reflection and specified it by saying: ﴿their companion﴾, that is, the one whose experience they have had for a long time, because he is the most intellectually sound among them and the most excellent in character. He did not say "my messenger" or the like, lest their obstinate ones say what is not hidden. He went to the extreme in negation and said: ﴿there is no madness in him﴾, that is, no state of any of the states of madness.

When He negated that there was in him anything of what they attributed to him and fabricated against him, and thus his prophethood was established, He confined his matter to warning (al-nidharah), because it is what benefits them, especially since the setting of this surah calls for it. So He said: ﴿He is only a warner﴾, that is, one who fully delivers warning, ﴿clear﴾, that is, one who makes the path clear with a clarity that no one else can reach. Among the proofs of this is the inability of creation to oppose anything he brings, [together with the fact] that he is the best of people in form, the highest of them in character, the most agreeable in companionship, the most pleasing in manner, the most just in conduct, the purest in inner nature, the most noble in deed, the most knowledgeable, the most sound in judgment, the greatest in intellect, the most trustworthy, and the most evidently noble.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 185:

Since the consideration of the matter of prophethood is built upon the establishment of the proofs of tawhid (the oneness of God), and the purpose of warning is to turn back from ilhad (deviation from the truth, or denial), He said, rebuking them for not reflecting on the proofs of tawhid, which turn one away from every evil state: ﴿Have they not considered?﴾ Since the matter was clear, He said: ﴿they consider﴾, meaning a consideration of reflection and taking lesson, and this indicates that it is by insight, not by sight alone, that this is connected. He said, pointing to every atom in which there are abundant proofs: ﴿in the dominion of﴾, and He magnified the matter by saying: ﴿the heavens and the earth﴾, meaning their dominion, which has reached a degree of greatness, a matter dazzling in its outward aspect, which they know, and in its inward aspect, which shines for them but which they do not grasp.

Since the proofs of tawhid cannot be enumerated, for in every atom there is an overpowering demonstration and a brilliant, shining proof, He said: ﴿and what﴾, meaning: and in what ﴿God has created﴾, meaning: in accordance with what He possesses of majesty and beauty ﴿of any thing﴾, meaning: other than these two, so that they may know that He is not able to do any of that, let alone others besides Him, and so that they may be certain that His Book, glory be to Him, is distinct from all His creatures, and thus they may know that it is His attribute, glory be to Him, and His speech. So they will not deviate concerning His names, and will not name anything other than Him by any of them, because of what has become manifest to them of the completeness of His power, the completeness of the incapacity of others with regard to everything, the all-encompassing scope of His knowledge, the utter ignorance of others concerning everything, and so on, until they know, through the greatness of this created order, that He, glory be to Him, is Great; and through His subduing of everything, that He is the Subduer, the Mighty; and through the incapacity of everything with regard to every matter of His command, that He is the Almighty; and through His bestowing of blessings, that He is the Merciful, the Generous, and so on, of His Most Beautiful Names and Highest Attributes, which things speak of through the tongues of their states, and which the souls of created beings narrate even though they have no speech, and which the discourse of governance explains with what it has of perfection. ﴿And that perhaps﴾, meaning: and that they may consider, in apprehension and fear, that it is possible, likely and fitting ﴿that their term has drawn near﴾, meaning: [it has drawn near greatly, ﴿their term﴾, meaning] which there is no doubt in their minds that it will come by one death of these nations whose reports we have already related, as a single soul, or gradually. So they should hasten to believe in Him, fearing the cutting off of the term, in order to be saved from the greatest dread, for every intelligent person, when he deems a danger possible, should consider its consequence and strive to escape it.

Since it has already been mentioned at the beginning of the surah that one must not feel constrained about warning with this Book, and it has become clear through these verses that he (ﷺ) was characterized by warning with it in the truest sense, and it has become clear that the Qur'an is distinct from all created beings, and thus it is established that it is the speech of God, this has led to a denunciation of those who hesitate to believe in it, and to a warning about the arrival of their term before that, so that they fall into what they cannot remedy. This is in a style that indicates that belief after this clarification is not something for which hesitation is permissible, except while waiting for another speech. So He said: ﴿then in what discourse﴾, meaning: what speech that renews, in every occurrence, a clarification of the way out of it ﴿after this﴾, meaning: after this great rank ﴿will they believe?﴾ This verse indicates that belief has two paths: one is transmitted (sam'i, by revelation and report), and the other is rational (aqli, by reason). Al-Harrali said in a book of his on usul al-fiqh (the foundations of jurisprudence): Judgment is only received from the address of God, conveyed through the tongues of His messengers. It is well established and widely known that hearing is one of the means of understanding the address of God which the messengers convey. Likewise, it has also been established for a people of people of intellect that sight and the other senses are also a means of understanding the address of God, by which the rational intellect comprehends the meaning of sending in His created Book, just as the intellect comprehends the meaning of sending from the concept of His spoken speech. And a group of those who understood sending from the visible Book of God and grasped rulings are called the Hanifs, such as Qass ibn Sa'ida and Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) testified for them that each one of them "will be raised as a community on his own." This is because each of them was guided by himself without the message of a guide external to him, but from the Messenger of his existence and his perception of the world. And because he only took up the universal ruling of faith and the obligation of equity with creation from witnessing the creation of God, and he became, along with that, awaiting the confirmation of what he obtained by reason from the heard address of God. Upon this condition, and more complete than it, is the condition of the prophets and the truthful before the descent of revelation upon the Prophet, and before the hearing of his companion of the revelation's arrival. These are the ones who do not hesitate to believe in the Prophet when his call begins. Just as the Prophet does not impose or judge, but conveys from God, so too the reasoning of the intellect does not impose or judge, but conveys from God. Thus the judgment, which is the disposal of the Truth in the actions of creation, is of two kinds: legal (shar'i), meaning taken from the legal sending, and rational (aqli), meaning taken from the rational sending. The conclusion of this is that the visible world expresses the command of God, and everything that expresses is a conveyer. Thus knowledge is a conveyer, meaning of what the one who understands grasps from His speech concerning God. The grammarians said, as Ibn 'Usfur mentioned in his commentary on Abu 'Ali's (al-Farisi's) al-Idah, and likewise others: speech in terminology applies only to a compound utterance, existing or implied, that conveys meaning by convention. He said: They excluded from "utterance" what is called speech linguistically but is not an utterance, such as writing, gesture, what is in the self, and what is understood from the state of a thing. Al-Harrali said: such as the state of one who is embarrassed or angry; and by action, such as pointing with the hand and counting with the fingers, and by the traces of action, such as crafts and works; and by the utterance which the heart articulates to the outer part of the tongue; and by the traces of inscriptions by which the concept of an utterance is represented, which is writing. End.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 186:

When all of that is among the most astonishing of wonders, its concluding statement comes as a decisive cause (ta'lil) for what preceded it, namely their turning away from what should not be turned away from, as evidence that the matter rests in no hand but that of its Sender, glorified is He. His saying: ﴿Whomever Allah leaves astray﴾, i.e., the One who possesses all greatness, ﴿there is no guide﴾ at all ﴿for him﴾ in any way whatsoever. Since the singular form indicates that every individual is in His grip, and the intended sense was: rather, he persists in his misguidance, and He joined to it with a plural pronoun, indicating that their gathering avails them nothing against Allah, He said: ﴿and He leaves them﴾, i.e., He abandons them in a disgraceful state. He expressed it with the adverbial form (zarf) to indicate the encompassing of His judgment over them, so He said: ﴿in their transgression﴾, i.e., their overstepping of the bounds, while they are ﴿wandering blindly﴾, i.e., bewildered and vacillating in misguidance, not knowing a path and not understanding a proof.

When he had explained tawhid (the oneness of God), prophethood, qada' (divine decree) and qadar (divine measure), he followed them with ma'ad (the return and the afterlife), so that the four principal themes, which are the mothers of the Qur'an's themes, would be complete. This explains what this discourse contains of their dullness in blindness and their wandering in associating likenesses, through His words: ﴿They ask you﴾, that is, repeatedly, ﴿about the Hour﴾ (al-sa'ah), that is, about its time, asking in mockery, ﴿When will be its mooring?﴾, that is, when is the time of the settling and fixing of its weight. Al-mursa can be a verbal noun, a time, or a place, from "rasat al-safinah," meaning the ship became fixed with the forked anchor. This was a clarification of their blindness, for they fell into error in two ways: by asking about something whose other aspects were more important for them, and by making it a matter of mockery despite the proofs established concerning it. He will repeat this in this surah. The fitting course for them would have been, instead of asking about it, to guard against it through righteous deeds.

Since the question about the Hour was first general and then specific to its time, the answer came generally about it, in His words: ﴿Say: Its knowledge is only﴾, that is, the knowledge of the time of its settling and of other matters, (p-186) ﴿with my Lord﴾, that is, the One who has graciously brought it about for me, so that He may bestow favour upon those who follow me and take vengeance on those who abandon me. No one of His creation has been informed of it, and He will not bring it about except at the best and most beneficial times for me. Concealing it is more beneficial for creation, because that magnifies its matter and makes it more awe-inspiring, so it becomes more conducive to obedience, more restraining from disobedience, and nearer to repentance. Then it was specified with respect to time by His words, indicating that it has signs preceding it: ﴿None will reveal it﴾, that is, none will make it clear with complete clarity, ﴿at its time except Him﴾.

Since He had indicated the weight of the Hour by the word "mooring," and since when a thing is unknown in some respect it becomes obscure, and when it becomes obscure it becomes weighty, He said: ﴿Heavy it has become﴾, that is, the Hour, so it sank to a point where the knowledge of the servants does not penetrate to it, and so its great matter worried them all. For this reason He expressed it with the adverbial form, saying: ﴿in the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, the relation of their inhabitants to its obscurity and to fear of it is on an equal footing, because its Owner is capable of whatever He wills, and He may do whatever He wills. Then He established its concealment from all, saying: ﴿It will not come upon you﴾, that is, in any state of affairs, ﴿except suddenly﴾, that is, at a moment of heedlessness.

Since they had persisted in pressing him, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, about it, and since the attribute of lordship mentioned in the first sentence might have been taken as a reason for asking him, in hope of learning of it from the One who had bestowed favour upon him, He cut off those hopes by his words, emphasising the meaning: ﴿They ask you﴾, that is, about the Hour absolutely, regarding the time of its occurrence, what will happen in its matters, and what severities will arise in it. That is, they press you with questions whenever you inform them that none knows it except Allah. (p-187) ﴿As if you were versed in it﴾, that is, knowing its matter, thoroughly investigating and insistent in asking ﴿about it. Say﴾, that is, to cut off their questioning, ﴿Its knowledge is only with Allah﴾, that is, the One who possesses all might, greatness and majesty, so nothing of what is with Him can be known except by His permission, and He has not permitted anyone of creation to know it. ﴿But most people﴾, that is, those in whom the attribute of disquiet has prevailed, ﴿do not know﴾, that is, they are not among the people of knowledge, so by asking about it they mock. Had they been among its people, they would not have denied you. Thus they fell into what does not concern them in asking about it and other kinds of obstinate contention, and they abandoned what would save and enrich them, namely hastening to faith in this Qur'an, out of fear that their terms would be cut short while they wander in the valleys of error.

When the knowledge of the unseen was necessarily linked to bringing about benefit and warding off harm, and the Hour was the most subtle branch of the knowledge of the unseen, He commanded him to negate this necessary attribute, so the more general is negated, and with its negation the more specific is negated as well. He put benefit first because it is more important to the soul, and nothing in the context requires delaying it, unlike the case in Surah Yunus, peace be upon him. So He said, commanding him to display the humility of servanthood: ﴿Say: I do not possess﴾, that is, at any time whatsoever at all, ﴿for myself any benefit﴾, that is, any bringing about of benefit, whether little or much, ﴿nor any harm﴾, likewise, for my power is limited and my knowledge is small, and everyone who is a servant is like this.

Since it is known, indeed observed, that every living creature can harm and benefit, He informed them that this is only by God. So He said: ﴿except what God wills﴾, that is, He to whom the whole command belongs, and no one besides Him has any command, that He should empower me to do it.

Since He had shown them by this that their asking him about the Hour and other unseen matters was ignorance on their part, because his condition is clear: he knows of these things only what God has taught him, the One who is singled out with the knowledge of the unseen, He indicated this by His saying: ﴿And if I had known﴾, that is, of myself, ﴿the unseen﴾, that is, its kind, ﴿I would have acquired abundantly﴾, that is, I would have brought about for myself much ﴿of good﴾, by seeking out benefits and establishing their causes.

Since harm cannot be tolerated from him in any way, He said: ﴿And evil would not have touched me﴾, that is, this kind of evil, by setting up barriers against it from me, because the necessary consequence of comprehensive knowledge is the comprehensiveness of power, as will be established, God willing, in Surah Ta-Ha. And since He had shown that knowledge of the unseen is the rank of God, He concluded the verse by explaining His rank. He said, reversing what they had claimed of him in terms of madness, in view of what became clear from his saying: "O Banu 'Abd Manaf! Be mindful of God! O Banu so-and-so, O Banu so-and-so!" And likewise what followed from their demand that he know the Hour, namely that he would then be a god: ﴿I am but﴾. Since the surah is for warning, He placed it first and said: ﴿a warner﴾, that is, absolutely, to the disbeliever so that he may turn back from his disbelief, and to the believer so that he may remain firm in his faith, ﴿and a bearer of good tidings for a people who believe﴾, that is, specifically. Or the two attributes are for them specifically, in view of benefit, whereas for what has no benefit in it, there is nothing.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 189:

When He, glory be to Him, mentioned the Hour here, as He had mentioned it at the beginning of the surah, He mentioned it with something He did not mention there of their mockery and derision. He concluded here by restricting knowledge and power to God, which necessitates His singularity in divinity. What had led them to that mockery was their associating partners with Him. So He mentioned, on the basis of restriction, what He had mentioned before it at the beginning of the surah, namely the beginning of creation, which necessitates the completeness of power, which in turn necessitates the negation of partners, and belief in His power over the Hour and other things, and truthfulness in all that has been reported about it and other matters, which necessitates steadfastness in accepting His good tidings and warnings and turning wholeheartedly to the Creator. So He said, affirming tawhid and emphasizing His command: ﴿He﴾, that is, alone, ﴿Who created you﴾, that is, when you were not anything, ﴿from a single soul﴾, that is, He created it initially from earth, and it is Adam, peace be upon him, as has already been explained. Whoever is able to bring a living being into existence from a thing that has no origin in life, is even more able to restore it to life from that same thing after it has come to have an origin in life.

Since Adam, peace be upon him, after becoming flesh and blood, was closer to being the cause for creating a being of flesh and blood from him, He said [expressing it with the particle waw (and), because it suffices for negating the association which the context is warning against; this differs from the Zumar, where it is with fa', because that is for compulsion; and the delay of the effects after their causes for a period is more indicative of it, because it contradicts the original]: ﴿And made﴾, because making (ja'l), as al-Harrali said, is the manifestation of a matter from a cause and its transformation, ﴿from it﴾, that is, not from anything else, ﴿its mate﴾, that is, Eve, from its flesh, its blood and its bone.

Since the intended meaning of "soul" is Adam, peace be upon him, and "mate" (zawj) is used for both the male and the female, He used a pronoun for the masculine, mentioning the reason for the making with His saying: ﴿so that he might find rest﴾, that is, Adam is intended by "soul" here. Since the mate here is the woman, He made the pronoun feminine and said: ﴿in her﴾ [and your movement from that rest, from him, to her], because the soul inclines more toward its kind and turns to it more, especially if it is a part of it. Do you not see the love of a parent for his child and of a relative for his relative? God, glory be to Him, prevented marriage between ascendants and descendants only because of the harm in that and other great wisdoms. So he covers her when he has found rest in her, and conception and birth occur, and souls branch out from that one soul.

Since [the rest here is a metaphor for intercourse, He repeated it with a word closer to it], He said, indicating the nearness of his covering her after her creation, [or] coordinating it with a supposed sentence: so he found rest in her, and his soul inclined to her, and he could not restrain himself from covering her: ﴿So when he covered her﴾, that is, Adam, peace be upon him, who is expressed by "soul", covered her with great desire, ﴿she bore a light burden﴾, that is, because it was a drop of semen, ﴿and she carried it about﴾, that is, she went about her affairs, she stood and sat, and it did not hinder her from any of that, to inform that her condition in it was according to the custom of women that we know, ﴿then when she became heavy﴾, that is, she became burdened by its size and its movement in her womb, ﴿they both called upon God﴾, that is, Adam and Eve, peace be upon them.

When He mentioned the Greatest Name, to bring to mind that the One called upon is the one who possesses all perfection, and so He is capable of what they asked for, since He is capable of all that He wills, He mentioned the attribute of benevolence, hoping for acceptance and favor, and said: ﴿their Lord﴾, that is, the One Who did good to them, (p-191) swearing: ﴿If You give us a righteous one﴾, that is, a child without defect, ﴿we will surely be among the thankful﴾, that is, we and our children, for Your blessing upon us. They allowed that it might not be sound, because of God's power over all that He wills, since He is the Chooser who acts, not nature or anything else. He indicated with the fa' the nearness of the birth to the supplication, and so He said:

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 190:**

﴿When He gave them﴾, i.e., your two parents, Adam and Eve, ﴿a righteous [child]﴾, i.e., the kind of righteous offspring that is complete in creation, in body, strength and intellect. So they multiplied on the earth and spread throughout its regions, male and female. ﴿They made﴾, i.e., the two kinds of their offspring, the males and the females, ﴿for Him partners﴾, i.e., some of them made idols, some made fire, some made the sun, and some made other things. This is according to the reading of the majority (qira'at al-jama'a). According to the reading of Nafi' and Abu Bakr from 'Asim, with a kasra on the shin, a sukun on the ra', and tanwin (shirkan), the meaning is: possessors of partnership ﴿in what He gave them﴾, i.e., of the powers [given] for worship, and of provision [devoted] through vows and the like.

Since the polytheists harmed none but themselves by their association, He based on this His statement: ﴿Exalted is Allah﴾, i.e., by what He has of the attributes of perfection that belong to no one else, ﴿high exaltation﴾. The evidence that both kinds are intended is His statement ﴿above what they associate﴾ in the plural, (p-١٩٢) and likewise what follows it concerning the blameworthiness of worshipping idols.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 191:

When He mentioned His exaltedness, glory be to Him, he began to mention, through expression and allusion, of His attributes what indicates this, and to establish the proofs that what they associated with Him is not fit to be a partner, by its incapacity, since it is among the number of His creation and has no action by which it deserves any aspect of glorification. So he said, rebuking its worshippers and indicating that the intended meaning is true association (shirk haqiqi), not what was mentioned about the story of Iblis in his causing the naming "Abd al-Harith" and the like: ﴿Do they associate﴾, i.e., the polytheists and their offspring, in worship, ﴿that which creates nothing﴾, i.e., of idols, natures, stars and others, ﴿anything﴾, i.e., brings it into existence from non-existence, as God does, the One with whom they associated them.

Since it would follow that what creates nothing is itself created, because it does not come into being incapable without a capable one who brought it into existence, he stated this explicitly in His saying, treating the idols as though they were those endowed with knowledge, since they have been given the same status as them in belief and worship: ﴿while they are created﴾. Since what is made cannot be a maker, he was content with the passive form and said: ﴿they are created﴾, i.e., their accidents, their essences and their like are being created continuously.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 192:

﴿And they are not able to help them﴾, meaning: to the polytheists who worship them, ﴿any help﴾, which is assistance against an enemy. Perhaps he expressed it with the form used for rational beings to indicate that if they were rational, and if they had these base qualities, they would not have qualified them to be their beloved ones, let alone to take them as their lords.

Since one who does not help others may still help himself, he negated that with His saying: ﴿nor can they help themselves﴾, meaning: at any time, when harm befalls them. Rather, their worshippers defend them.

(p-193)

When it became clear from this interrogative of denunciation, which expresses wonder at their condition in their misguidance, and which is phrased in the third person (*al-ghaybah*, third-person address), that the one they associated with God has no capacity whatsoever for what they have attributed to him, since the worshipped must be capable, and whoever is incapable in any way is a created being under the authority of another, and since direct address (*al-khitab*) has a power of alerting that third-person address lacks, he followed this with another expression of wonder at them, one more severe than the first. This is because their idols, to which they ascribed partnership, do not act of their own accord, and they neither respond when someone calls upon them nor are they guided to anything. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And if you call them﴾, meaning: and if you, O polytheists, call upon your idols with a continuous and repeated calling, ﴿to guidance﴾, meaning: to that which the caller definitely indicates, which shows that whoever fails to respond to it has a corrupted disposition and needs treatment, because he has failed to do what whoever has some measure of goodness never fails to do, since it is the noblest of things; so whoever fails to respond is content with his own baseness. ﴿They will not follow you﴾, meaning: in that guidance to which you have called them, even if you exert yourselves greatly in seeking their following. Perhaps He expressed it with the form *ifti'al* (the reflexive verbal pattern *yattabi'uukum*) to indicate that they cannot conceivably intend to follow, let alone bring about such following. Then He explained that this is not an incidental matter, but rather something constant and perpetual, by His saying, resuming the speech as an emphasis of the meaning: ﴿It is all the same for you﴾.

(p-194) Since equality (*al-sawa'*) can only exist between two matters, the hearer's attention was drawn to them, so He said: ﴿whether you call them﴾, meaning: that calling which was indicated as continuing has taken place from you, and He expressed it with a nominal sentence (*al-ismiyyah*) to indicate that they do not call upon them at times of hardship, but rather call upon God, so He said: ﴿or whether you remain silent﴾, meaning: silent concerning that on a lasting basis, in keeping with your habit of turning away from calling upon them in times of distress. Those who call upon what they believe in during times of necessity are in a worse state in this respect than the polytheists. [It is possible that this verse is an instance of *al-ihtibak* (a rhetorical device in which parallel elements are mutually omitted), so its arrangement would be: "Did you call upon them once, or are you continually calling upon them, or did you fall silent from calling upon them at some time, or are you constantly silent from calling upon them?" Each of these answers is governed by equality in the non-granting of response, with no difference whatsoever in it. By the verb first, it indicates the omission of its like second, and by the noun second, it indicates the omission of its like first.]

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 194:

When following someone who claims to be the most intelligent of people, the furthest from deficiencies, the most rooted in noble character and the highest above its base forms is the most shameful disgrace and the ugliest stigma for one whose path this is, and when they, despite knowing what this (Lord) is described with, did in associating partners with Him and in their fear and hope toward their objects of worship what is pure ignorance, (al-Biqa'i) repeated their rebuke for following them in another style, clearer than what came before, in clarifying the deficiencies and alerting to the faults, compelling them to acknowledge or openly declare obstinacy or madness. So he said, emphatically: ﴿Indeed, those you invoke﴾, meaning: O polytheists, an invocation (p-195) of worship, constantly bound to it. Or he applied "invocation" to worship, indicating that the worship of one who lacks the capacity to be called upon is not valid. The summary is that invocation is inseparable from the one invoked.

Since their invocation of them is only in the manner of association, he said, indicating the lowness of their rank by affirming the preposition: ﴿besides Allah﴾, meaning the One who possesses the attributes of perfection, greatness and majesty, ﴿are servants like you﴾, meaning: in being incapable of everything, especially that for which the challenge was issued, namely producing an equal to the Qur'an and other things, while you exceed them in life and reason. And the object of worship cannot be like the worshipper, so how much less when it is beneath him. Since they did not concede that they are like them, he drew from this the command to invoke them, to demonstrate the claim of equality, or rather inferiority, and he said: ﴿So call upon them﴾, meaning: for something among things.

Since the true God answers His friend at the challenge without fail, he indicated this by linking with the particle "fa" and said: ﴿then let them respond to you﴾, meaning: let them bring about a clear response to you in producing a sūrah resembling something of the Qur'an and in some of its benefits.

Since the situation required further rebuke and goading, he presented what I have seen of it, then increased the goading, saying: ﴿if you are﴾, meaning: by nature and disposition ﴿truthful﴾, meaning: in the claim that they are gods, for the rank of divinity requires this. Sa'id ibn Jubayr recited "in" (إنْ) with a light pronunciation and "ʿibādan amthālakum" with the دال and لام in the accusative. (p-196) The exegetes agreed on its interpretation that "in" is the negating particle, functioning like the Hijazi "mā", raising the subject and putting the predicate in the accusative. Its functioning in this way is disputed: al-Kisā'ī and most of the Kufans permitted it, and among the Basrans Ibn al-Sarrāj, al-Fārisī and Ibn Jinnī; al-Farrā' and most Basrans prohibited it, and the reports from Sibawayh and al-Mubarrad differ. The correct view is that its functioning this way is a dialect attested in poetry and prose. Abū Ḥayyān mentioned all of this and said that he expounded on it most fully in his commentary on al-Tashīl. This interpretation has been objected to on the ground that it entails its conflict with the well-known recitation; but that objection would hold only if negation and affirmation fell upon one and the same thing, and this is not the case here: the affirmation is for their similarity to them in general incapacity, and the negation is for their equality with them in it, since they exceed them in seizing and the like. Or the matter is, as al-Zamakhsharī said, that the affirmation is by way of supposition and the negation is in reality.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 195:

When he had established their incapacity and that they are like them, he indicated this, and that they are inferior to them, by way of denunciation and wonder, detailing some of what he had negated [from them]. So he said, placing the feet first because the first thing feared from a thing is its moving: ﴿Have they feet with which they walk?﴾ And since they have fashioned limbs, he made clear the meaning of his saying: ﴿with which they walk﴾.

And since what is feared after movement is the extending of the hand, he said: ﴿Or have they hands with which they strike?﴾ That is, described as being such that they ﴿strike with them﴾, that is, a kind of striking. And since what is feared after striking with the hand is sight, because of the indication [of the threat], [he said]: ﴿Or have they eyes with which they see?﴾ (p-197) That is, described as being such that they ﴿see with them﴾, that is, a kind of seeing. And since a person may fear what intends his harm, so that it is hidden from him and he then reaches it only by hearing, he said, concluding: ﴿Or have they ears with which they hear?﴾ That is, it is said of them that they ﴿hear with them﴾, that is, some kind of hearing.

When he had made them equal to these [idols] and negated from them what has been mentioned, it followed that these [idols] are deficient compared with them, and that in reality the [faculties] are stripped from them, because they have nothing of their own essences but nonexistence; and the power in what they are able to do belongs only to the Maker, who gave them a share in it. He said, showing this and resuming: ﴿Say﴾, that is, to these polytheists: ﴿Call upon your partners﴾, that is, these that have been mentioned, and whatever else you wish besides them, and seek their help in your enmity toward me.

Since this is a great challenge which entitles the one who makes it to boast of it, he drew attention to it with the particle of delay, and said: ﴿Then plot against me﴾, that is, all of you together, you and they, and you are more numerous than the pebbles of the valley and the sand of the wide plain, and I am alone. Since the meaning is "and hasten," he joined with the causal fa' his saying: ﴿and give me no respite﴾, that is, do not grant me a moment or more, lest you find an excuse for delay with some pretext. He gave as the reason for his not caring about their plotting, with his saying, indicating that his God possesses what he negated from their partners, namely comprehensive knowledge of the benefits of both abodes in what concerns religions and bodies, and he put religion first to show that it is the more important; so he said, emphasizing in response to their denial:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 196:

﴿Indeed, my Protector﴾ i.e., my helper and the one who takes charge of all my affairs, ﴿is Allah﴾ i.e., the one who combines all the attributes of perfection, ﴿who has sent down﴾ i.e., in stages, ﴿the Book﴾ i.e., comprehensive of the sciences of the earlier and later peoples, the matters of livelihood and the Hereafter, the conditions of the two abodes, and everything in it that is good, including the states of the hearts and other things, ﴿which you, all of you together, and those whom you claim as His partners, have been unable to match in any part of it.﴾

Since this revelation has taken on responsibility for all the attributes, namely perfect life, which necessitates will, power, knowledge, hearing, sight, and speech, and since their inability to match the Book was a verbal, witnessed proof against their lying, He followed this with another witnessed proof, one of action, saying: ﴿And He﴾ i.e., He alone ﴿protects﴾ i.e., takes on complete guardianship of ﴿the righteous﴾ i.e., all of them, by granting them victory over every enemy and sufficing them in every important matter. You have known what He set forth in this surah of His events, concerning those who denied His prophets and mocked His messengers, and that He saved everyone who was loyal to Him and destroyed all who opposed Him, such as those whom they took as gods. This verse, along with what comes before and after it, turns toward His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Follow what has been sent down to you from your Lord, and do not follow other than Him as protectors﴾ [al-A'raf: 3], as an explanation. It indicates that He is the one who did what was mentioned before for the sake of His allies, as evidenced by the fact that He rendered them unable to match any part of His Book, and unable to reach everything they wanted against His allies and beloved ones.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 197:

When he portrayed His majesty through this, and established His greatness and perfection by His being described with all the lofty attributes, among which is the power that restrains them from Him, he repeated the warning against their equals (andad) in another style, as an emphasis on the previous meaning with an extremely powerful addition regarding their incapacity, namely the directing of the gaze without seeing (taswib al-nazar min ghayr ibsar). Although the first was for rebuke, this distinction between one who is worshipped in truth and one who is worshipped in falsehood is so that they might turn back from their error and obstinacy. So he said, clarifying that they possess none of His attributes, explicitly negating the help which He attributed to Himself against them, together with direct address, which is more severe in the answer: ﴿Indeed, those you invoke⦅ besides Him⦆ cannot help you﴾, meaning: you persist in calling upon them – for they call upon Him, glorified is He, at some times – or you call upon them while abandoning Him ﴿cannot help you﴾, meaning: in any aspect of help, as evidenced by your inability against me while I am alone and you are the people of the earth ﴿nor can they help themselves﴾, as evidenced by the fact that a dog urinates upon them and they cannot prevent it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 198:

Since calling a group is closer to being heard than calling one individual, he (God) joined to what came before His saying ﴿And if you call them﴾, meaning: O you who are more misguided and more powerless than they are, ﴿to guidance﴾, meaning to that which is the most noble of qualities, so that they might be guided in defending themselves or otherwise, ﴿they do not hear﴾, meaning nothing of that call or of anything else. And since their state of sight, in relation to every person, is equally the same, He said, addressing a single listener: ﴿And you see them﴾, meaning, O you who look at them, ﴿looking at you﴾, meaning as if they look toward what they have made for themselves of eyes, ﴿but they do not see﴾, meaning not any kind of seeing. The content of these verses resembles what is in the Book of the Prophets of the Children of Israel, in the prophecy of Isaiah: Thus says the LORD, the King of Israel and his Redeemer: I am the first and I am the last, and there is no god besides Me. And who is like Me? Let him declare and show it, and recount it in order to Me, from the time I established the ancient nations. Let them show the things that are coming and shall come. Do not be afraid, nor be dismayed; have I not told you from of old and declared it? And you are My witnesses. Is there a god besides Me? There is no other Rock; I know not any. (p-200) Since the beginning of the world I have declared the things that were to come. Those who make idols are all nothing, and their precious things do not profit; and their own witnesses do not see or know, so that they may be put to shame. Who has formed a god or cast an idol that profits nothing? Behold, all his fellows shall be put to shame, and the craftsmen are mere men. Let them all assemble and stand up; they shall be terrified; they shall be put to shame together. The ironsmith with the tongs works at the coals and fashions it with hammers, and works it with the strength of his arm; he becomes hungry and his strength fails; he drinks no water and is faint. The carpenter stretches a line, marks it out with a pencil, shapes it with planes, and marks it with the compass, and makes it into the form of a man, the beauty of a man, to dwell in a house. He cuts down cedars for himself, and takes a cypress or an oak and strengthens it for himself among the trees of the forest. He plants a fir, and the rain makes it grow. Then it becomes fuel for a man. He takes some of it and warms himself; he kindles a fire and bakes bread. Then he makes a god and worships it; he makes it an idol and falls down before it. Half of it he burns in the fire; over the half he eats flesh; he roasts meat and eats it and is satisfied. He also warms himself and says, "Aha, I am warm; I see the fire." And the rest of it he makes into a god, his idol; he falls down before it and worships it and prays to it and says, "Deliver me, for you are my god!"

They have not considered, nor do they have knowledge or understanding, to say, "Half of it I have burned in the fire; over its coals I have baked bread, roasted meat and eaten it. And shall I make the rest of it an abomination? Shall I fall down before a block of wood?" He feeds on ashes; a deluded heart has turned him aside, so that he cannot deliver his soul, nor say, "Is there not a lie in my right hand?" (p-201) Then He said: Is not My hand the one that is upon the Lord from the beginning, and there is no god besides Me, and no savior but Me? Turn to Me and be saved, all you ends of the earth, for I am God, and there is no other. I have sworn by Myself; from My mouth has gone forth in righteousness a word that shall not return: to Me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear. They will say of Me, "Surely in the LORD are righteousness and strength." To Him shall come, and all who are incensed against Him shall be ashamed. In the LORD all the offspring of Israel shall be justified and shall glory. To whom then will you liken Me, and to whom will you compare Me, that we may be alike? Those who lavish gold from the purse and weigh silver on the scales, hire a goldsmith, and he makes it into a god; then they fall down and worship it. They lift it upon the shoulder, carry it, and set it in its place, and it stands there; it cannot move from its place. If one cries to it, it does not answer or save him from his trouble. Remember this and show yourselves men; recall it to mind, you transgressors. Remember the former things of old, for I am God, and there is no other; I am God, and there is none like Me. I declare the end from the beginning, and from ancient times things not yet done, saying, "My counsel shall stand, and I will accomplish all My purpose." I call a bird of prey from the east, the man of My counsel from a far country. Truly I have spoken; I will also bring it to pass; I have purposed; I will also do it. I have created, and I will also carry it out.

And in the Psalms, in Psalm one hundred and thirteen: Our God is in heaven; He does whatever He pleases. The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the work of human hands. They have mouths, but do not speak; eyes, but do not see; they have ears, but do not hear; noses, but do not smell; they have hands, but do not feel; feet, but do not walk; nor do they make a sound in their throats. (p-202) Those who make them will be like them, and so will all who trust in them. End.

When their overall state was rejection of what came to them and turning toward what had not come to them, with demands and obstinate questioning, such as asking about the Hour, and commanding what is objectionable, which is polytheism and the ugly character traits that follow from it, and forbidding what is good, which is monotheism and the fine teachings of the Sharia that follow from it, and this is ignorance, He concluded this by informing that He had set right their religion through the Book and their worldly affairs through protection from every affliction, and their condition may have been a cause for despair of their success and a reason for slackening in calling them to their own betterment, the caller to them (ﷺ) was as if he had said: "What shall I do about their affair?" So He answered him by warning against the likes of their condition, commanding the opposite of their speech and deeds, and fully exercising gentleness toward them, and said: ﴿Take what is easy﴾, that is, what comes to you from Allah and from people without effort and hardship. This root (al-'afw, "what is easy/surplus") revolves around ease, and sometimes comes from abundance and sometimes from scarcity. So "'afa al-mal" means the wealth increased, so that it became easy to spend and one gives it generously because of its excess beyond need, and "'afa al-manzil" means it was effaced, so its matter became easy until it was no longer looked at.

(p-203) When He commanded him with this regarding himself, He commanded him with it regarding others, saying: ﴿And enjoin what is known as good﴾, that is, everything the Sharia recognized and permitted, for it is part of pardon in ease and nobility. This includes the forbidding of what is objectionable, so He dispensed with mentioning it, because the context is about leniency. When He commanded him with the action in himself and in others, He followed it with abstention, saying: ﴿And turn away from the ignorant﴾, that is, do not repay them in their lightness and foolishness, and do not dispute with them, for that is easier than other than it. This is after their disgrace through the call [and that is] because the center of their condition is following desire, so it leads them to the effort of opposing these qualities. In it there is an indication of the prohibition against letting himself go in grief over them out of excessive compassion for them. And from Ja'far al-Sadiq that there is no verse in the Qur'an more comprehensive of noble character than this one.

When Satan, out of his enmity toward the children of Adam, was striving to repel them from these excellent qualities and to encourage them toward their opposites, and when the Prophet (ﷺ) had been relieved of Satan's share (ḥaẓẓ al-shayṭān) by the removal of that black clot from his heart, when Jibril (peace be upon him) split open his chest, washed his heart, and said, "This is Satan's share from you," God prescribed for his community what would protect them from Satan when he prods them, addressing the Prophet with this so that it would be more persuasive to them and more fitting to intensify the fear that calls for flight, which in turn yields salvation. For when they know Satan's aim toward one from whom his share has been removed and who has been protected from every trial, they will know that his aim toward them is even stronger, his scheming greater, and his obstruction more severe. So He said, emphasizing with various kinds of emphasis, to indicate the intensity of Satan's aim at seduction and his excess in it, so that the believers would take great precaution against him, even though his aim in this case is in the position of disavowal, since he knows the Prophet is protected. For this reason He expressed it with the particle of doubt (in ﴿إن﴾ ... "if"), indicating the weakness of Satan's scheming against the Prophet (ﷺ), because God Most High had helped him against his companion (the devil assigned to him), and so he submitted.

﴿وإمّا﴾: that is, "if" (in); it is reinforced by "mā" (in وإمّا being "wa-in" plus "mā"), affirming the meaning and negating its opposite. ﴿يَنْـزَغَنَّكَ﴾: that is, he will prod you with a great prodding. ﴿مِنَ الشَّيْطانِ نَـزْغٌ﴾: that is, a prodding by his whispering, which is of a nature that agitates and drives one to act contrary to the excellent qualities mentioned before, such as anger at the ignorance of the ignorant and the folly of the fool, or excess in some aspect, just as a beast is driven by what prods it. Thus the verbal noun (nazgh) is interpreted and made to act as the one who prods, to indicate its intensity. ﴿فاسْتَعِذْ﴾: that is, seek refuge or ask for protection, which is seeking shelter (al-ʿawdh, meaning taking refuge) ﴿بِاللَّهِ﴾: that is, in God, to whom belong all might, greatness, power and dominion, since you are cut off from brothers and helpers toward Him; there is no protector for you and no helper except Him. For when He wills to protect you, He reminds you of the mighty favors and severe retributions that will turn you away from corruption, out of desire and fear. The verse refers back to His saying Most High [its first part]: ﴿Surely I will sit in wait for them on Your straight path﴾ [al-A'raf: 16].

When God Most High negated that their partners had any hearing or knowledge, the affirmation of that for Him became sufficient to establish His exclusive possession of it, without any need for an exclusive restriction (ḥaṣr) that would imply its negation from others, because it had been stated explicitly earlier, unlike what occurs in Fussilat. So He said, giving a reason: ﴿Indeed He is All-Hearing﴾: that is, of far-reaching hearing; He hears your seeking refuge and will answer you if He wills. ﴿All-Knowing﴾: of comprehensive knowledge of what you seek and what your enemy seeks from you, so nothing overpowers Him. He concluded with the attribute of knowledge in both places, because whispering belongs to the category of what is known. In Surah al-Mu'min He concluded with "All-Seeing" (al-baṣīr), derived from sight (baṣar) and insight (baṣīrah), because what is sought refuge from is a matter of human beings, and among it is what can be seen.

Since the Prophet ﷺ experiences only a very slight stirring, as indicated by the word nazgh (prompting), and it is not something certain, as indicated by the particle of doubt, and since only the God-fearing (al-muttaqun) seek refuge in God, it is as if it were said: do that at the first stirring of it, so that you may be among the God-fearing. He justified this with His words: ﴿Indeed, those who have feared God﴾, meaning: this quality has come about for them, and He confirmed its harm to them with the particle of certainty, unlike what passed when the address was singular to the Prophet ﷺ. So He said: ﴿when an evil whisper (ṭā'if) from Satan touches them﴾, meaning a circling (ṭawāf), taking it as a verbal noun. It may also be a lightened form of ṭayf, like mayyit (for mayyit, "dead"), and has the same meaning as the reading ṭā'if taken as an active participle, like mayyit and mā'it. It may also be a verbal noun. This indicates that Satan is circling around them and does not leave them. At times his circling affects them, so he has touched them with a touch greater than the prompting, because he has encircled them from all sides; and at times it does not affect them. ﴿From Satan﴾, meaning the one far from mercy, burned by the curse, ﴿they remember﴾, meaning they compel themselves to remember God with everything that benefits them in that matter, by advancing and by holding back.

Since they, through the swiftness of their remembrance, are as if no part of his affair had touched them, He indicated this with the nominal sentence, emphasizing the swiftness of sight with the sudden particle "idhā": ﴿then behold, they are seeing clearly﴾, meaning, by the light of their inner consciences, ﴿seeing﴾, meaning their sight is firmly established, so they do not follow Satan, for the God-fearing person is one who desires and then refrains, and sees and then restrains. In this there is a warning that whoever persists with Satan becomes blind, because he is a wrongdoer (ẓālim), and the wrongdoer is one who is as if he were in darkness.

[Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah al-A'raf, verse 202]

When the God-fearing (al-muttaqun), who are the scholars (al-'ulama'), were described, alluding to their counsel to those they are responsible for, and it was known of their condition that they are enemies of Satan, and it was known that their opposites are his allies, he followed it with the description of the ignorant (al-jahilun) and the deceit of their allies towards them, while all of them are not God-fearing. So He said: ﴿And their brothers﴾, meaning: and the brothers of the ignorant from the devils of mankind and the jinn, ﴿extend them﴾, meaning: they extend the ignorant, from al-madd, which is respite and prolongation according to the reading of the majority (al-jama'a), and it has the meaning of the reading of the people of Madina with the damma, from al-imdad [supplying]. [Al-Wahidi said: this is most often used in what is praised, like "We supplied them with fruit" (amdadnahum bi-fakiha), so it is from the usage of a thing in its opposite, like: ﴿So give them good tidings of a painful punishment﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 24]. It seems he is indicating that Satan most often comes to man in the form of a sincere, compassionate counselor. The more apparent view is that "their brothers" refers to the ignorant because they are in contrast to: ﴿those who are God-fearing﴾ [al-A'raf: 201], and the pronoun refers to Satan, meant as a kind, i.e. and the brothers of the devils, who are the ignorant who do not fear God, are extended by their allies among the devils.] ﴿in error (al-ghayy)﴾, which is the opposite of guidance (al-rushd). [He indicated] the greater care they take in misleading and their persistence in misguidance and enticement with the particle of delay, so He said: ﴿then they do not cease﴾, meaning: they do not stop misleading them, not even for a moment, due to their ignorance and their evil.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 203:

When it had been established what He prescribed of chastity (ta'affuf) and of avoiding excess (tanaTTu') and affectation (takalluf), and He had informed that among their blindness is their affectation in asking about the Hour, while the devils never cease in their seducing of them, He informed him about the absolute affectation of theirs, marvelling at them and showing their persistence alongside the seduction of their devils. He commanded him, ﷺ, with what he should answer them with, and so He said, conjoining it to ﴿They aid them﴾ [al-A'raf: 202]: ﴿And when you do not bring them a sign﴾, that is: according to their proposal. ﴿They say, "Why do you not choose it?"﴾, that is: "Why not?" ﴿Choose it﴾. Al-jaby is gathering, al-ijbaa' is leaving it, and al-ijtiba' is the earnest gathering, and it entails selection and choosing. So the meaning of "you chose it" is "you sought it out", that is: you exerted yourself on your own accord to bring it chosen.

And since the situation called for a question in teaching the answer, He supported that with His saying: ﴿Say﴾, that is: when they say that, ﴿"I only follow﴾, that is: I deliberately and affectedly follow ﴿what is revealed to me﴾, that is: what the angel brings me ﴿from my Lord﴾, that is: the One who does good to me by teaching me what benefits me, not that I bring anything from my own self, nor do I propose to my Lord.

Since He confined his state to following revelation, it was as if it were said: "What is this that is revealed to you?" (p-208) So He said — and it is permissible that this be a justification for his following it, because it is sufficient in establishing his prophethood, independent of proposed signs, and compelling in the obligation to follow it —: ﴿This﴾, pointing to what is revealed to him, as an alert that it must be kept present in all minds, present between the eyes of every person, ﴿are insights﴾, that is: things which are — according to what you sought — chosen; rather, they are the choicest of the choice, through which the light of the heart comes into being, so that the eyes too gain a sight that brings them close to the visible signs which the Book urges to be looked at, to knowledge they did not have before. They are clear proofs, compelling for my affirmation and the acceptance of everything I have brought. He named it so because it is a cause of the sight of intellects toward the proofs of monotheism, prophethood, the return, and the whole Shari'ah in its roots and branches. So it is the naming of the cause by the name of the effect. And I praise them by His saying: ﴿from your Lord﴾, that is: the One who has never cut off His goodness from you at all, so He is worthy that what comes from Him be received with every beauty.

Since the insights are plural, and the custom is that the individual members of a plural vary, He emphasised them with what indicates that they are beyond habit, in that they are equal in the highest ranks of guidance. So He said: ﴿and guidance﴾, that is: clarification; and since clarification may not be in the form of honour, He said: ﴿and mercy﴾, that is: honour. (p-209) And since one who does not benefit from a thing may rightly deny the benefit of a beneficial thing in relation to himself, He said: ﴿for a people who believe﴾, that is: who actualise this reality and persist in renewing it at every time. As for others, it may be a punishment upon them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 204:

When Allah magnified the status of the Qur'an, the implied sense being: "So believe in it, and you will prosper," He joined to it His saying: ﴿And when the Qur'an is recited﴾, that is, this which is revealed to me, "then behave with courtesy and humility, for it is an attribute of your Lord," ﴿then listen to it﴾, that is, lend it your ears, striving to be free of anything that would distract you from listening.

Since some of the understanding ones would listen while speaking, He indicated that this Book is too exalted to be attained by one who occupies himself with it even with the slightest distraction, and so He said: ﴿and be silent﴾, that is, for reflection and contemplation, so that your hearts may be illuminated and you may know its reality, and thus act upon what is in it, and there will be no constriction in your breasts concerning it. Since the apparent meaning of the verse is the obligation of silence for every listener to every reciter, He encouraged it, magnifying its status, and so He said: ﴿so that you may be shown mercy﴾, that is, so that you may be hopeful that your Lord will honour you and do with you everything that the merciful does with the one he shows mercy to.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 7, verse 205:

When the command to remember (dhikr) at the moment of the whisperings of Satan (nazgh al-shaytan) had preceded, and the discourse had passed on until He commanded listening to the greatest remembrance, and the reciter may have exaggerated in raising his voice so that his hearers would be many, and perhaps he lowered it so as not to make others obliged to listen, He taught them the etiquette of recitation (adab al-qira'a) (p-210) and made it general in every state, because one who understands might restrict it to remembrance in the state of the whisperings. The address then rose from them to their Imam, so that it would be more inducing to their acceptance, together with an indication that no one else can perform this matter as it should be performed except him (ﷺ). So He said: ﴿And remember﴾, that is, with every kind of remembrance from the Qur'an and other than it, ﴿your Lord﴾, that is, the One who has reached the utmost in kindness toward you, ﴿within yourself﴾, that is, a remembrance that is firmly established in you, held within you by your understanding of its meanings and your adorning yourself with what is in it. Let it be secret, for that is closer to sincerity (ikhlas) and more helpful to reflection (tafakkur). And its being secret indicates the most noble of states, which is watchfulness (muraqaba) together with the realization of nearness. When this is so, His saying ﴿with humility﴾ bears fruit, that is, while you are humble outwardly, ﴿and with fear﴾, that is, so that fear calls you to humble yourself inwardly, so that you combine the humility of secrecy and openness. By this the humility of servanthood is perfected through the might of lordship.

When He commanded secrecy, He said, in contrast to it: ﴿And without loudness﴾, that is, because it is more inward in sincerity. It is known that it is above secrecy, otherwise the phrase would convey nothing. And since loudness may occur in actions, He emphasized it with His saying: ﴿in speech﴾, that is, for that indicates humility and submission without shouting, as kings are addressed privately and favours are sought from them. And as (ﷺ) said to the Companions when they raised their voices in supplication beyond the measure: "Indeed you do not call upon one who is deaf or absent."
