(p-211) For the aim is the attainment of verbal remembrance so that it aids the remembrance of the heart, and the aim is achieved by making oneself hear it; for the imagination is affected, and so the remembrance of the heart is strengthened, and the lights continue to increase, so that the reflection of some of them upon others is reflected, until the ascent increases from the darknesses of the world of bodies to the lights of the Governor of light and darkness.

When He commanded remembrance qualified by its fitting manner, He (ﷺ) commanded him to persist in it, remembering it at the best and most fitting times, because of what those times contain of preoccupation, which indicates more strongly his preference for greater love and exaltation. So He said: ﴿in the mornings﴾, that is, the times of early dawn. Perhaps He made it singular by making it the verbal noun of "ghada"; for there is nothing there except the dawn prayer, and He made what follows plural for the two afternoon prayers and the evening prayer, so He said: ﴿and the evenings﴾, that is, the times of the night prayer. It was said: al-ghuduww is the plural of ghadwa, so that what is meant then along with the dawn is the forenoon (duha). The end of every day is joined to the beginning of the night of the following day, so the end of the day is called asil, because it joins with what is the origin (asl) of the following day. He specified these two times, although what is meant is constancy, by naming each of day and night by the name of its part, so that by the mornings he would mention departure from death, and by the evenings tranquility in death and return to the state of non-existence, and thereby he would summon the majesty of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, so that this would contain His exaltation as is due.

Since this specification by these two times might have given the impression, although it is apparent in constancy, He stated explicitly: ﴿and do not be among the heedless﴾, that is, at other times than these two, but rather be mindful of Him at every time and in every state;

Then he gave the reason for the command as vigilance (*muraqabah*, awareness of being watched by God), which indicates the greatest humility, in that it is the duty of those brought near. So he said: ﴿Indeed, those who are﴾. He increased the encouragement to this by saying: ﴿with your Lord﴾, meaning the one who is good to you by bringing you close to His presence and making you the most honored of His beloved. They are the noble angels, possessed of infallibility and nearness, a nearness of rank and not of place, ﴿who do not disdain﴾, meaning they neither exhibit nor seek arrogance ﴿from His worship﴾, meaning from submitting to Him and engaging in every form of humbling oneself, along with their great nearness, their utmost purity, and their love. ﴿And they glorify Him﴾, meaning they declare Him free of everything unfitting, with their sincerity free from the motives of desires and personal interests.

Since this relates to knowledge of God (*ma'arif*), and he placed it first to show that the foundation of worship is the deeds of the heart, he followed it with his words: ﴿And to Him alone﴾, meaning exclusively, ﴿they prostrate﴾, meaning they humble themselves by affirming for Him every perfection and by directly performing the finest deeds. The verse includes information about the righteous angels in three reports: the absence of arrogance, which is the most exalted kind of worship, since it is what drives one to obedience just as its opposite drives one to disobedience; the glorification, which is declaring Him free of everything unfitting; and the specification of prostration to Him. Since worship arises from the absence of arrogance, and since it is of two kinds, inward and outward, he indicated the inward kind by glorification and the outward kind by prostration. This is the state in which the servant is near his Lord, like the angels, in closeness and nearness. [p. 213] "The closest a servant is to his Lord is when he is prostrating," which Abu Hayyan pointed out, indicating that both kinds of worship return to the heart, one of them indicated by speech and the other by action. The end of the surah has returned, in the command to follow the Qur'an, to its beginning in the best of returns. By describing the nearest ones with the absence of arrogance and constancy in the duties of humility, the surah turned, in the most apparent way, to describing Iblis with disobedience to God's command to prostrate to Adam, peace be upon him, out of arrogance. Rather, it began to return the closing section to the opening once it had completed the stories of the prophets. So His words: ﴿And We certainly created﴾ [al-A'raf: 179] correspond to His words: ﴿And the land that is bad, its produce comes forth only poorly﴾ [al-A'raf: 58]. This will become clear to you if you review what I have already presented regarding their meaning. ﴿And to God belong the most beautiful names, so call upon Him by them﴾ [al-A'raf: 180] corresponds to: ﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly﴾ [al-A'raf: 55]. And ﴿And among those We created is a community that guides by the truth﴾ [al-A'raf: 181] corresponds to: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds, We do not burden any soul except according to its capacity; those are the companions of Paradise﴾ [al-A'raf: 42]; ﴿And those who denied Our signs and were arrogant toward them﴾ [al-A'raf: 36]; ﴿And that it may be that their term has approached﴾ [al-A'raf: 185] corresponds to: ﴿And when their term comes, they cannot delay it﴾ [al-A'raf: 34]; and ﴿They ask you about the Hour﴾ [al-A'raf: 187] corresponds to: ﴿As He originated you, you will return﴾ [al-A'raf: 29]; ﴿And for you on earth is a dwelling place and provision for a time﴾ [al-A'raf: 24]; and ﴿It is He who created you from one soul﴾ [al-A'raf: 189]; ﴿And We have certainly created you and then fashioned you﴾ [al-A'raf: 11]; ﴿I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord﴾ [al-A'raf: 203], through to its end, after the warning against rivals. It corresponds to: ﴿A Book revealed to you, so let there be no distress in your breast concerning it﴾ [al-A'raf: 2], through to His words: ﴿And do not follow, besides Him, any protectors. Little do you remember﴾ [al-A'raf: 3]. Glory be to Him whose speech this is, exalted is His veil, mighty is His aim, and upon the one to whom it was revealed be His blessings, peace, greetings, and honor.
